jobs.title: Business Systems Product Manager
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Business Systems Product Manager is a senior individual contributor role within the Customer Excellence Group (CEG) responsible for owning and executing on a high-impact area of the Customer Success Platform (CSP). This role partners closely with Digital Technology (DT) counterparts to translate business priorities into precision-executed platform capabilities. The CSP is a major strategic bet for CEG, and this BPM is expected to operate at a level that reflects that.

CSP is the home for all 2,500+ CEG users and serves as the next-generation tooling that powers how CEG drives product adoption, NRR/GRR, and NPS for ServiceNow's customer base. Every workflow, automation, and AI capability shipped on CSP directly compounds the productivity and outcomes of the entire post-sales organization.

This is a deep product craft role for someone who thrives on personal ownership, end-to-end execution, and influence without authority. The right candidate is obsessed with AI, outcome measurement, and enabling the customer success organization to focus on high-value work by eliminating manual, repetitive tasks through intelligent automation. They set the technical and product bar within their domain and are looked to as a subject-matter expert by peers and senior leaders alike.

What You Will Do Product Ownership & Prioritization

• Own a major workstream within the CSP product roadmap end-to-end, from problem definition through delivery and adoption.
• Drive structured prioritization within your domain, balancing competing demands with a rigorous, data-informed lens and clearly articulated tradeoffs.
• Translate complex business pain points into crisply scoped business requirements with measurable outcomes.
• Author detailed BRDs that capture current-state processes and workflows, the future-state vision, and the transformation needed to get there, leaving no ambiguity for engineering or stakeholders.

Execution & Delivery

• Drive elite-level execution on your roadmap, ensuring features are delivered with precision, on time, and to specification.
• Partner with DT/CCX engineering counterparts on delivery cadence, surfacing blockers early and helping resolve them quickly.
• Maintain rigorous program hygiene on your initiatives: clear scope, milestones, risks, dependencies, and status at all times.
• Ensure every capability ships with a high-quality, intuitive user experience that CEG users adopt without friction.
• Build the UAT strategy for your domain: recruit UAT testers across CEG personas, write detailed test cases, and lead UAT execution end-to-end.
• Lead effective release communications to stakeholders, ensuring CEG users and leadership know what is shipping, when, and what it means for them.

AI Strategy & Integration

• Embed AI-first thinking into every capability you ship, identifying opportunities to automate manual workflows and free CS teams to focus on strategic, high-value activities.
• Develop a point of view on how emerging AI capabilities apply to your domain and advocate for AI investment in the roadmap.
• Stay ahead of the AI landscape as it applies to customer success operations, internal tooling, and workflow automation, and bring that perspective into design discussions.
• Prototype, evaluate, and partner with engineering on AI/agentic feature design.

Measurement & Outcomes

• Define and track adoption, usage, and business impact metrics for every feature you deliver.
• Operate with a default to data: decisions, tradeoffs, and post-launch reviews are grounded in measurable outcomes.
• Use clear ROI frameworks to justify your roadmap investments and demonstrate platform value to senior stakeholders.

Stakeholder Management & Communication

• Communicate roadmap, status, and outcomes for your domain clearly and confidently to senior executives, including VP and SVP-level audiences.
• Proactively surface risks, tradeoffs, and mitigation plans before they become escalations.
• Build strong, trusted relationships across CEG business stakeholders, DT, and cross-functional partners.
• Navigate complex organizational dynamics with strategic judgment and composure, leading through influence rather than authority.

Product Craft Leadership

• Set the bar for product craft within the CSP team: discovery quality, written artifacts, decision frameworks, and execution discipline.
• Identify systemic gaps in process, tooling, or architecture across the CSP and drive cross-team improvements.

Required

• 8+ years in Product Management, business systems, or enterprise technology, with demonstrated growth in scope and impact across roles.
• Proven track record owning and shipping product roadmaps for internal or customer-facing platforms in complex enterprise environments.
• Demonstrated ability to drive cross-functional execution in close partnership with engineering or DT teams.
• Track record of delivering results in high-pressure, high-stakes environments with competing priorities.
• Experience presenting strategy and program status to VP and C-level stakeholders with clarity and confidence.
• Exceptional organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail.
• Genuine passion for AI and experience applying or advocating for AI/automation in product strategy.
• Demonstrated ability to lead through influence without direct reports.

Preferred

• Experience in a post-sales, customer success, or CS operations environment.
• Familiarity with ServiceNow's platform capabilities, particularly as applied to internal tooling or CS workflows.
• Experience with customer success platforms, CRM, or internal enablement tools.
• Background in experience design or a strong aesthetic sensibility for product UI/UX.
• Hands-on experience prototyping, building, or shipping AI/agentic features.

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $126,800 - $221,900, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.

Work Personas

We approach our distributed world of work with flexibility and trust. Work personas (flexible, remote, or required in office) are categories that are assigned to ServiceNow employees depending on the nature of their work and their assigned work location. Learn more here. To determine eligibility for a work persona, ServiceNow may confirm the distance between your primary residence and the closest ServiceNow office using a third-party service.

Equal Opportunity Employer

ServiceNow is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, gender identity,  veteran status, or any other category protected by law. In addition, all qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with legal requirements.

Accommodations

We strive to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application process, or are unable to use this online application and need an alternative method to apply, please contact globaltalentss@servicenow.com for assistance.

Export Control Regulations

For positions requiring access to controlled technology subject to export control regulations, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), ServiceNow may be required to obtain export control approval from government authorities for certain individuals. All employment is contingent upon ServiceNow obtaining any export license or other approval that may be required by relevant export control authorities.

jobs.title: Customer Experience Coordinator - Indianapolis, IN (Nora)
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As a Customer Experience Coordinator, your job is to define the customer’s experience through service, focus, and participation—so, you are passionate about perfecting the experience before, during, and after their time at VEG. Outgoing and personable, with each customer, you conduct yourself professionally in both demeanor and presence. You find ways to say yes and put patient and customer experience above all else. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to grow where you want to go, building valuable experience and paving the way for your career to take unexpected and rewarding directions.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Greet every customer with warmth and urgency, whether in person, over the phone, or online

• Oversee all customer communications (calls, emails, texts), record details accurately, and route urgent medical calls to a doctor quickly

• Deliver personalized, memorable experiences—always looking for creative ways to say “yes” to customer needs

• Listen with empathy, resolve concerns quickly, and anticipate issues before they escalate

• Keep nursing team and doctors updated on customer needs for a seamless care experience.

• Provide confidential, compassionate guidance on financial options and end-of-life decisions

• Process payments accurately while protecting personal and financial information

• Follow up with customers after visits to check on their pet’s care and strengthen relationships

• Celebrate and capture special moments (with permission), creating lasting connections between customers, their pets, and the hospital

WHAT YOU NEED

• 2+ years of experience in a customer service role

• Advanced knowledge in computer programs and practice management software

• Highly organized, with strong attention to detail

• A strong communicator; able to interact positively with anyone and everyone

• A strong multitasker, able to thrive amid chaos

• High emotional intelligence, able to read a room and plan and act accordingly

• Adaptable and amenable in high stakes environments

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Competitive compensation, including base and 401K match

• Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including QPR training and access to free therapy or counseling

• Based on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success

• A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.

• Clinical student loan repayment so you don’t need to worry about your student debt

• Paid parental leave, up to 12 weeks at 100% of regular salary and inclusive fertility and family-building care for all types of families

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

• Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people

• And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

jobs.title: Solutions Architect - Pre Sales
jobs.description:
ABOUT HYPEREXPONENTIAL (HX)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Field Engineering (FENG) is the technical core of our go-to-market organisation. The team sits at the intersection of product, sales, and customer success, owning the “technical win” in each opportunity and making hx platform real for some of the most demanding insurers in the world. We work with underwriters, actuaries, IT, and security leaders to design solutions they can trust with their most critical pricing and underwriting decisions.

This is a team that thrives at the edge of what’s possible for our product and our customers. We specialise in the hardest integration and implementation challenges, where deep technical understanding, domain insight, and creativity are all required. As a Solutions Architect, you’ll be one of the first hx’ers many prospects meet, shaping how they understand our platform and what it can do for their business.

Solutions Architects at hx are the voice of IT, security and infrastructure - both inside hx and in front of customers. We figure out how hx Renew fits into complex, often ancient system landscapes, translating between modern cloud architectures and 1990s reality without losing sight of the bigger transformation.

The culture is high-ownership, collaborative, and very visible: every engagement is high stakes, every interaction leaves a lasting impression, and your work feeds directly into both revenue outcomes and product direction. You’ll partner closely with Sales and Product Engineering, acting as a trusted advisor throughout the sales cycle and beyond, and helping customers realise the full value of hx's core product suite.

Have a look at our Field Engineering Candidate Hub https://www.hyperexponential.com/careers/hubs/field-engineering, for a sneak peak behind the scenes into our culture. 




WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - Accelerating the Tech Win by translating prospect requirements and legacy constraints into clear, actionable integration approaches aligned to our onboarding and integration playbooks.

 - Run focused, high-impact technical discovery and design workshops with underwriters, actuaries, and IT stakeholders to deeply understand their workflows and shape viable solution architectures.

 - Act as the trusted technical voice throughout the sales cycle, guiding stakeholders through RFPs, RFIs, due diligence, and security reviews to remove friction and keep deals moving.

 - Design, build, and present compelling POV (Proof of Value) materials, Proofs of Concept and demos that showcase hx Renew’s integration capabilities and how we can transform customers’ pricing and underwriting processes.

 - Partner with Product Engineering as “Customer Zero”, testing new features in real-world scenarios, surfacing edge cases, and feeding back insights that improve product quality and relevance.

 - Create and maintain reusable assets – from integration libraries and reference architectures to demo environments and technical presentations – that scale the impact of the Field Engineering team across multiple deals and regions.




WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO HAVE DONE

 - Supported with technical solution design and integration for complex B2B or enterprise software opportunities, ideally in data-heavy domains such as insurance, financial services, or adjacent regulated industries.

 - AI-native in practice - Uses AI tools as a natural part of technical and delivery work - documentation, troubleshooting, first-pass analysis - not exploring what's possible but already doing it.

 - Run technical evaluations and POVs with multiple stakeholder groups (e.g. business, IT, security), successfully navigating RFP/RFI processes, due diligence, and technical Q&A to a clear “Tech Win”.

 - Designed, documented and positioned solution architectures within known patterns (e.g. APIs, event-driven integrations, identity and access management), clearly articulating assumptions, risks, and trade-offs.

 - Built and delivered tailored Proofs of Concept or Proof of Value that directly contributed to winning or expanding high-value accounts, ideally with measurable commercial impact.

 - Collaborated closely with Sales teams, using structured sales methodologies to align technical work with deal strategy, timing, and stakeholder influence.

 - Contributed to shared technical assets and standards – such as playbooks, reference diagrams, or demo environments – and used structured learning habits (enablement, shadowing, self-study) to quickly ramp up on new products or domains.




YOU’RE UNLIKELY TO THRIVE HERE IF

 - You prefer to follow a fixed, prescriptive playbook rather than dealing with ambiguity, evolving requirements, and messy legacy environments.

 - You’re uncomfortable being highly visible – with customers, internally with senior stakeholders, and in situations where the stakes (and expectations) are high.

 - You see yourself purely as either “sales” or “engineering” and don’t enjoy operating in the grey space between commercial outcomes, technical depth, and product thinking.

If reading our Culture Document https://hx.wiki/ leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.




BENEFITS

 - $6,000 training and conference budget

 - Full medical, dental, and vision package

 - Mental health support via Spring Health and Rula

 - Access to One Medical

 - Flexible vacation policy

 - Pet discount plans, retirement plan (401K), and discount programmes

Additional perks

 - Top-spec equipment

 - Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights

 - Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and WeWork office space

 - Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth




INTERVIEW PROCESS

 - Initial call with our Talent team to kick things off

 - Manager interview with our Director of Solutions Engineering

 - Skills Assessment Stage

 - Values Interview + Meet the CEO

 - We offer!




OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY

hxer's are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.




NEXT STEPS

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations. jobs.title: Sales Trainer
jobs.description:
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5ac97b31-49cd-4012-8bb0-5caf15e33c69/B25.png]





WE ARE LOOKING FOR A SALES TRAINER TO JOIN OUR SALES TEAM; AS WE SCALE UP AND DRIVE DIGITAL AND FINANCIAL INCLUSION ACROSS OUR MARKETS.



[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/2c6957b4-39d2-40b3-8eb6-7e380a0c2f9c/B13.png]



THE ROLE

As Sales Trainer, you equip our sales force in your region with the tools, skills and knowledge to sell new and existing products well. You will raise the productivity of new DSRs, make sure newly recruited DSRs convert, and support sales activity across the region. You sit in the Sales department and report to the Regional Sales Training Lead.



[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/5e9f3448-2fed-4b66-b1ee-9474279a7947/B13.png]




ABOUT US

M-KOPA is a pan-African fintech providing asset financing and credit to underserved customers. We have reached 10 million customers and extended $2B+ in credit. 86% of customers report a better quality of life, and 55% are accessing financial services for the first time. Our 2,300+ employees and 35,000+ field agents make it happen, and the Direct Sales Representatives (DSRs) you train are where every customer relationship begins.



[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/ba282a12-7335-4f14-b5d0-85744a5ad867/B7.png]



This is a hybrid role, you would be working from our offices in Ghana, partnering with a diverse group of employees from our different markets and locations across the UK, Europe and Africa. You will be reporting to the Head of Sales.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the conversion of every newly recruited DSR, measured by F7 (at least 1 sale within 7 days of registration), F30 (at least 8 sales within 30 days) and F60 (at least 8 sales in the next calendar month after F30).

 - Deliver regular in-class onboarding per territory each month, plus DSR career training and FSM/SE training as required. Teach proper onboarding and KYC fidelity so Quality of Sales reaches 95%.

 - Build the annual training calendar from needs surveys, assessments and feedback. Define clear outcomes with stakeholders, design training that can be applied the day after, and document your results.

 - Keep DSRs informed during outages such as system downtime, credits not updating or internet issues.

 - Reach at least 80% satisfaction and make sure every team is trained and ready to perform.




WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - At least a bachelor’s degree from a recognised university and at least 18 months as a Sales Trainer.

 - Strong command of Learning Management Systems, excellent presentation and MS PowerPoint skills, and solid business strategy, reporting, coaching and data analysis skills.

 - Self-motivation, a drive for results and a professional approach. You can train effectively in English and a local language, and Twi is an added advantage.





The honest part
This role is accountable. Your DSR conversion numbers are visible, the 95% Quality of Sales and 80% satisfaction targets are real, and outages will ask you to communicate clearly at short notice. If you want your training judged by what your people go on to sell, you’re probably ready for exactly this.




WHY M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.



Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com http://m-kopa.com.



[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/369018b8-cf9c-49c7-95f1-1d414482ba57/B13.png]

Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/1d985516-2a99-43c0-b591-957f5adaceb9/481f6724-8375-4f39-b514-fbe00b8fc3b5/B13.png]



Important Notice

M-KOPA is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer committed to assembling a diverse, broadly trained staff. Women, minorities, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.



M-KOPA explicitly prohibits the use of Forced or Child Labour and respects the rights of its employees to agree to terms and conditions of employment voluntarily, without coercion, and freely terminate their employment on appropriate notice. M-KOPA shall ensure that its Employees are of legal working age and shall comply with local laws for youth employment or student work, such as internships or apprenticeships. 



M-KOPA does not collect/charge any money as a pre-employment or post-employment requirement. This means that we never ask for ‘recruitment fees’, ‘processing fees’, ‘interview fees’, or any other kind of money in exchange for offer letters or interviews at any time during the hiring process.



Applications for this position will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisting and interviews will take place at any stage during the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a suitable candidate is selected before the advertised closing date.

jobs.title: Principal Information System Security Officer
jobs.description:
Clarity Innovations is a trusted national security partner, dedicated to safeguarding our nation’s interests and delivering innovative solutions that empower the Intelligence Community (IC) and Department of Defense (DoD) to transform data into actionable intelligence, ensuring mission success in an evolving world.

Our mission-first software and data engineering platform modernizes data operations, utilizing advanced workflows, CI/CD, and secure DevSecOps practices. We focus on challenges in Information Warfare, Cyber Operations, Operational Security, and Data Structuring, enabling end-to-end solutions that drive operational impact.

We are committed to delivering cutting-edge tools and capabilities that address the most complex national security challenges, empowering our partners to stay ahead of emerging threats and ensuring the success of their critical missions. At Clarity, we are people-focused and set on being a destination employer for top talent, offering an environment where innovation thrives, careers grow, and individuals are valued. Join us as we continue to lead innovation and tackle the most pressing challenges in national security.

Position Overview

The ISSO supports the ISSM and owns the authorization documentation for this platform at the unclassified (CUI) classification level, across every development team on it. This is the single ISSO seat for that platform and classification combination at this time, and separate ISSOs cover the other environments. The ISSO is not embedded with any one team. Instead, the ISSO works with all of them, each with its own goals and priorities, and consolidates those into a single authorization package covering the entire platform. The role centers on establishing and maintaining ATO packages and their associated artifacts, maintaining interconnection agreements (ISAs and related), and transitioning the package from NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 to Rev 5. Initial scope is the unclassified (CUI) system only. As clearance and access are completed, the ISSO also provides surge support and backfill for the ISSOs of other environments, including leave coverage. Success requires comfort switching context between teams, a commitment to keeping documentation accurate as the system changes, and interest in improving documentation and reporting through automation where practical.

Key Responsibilities

• Owns and maintains the authorization package and its body of evidence (BoE), including the SSP, control statement responses, and supporting artifacts, so that documentation reflects the current state of the system. eMASS is the system of record for the BoE and POA&Ms in this role.

• Executes the package transition from NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 to Rev 5 in coordination with the ISSM, using artifacts demonstrating compliance provided by security engineers and engineering development teams

• Develops and maintains interconnection and boundary documentation, including ISAs and related agreements

• Owns POA&M entries and milestone tracking, coordinating with security engineers and development teams on remediation artifacts and status

• Prepares ConMon documentation and reporting on schedule and ensures findings are accurately captured in the package

• Maintains the SBOM and component version representation in the package, and validates components against CVE data and mitigation guidance. Where a component carries a vulnerability, identifies the required remediation (for example, moving to a fixed version or above) and communicates it to the owning team. Where a compensating control is proposed instead, participates in the architectural plan and in obtaining AO and government customer buy-in. The role identifies vulnerabilities and required mitigations; it does not choose between alternative libraries or products.

• Participates in the CCB, documenting the authorization impact of proposed changes and keeping the package aligned with approved changes, including filling in for the project ISSM on the unclassified system when the ISSM is unavailable. Contractor ISSOs and ISSMs do not accept new risk. They determine whether a proposal aligns with the current risk posture and refer anything outside it to the appropriate government authority.

• Coordinates with security engineers for technical evidence, with development teams across the platform for artifacts, and with SCAs, AO staff, and government counterparts on documentation requests and findings

• Drafts risk acceptance and deviation documentation when assigned by the ISSM, for ISSM review before submission

• Identifies project-specific security training and awareness gaps not covered by customer or company guidance, in coordination with the ISSM

• Supports security authorization activities in compliance with RMF, DoDI 8510.01, and related DoD processes

• Provides surge support and backfill for ISSOs of other environments, including leave coverage, as clearance and access allow. This is a longer-term expectation; initial duties are limited to the unclassified (CUI) system.

Qualifications

• U.S. citizen able to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI clearance with CI polygraph, as longer-term duties include cross-environment coverage

• Current DoD 8570.01-M IAM Level II or III certification. This program is currently bound by 8570 certification requirements and will transition to DoD 8140 qualification once the applicable 8140 certification list is approved.

• 5 or more years of relevant experience developing and maintaining RMF authorization packages (7 or more preferred)

• Working knowledge of RMF, NIST SP 800-37, NIST SP 800-53 (Rev 4 and Rev 5), NIST SP 800-53B, NIST SP 800-60, and DoDI 8510.01

• Experience maintaining the BoE, control statements, and POA&Ms in eMASS

• Experience writing or maintaining ISAs or other interconnection agreements (NIST SP 800-47 Rev 1)

• Understanding of network flows and architecture, especially cloud (Azure and AWS), on-premises, and hybrid environments, and the complexities each introduces

• Ability to context switch across multiple teams with differing goals and priorities, and to consolidate them into one coherent authorization package for the whole platform

• Familiarity with auditing and control assessments, including working with SCAs

• Familiarity with the SDLC and with working across multiple Agile or DevSecOps development teams

• Knowledge of government security requirements for unclassified and CUI systems

• Strong written and verbal communication skills. Documentation in this environment is produced with limited AI/LLM support, because many LLMs are not approved to process CUI or above, so candidates must write clear, accurate technical documentation on their own.

• Ability to work independently with engineering and government stakeholders

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical discipline. No experience equivalency applies.

Preferred Qualifications

• Active TS/SCI clearance with CI polygraph

• Experience migrating an authorization package from NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 to Rev 5

• Experience taking a package from creation to full ATO

• Experience with classified system authorization (for example CNSSI 1253 overlays)

• Experience reading and interpreting vulnerability scan results to support CVE validation and POA&M entries

• Experience mentoring junior teammates

Location and Clearance

This is a hybrid position with an expected 3-4 days onsite. Clarity Innovations strives to set consistent expectations and ensure a flexible and healthy work-life balance, but due to the position's nature and emergent customer needs, some weeks may exceed 3-4 days and others may require no onsite work.  It will require a counterintelligence polygraph upon hiring if not already attained.

Principal Information Security Engineer

$102,200—$173,700 USD

Pay Range

The posted pay range reflects the national salary range for this position and is provided to give candidates a general understanding of the compensation opportunity. The actual salary offered will be determined based on the requirements of the position and a variety of job-related factors, which may include geographic location, applicable Federal Government contract labor categories and wage rates, relevant experience, skills and competencies, education, certifications, and the scope and responsibilities of the role.

Because this position may be performed in multiple locations and may be subject to different contract requirements, the salary ultimately offered may vary based on the applicable location and contract. The posted range is not a guarantee of a specific starting salary or an indication that an offer will be made at any particular point within the range.

Total Rewards

In addition to competitive base pay, Clarity provides a Total Rewards package designed to attract and retain exceptional professionals committed to excellence. Our benefits reflect the value we place on skilled individuals who drive our impact in critical digital missions.

At Clarity, a career means joining a high-performing team advancing vital work in the digital landscape. We encourage you to consider the total value of joining us—competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and resources that support your growth and impact.

Our Total Rewards package includes performance-based bonuses, extensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan with company match, substantial paid time off and holidays, flexible work arrangements where possible, and a range of income protection benefits. We are committed to supporting your well-being, professional growth, and ability to contribute to essential digital missions.

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Senior Support Engineer
jobs.description:
Who we are

At CarGurus (NASDAQ: CARG), our mission is to give people the power to reach their destination. We started as a small team of developers determined to bring trust and transparency to car shopping. Since then, our history of innovation and go-to-market acceleration has driven industry-leading growth. In fact, we’re the largest and fastest-growing automotive marketplace, and we’ve been profitable for over 15 years.

What we do

The market is evolving, and we are too, moving the entire automotive journey online and guiding our customers through every step. That includes everything from the sale of an old car to the financing, purchase, and delivery of a new one. Today, tens of millions of consumers visit CarGurus.com each month, and ~30,000 dealerships use our products. But they're not the only ones who love CarGurus—our employees do, too. We have a people-first culture that fosters kindness, collaboration, and innovation, and empowers our Gurus with tools to fuel their career growth. Disrupting a trillion-dollar industry requires fresh and diverse perspectives. Come join us for the ride!

Role overview

The Senior Support Engineer is the technical specialist inside Customer Operations & Support who closes the gap between "a dealer reports a problem" and "Engineering has a clean ticket to act on." You will reproduce defects, read traces and logs, validate IMS partner integrations, and decide whether an issue is a bug, expected behavior, a configuration problem, or a partner-side failure.

What you'll do

• Serve as the technical escalation point for all products, including SaaS ones.

• Reproduce dealer-reported issues in-product, read distributed traces in Observe and Honeycomb, and correlate logs across Site, Dealer Data Service, Pricing services, ML rec models, and IMS partner APIs.

• Distinguish true defects from expected behavior, configuration issues, or partner-side failures (DealerCenter, DealerSync, vAuto, Dealer Specialties, Vincue, MotorcarMarketing).

• Submit clean, reproducible tickets to Product Acceleration (PAES) and Engineering, with steps, evidence, and impact framing.

• Own the FireHydrant trigger decision during business hours for products; coordinate with on-call engineers during incidents.

• Partner with Tier 1 and Tier 2 Dealer Support Operations to handle escalations and upskill the team over time.

• Contribute to and maintain the Product Support Playbook: SLA framework, severity definitions, escalation paths, status page integration, named case routing in Salesforce.

• Validate launch readiness for new products against the COS/Engineering intake gate (uptime SLO, alerting, status page, escalation tree, training, dedicated Slack channel).

• Participate in postmortems and represent the customer-impact narrative; help drive resiliency improvements upstream.

• Build feedback loops with Product Marketing and Sales Specialists so dealer expectations align with what we can support.

What you'll bring

• 4+ years in a technical support, support engineering, solutions engineering, or customer engineering role at a B2B company.

• Demonstrated ability to read logs and distributed traces (Observe, Honeycomb, Datadog, Splunk, or equivalent), validate API payloads, and reproduce defects in production software.

• Comfort working with SQL, XML, JSON, and REST API responses; basic scripting in Python, Bash, or a similar language to investigate issues.

• Strong written and verbal communication; able to translate between dealers, account teams, Product, and Engineering.

• Calm judgment in incident situations and the ability to make defensible "is this an outage" calls.

• Experience supporting products with third-party data integrations (CRM, DMS, inventory feeds, ML/pricing services).

jobs.title: Corporate Program Security Officer
jobs.description:
Clarity Innovations is a trusted national security partner, dedicated to safeguarding our nation’s interests and delivering innovative solutions that empower the Intelligence Community (IC) and Department of Defense (DoD) to transform data into actionable intelligence, ensuring mission success in an evolving world.

Our mission-first software and data engineering platform modernizes data operations, utilizing advanced workflows, CI/CD, and secure DevSecOps practices. We focus on challenges in Information Warfare, Cyber Operations, Operational Security, and Data Structuring, enabling end-to-end solutions that drive operational impact.

We are committed to delivering cutting-edge tools and capabilities that address the most complex national security challenges, empowering our partners to stay ahead of emerging threats and ensuring the success of their critical missions. At Clarity, we are people-focused and set on being a destination employer for top talent, offering an environment where innovation thrives, careers grow, and individuals are valued. Join us as we continue to lead innovation and tackle the most pressing challenges in national security.

Position Summary

The Corporate Program Security Officer (CPSO) is responsible for the oversight, coordination, and execution of security requirements supporting the organization's classified contract portfolio, including Department of War (DoW), Intelligence Community (IC), and Special Access Program (SAP) environments.

Reporting directly to the Director of Security, the Corporate Program Security Officer serves as the primary corporate security liaison between executive leadership, program management, government security representatives, and assigned Program Security Officers (PSOs). This position ensures consistent implementation of program security requirements, regulatory compliance, operational readiness, and effective security support across multiple classified programs and customer environments.

The CPSO provides strategic and operational security leadership, establishes standardized program security processes, identifies and mitigates security risks, and supports business growth through security planning for new contracts, proposals, transitions, and program expansions.

The ideal candidate is a highly experienced, solutions-oriented security professional who can balance regulatory compliance with operational effectiveness while enabling successful mission execution.

Role Expectations

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Corporate Program Security Oversight

• Provide centralized oversight and coordination of security operations across multiple classified programs, contracts, and government customers.

• Ensure consistent implementation of program-specific security requirements, corporate policies, and applicable government regulations.

• Serve as the primary corporate point of contact for program security matters, escalating significant risks, compliance concerns, and resource requirements to the Director of Security.

• Develop and maintain standardized program security processes, procedures, templates, and reporting mechanisms.

• Coordinate with assigned PSOs, CPSOs, CSSOs, and other security personnel to ensure continuity of security support.

• Monitor program security performance, identify operational gaps, and implement corrective actions.

• Maintain visibility into program security requirements, deliverables, staffing needs, and upcoming milestones.

• Collaborate with ISSMs and cybersecurity teams to align industrial security operations with system security plans (SSPs) and continuous monitoring requirements.

Regulatory Compliance and Security Program Management

• Ensure compliance with applicable security requirements, including: 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM) Intelligence Community Directives (ICDs), including ICD 705 DoD SAP security requirements, when applicable Customer-specific security classification guides and program security directives Contractual security requirements and DD Forms 254 Applicable personnel security reporting requirements, including SEAD 3

• Support the development, implementation, and maintenance of corporate and program-specific security policies.

• Coordinate internal security reviews, government inspections, assessments, and compliance evaluations.

• Identify deficiencies and develop corrective action plans to address security vulnerabilities.

• Ensure appropriate documentation, records, and supporting materials are maintained for inspection and audit readiness.

• Support the Director of Security in maintaining a proactive compliance posture across all assigned programs.

Program Security Operations

• Oversee the implementation of personnel, physical, administrative, and information security requirements for assigned classified programs.

• Coordinate personnel indoctrinations, debriefings, access nominations, visit authorizations, and program-specific security processing.

• Ensure program security personnel maintain accurate access rosters, accountability records, and required security documentation.

• Coordinate with the Personnel Security Team to facilitate clearance processing and program access requirements.

• Support the implementation and maintenance of classified information handling, storage, transmission, and accountability procedures.

• Assist with the development and maintenance of program-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), security plans, and security classification guidance.

• Coordinate with Physical Security personnel regarding SCIF/SAPF accreditation, modifications, inspections, and operational requirements.

• Ensure security incidents and potential violations are documented, reported, and addressed in accordance with applicable requirements.

Program Management and Government Customer Engagement

• Establish and maintain effective working relationships with government security representatives, Contracting Officer's Representatives (CORs), program managers, and corporate leadership.

• Serve as a trusted security advisor to program leadership regarding contractual security obligations and operational requirements.

• Participate in program kickoff meetings, contract transition activities, and recurring program management reviews.

• Coordinate security requirements for new contract awards, task orders, subcontractors, and program expansions.

• Review DD Forms 254 and associated security requirements to identify security responsibilities and potential compliance gaps.

• Support the resolution of program security challenges while minimizing operational disruptions.

• Provide security input for contract proposals, staffing plans, facility requirements, and program execution strategies.

Business Development and Program Growth Support

• Partner with business development, contracts, and program leadership to assess security requirements for new opportunities.

• Review solicitations, statements of work, and security requirements to identify potential security costs, staffing needs, and facility requirements.

• Assist with the development of security transition plans for newly awarded contracts.

• Support security integration activities associated with acquisitions, new business units, and expanding contract portfolios.

• Evaluate the organization's security capabilities and readiness to support emerging customer requirements.

• Identify opportunities to improve program security efficiency through process improvements, automation, and technology solutions.

Required Qualifications

Education

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Professional Experience

• 10+ years of industrial security experience supporting cleared federal contractors. Demonstrated experience managing or coordinating security requirements across multiple classified programs. Experience working directly with government security representatives and program leadership. Strong working knowledge of NISPOM, ICDs, and applicable DoW and IC security requirements. Experience supporting government security inspections, compliance assessments, and corrective action activities. Demonstrated ability to interpret DD Forms 254, security classification guides, and customer-specific security requirements. Experience developing and implementing security policies, SOPs, and program security processes. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Demonstrated leadership, mentoring, and cross-functional collaboration capabilities.

Salary Range: $145,900 - $248,000

Pay Range

The posted pay range reflects the national salary range for this position and is provided to give candidates a general understanding of the compensation opportunity. The actual salary offered will be determined based on the requirements of the position and a variety of job-related factors, which may include geographic location, applicable Federal Government contract labor categories and wage rates, relevant experience, skills and competencies, education, certifications, and the scope and responsibilities of the role.

Because this position may be performed in multiple locations and may be subject to different contract requirements, the salary ultimately offered may vary based on the applicable location and contract. The posted range is not a guarantee of a specific starting salary or an indication that an offer will be made at any particular point within the range.

Total Rewards

In addition to competitive base pay, Clarity provides a Total Rewards package designed to attract and retain exceptional professionals committed to excellence. Our benefits reflect the value we place on skilled individuals who drive our impact in critical digital missions.

At Clarity, a career means joining a high-performing team advancing vital work in the digital landscape. We encourage you to consider the total value of joining us—competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and resources that support your growth and impact.

Our Total Rewards package includes performance-based bonuses, extensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan with company match, substantial paid time off and holidays, flexible work arrangements where possible, and a range of income protection benefits. We are committed to supporting your well-being, professional growth, and ability to contribute to essential digital missions.

Position Summary

The Facility Security Officer (FSO) / Insider Threat Program Senior Official (ITPSO) is responsible for the administration, implementation, oversight, and continuous improvement of the organization's industrial security and insider threat programs. This position ensures compliance with the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), 32 CFR Part 117, Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) requirements, Security Executive Agent Directives (SEADs), and applicable Department of War (DoW), Intelligence Community (IC), and government customer security directives.

The FSO/ITPSO serves as a primary security authority for assigned cleared facilities and is responsible for managing personnel security, classified information protection, security education and awareness, incident reporting, government inspections, and industrial security compliance.

In the capacity of ITPSO, the individual is responsible for implementing and administering a comprehensive insider threat program designed to identify, assess, report, and mitigate potential insider threats to classified information, personnel, facilities, systems, and national security interests.

Working closely with the Director of Security, executive leadership, Information Technology, Human Resources, Legal, FSOs, CSSOs, CPSOs, and government security representatives, this position ensures security programs are compliant, proactive, scalable, and aligned with organizational mission requirements.

The ideal candidate is a highly experienced, solutions-oriented security professional who demonstrates strong regulatory knowledge, sound judgment, exceptional interpersonal skills, and the ability to balance security requirements with operational objectives.

Role Expectations

Industrial Security Program Management

• Serve as the designated FSO for assigned cleared facilities and CAGE codes, ensuring compliance with 32 CFR Part 117 and applicable government security requirements.

• Develop, implement, maintain, and continuously improve the organization's industrial security program.

• Establish and maintain Standard Practice and Procedures (SPP), security policies, operating procedures, and compliance documentation.

• Administer security requirements associated with the organization's Facility Clearance (FCL), including coordination with DCSA.

• Maintain organizational information and required facility records in the National Industrial Security System (NISS).

• Ensure applicable Key Management Personnel (KMP) are appropriately documented, processed, and maintained.

• Oversee compliance with classified contract security requirements, including DD Form 254 review, interpretation, and administration.

• Coordinate security requirements associated with new contract awards, subcontractors, facility changes, and organizational growth.

• Conduct periodic assessments of security processes to identify vulnerabilities, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.

• Advise the Director of Security and executive leadership on regulatory requirements, emerging security risks, and recommended mitigation strategies.

• Support security standardization across multiple facilities and CAGE codes operating under a Multiple Facility Organization (MFO), when applicable.

Insider Threat Program Management and Oversight

• Serve as the formally appointed Insider Threat Program Senior Official (ITPSO) for assigned cleared entities.

• Develop, implement, and maintain a written Insider Threat Program Plan compliant with 32 CFR 117.7 and applicable DCSA guidance.

• Ensure the Insider Threat Program addresses the identification, assessment, reporting, and mitigation of potential insider threat indicators.

• Establish and lead an Insider Threat Working Group (ITWG) or equivalent cross-functional coordination structure involving Security, Human Resources, Information Technology, Legal, and other appropriate stakeholders.

• Coordinate the lawful and authorized collection, evaluation, and integration of relevant insider threat information from appropriate organizational sources.

• Establish procedures for identifying, documenting, escalating, and reporting potential insider threat indicators.

• Coordinate with the FSO, Director of Security, and government authorities regarding reportable information and security concerns.

• Ensure timely reporting of applicable insider threat information and adverse information through required government channels.

• Maintain insider threat records and documentation in accordance with applicable legal, privacy, retention, and government requirements.

• Develop and deliver initial and annual insider threat awareness training.

• Ensure personnel assigned insider threat program responsibilities receive appropriate role-specific training.

• Conduct periodic insider threat program effectiveness reviews and implement improvements.

• Support DCSA insider threat program assessments, inspections, and corrective action activities.

• Promote a security culture that encourages responsible reporting, employee awareness, and early identification of concerning behaviors while protecting individual privacy and due process.

Security Compliance, Self-Inspections, and DCSA Assessments

• Plan, coordinate, and execute required annual security self-inspections.

• Develop and maintain security inspection checklists, compliance assessment tools, and supporting documentation.

• Prepare assigned facilities for DCSA security reviews, vulnerability assessments, and other government inspections.

• Coordinate employee interviews, document reviews, and inspection activities with DCSA representatives.

• Identify compliance deficiencies and develop corrective action plans with defined responsibilities and completion milestones.

• Monitor corrective action implementation and validate resolution of identified deficiencies.

• Prepare security compliance reports, self-inspection summaries, and management briefings.

• Support Senior Management Official (SMO) self-inspection certification requirements.

• Maintain inspection readiness through continuous monitoring, process improvement, and personnel training.

• Monitor changes in NISPOM, DCSA guidance, and government directives to ensure timely updates to internal security processes.

Classified Information Protection and Security Operations

• Oversee administrative security requirements associated with the receipt, handling, safeguarding, transmission, reproduction, and destruction of classified information.

• Ensure classified information is accessed only by authorized personnel with appropriate eligibility, access authorization, and need-to-know.

• Coordinate classified material accountability and document control procedures where applicable.

• Ensure approved classified storage and safeguarding practices are implemented and maintained.

• Collaborate with physical security personnel to address facility security requirements, access control, and safeguarding concerns.

• Coordinate classified visits and government security inspections.

• Support classified information incident response, preliminary inquiries, and required reporting.

• Ensure security violations and potential compromises are appropriately documented, escalated, and reported.

• Maintain coordination with program security personnel regarding collateral, SCI, and SAP security responsibilities, as applicable.

• Collaborate with ISSMs and cybersecurity teams to align industrial security operations with system security plans (SSPs) and continuous monitoring requirements.

Security Education, Training, and Awareness (SETA)

• Develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive Security Education, Training, and Awareness Program.

• Conduct initial security briefings, annual refresher training, insider threat awareness training, and specialized security training.

• Ensure training addresses applicable NISPOM, SEAD 3, insider threat, classified information protection, and organizational reporting requirements.

• Develop training materials, employee notifications, awareness campaigns, and security guidance.

• Track completion of required security training and maintain supporting documentation.

• Identify knowledge gaps and recommend targeted security education initiatives.

• Promote a positive security culture emphasizing accountability, awareness, collaboration, and mission support.

Security Incident Management and Reporting

• Manage the identification, documentation, assessment, escalation, and reporting of security incidents.

• Conduct or coordinate preliminary inquiries into suspected security violations, potential compromises, and reportable security concerns.

• Determine appropriate reporting and escalation requirements in coordination with authorized security leadership and government representatives.

• Ensure required reports are submitted within applicable regulatory and customer-directed timelines.

• Develop corrective actions and recommend measures to prevent recurrence.

• Maintain security incident documentation and track resolution activities.

• Coordinate with Human Resources, Legal, Information Technology, and leadership when incidents involve multiple organizational functions.

• Support the implementation of graduated disciplinary procedures consistent with organizational policy and applicable legal requirements.

Required Qualifications

Education and Experience

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 10+ years of industrial security experience supporting cleared federal contractors.

• Prior experience serving as an FSO, Assistant FSO, Senior Industrial Security Specialist, or comparable security program lead.

• Demonstrated knowledge of 32 CFR Part 117, NISPOM, DCSA requirements, and applicable Security Executive Agent Directives.

• Experience developing, administering, or providing substantial support to an insider threat program.

• Demonstrated experience preparing for and supporting DCSA security assessments and annual self-inspections.

• Proficiency with DISS, NISS, NBIS, and related government personnel and facility security systems.

• Experience administering personnel security processes and security reporting requirements.

• Demonstrated ability to interpret regulatory requirements and translate them into practical policies and procedures.

• Experience developing and maintaining SPPs, security plans, training programs, and compliance documentation.

• Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and project management capabilities.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• Demonstrated ability to manage sensitive information with discretion, professionalism, and sound judgment.

Security Clearance

Training Requirements

Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations. That pushes defenders like us to operate at the highest level, and it deepens our need for good people who want to make a meaningful impact.

Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress is a remote-first team working to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to businesses of all sizes. We work closely with security teams and service providers protecting complex environments, often without the time or headcount to handle it all. That’s why we build our technology in-house and back it with a 24/7 human-led Security Operations Center (SOC). As a result, our platform is never disconnected from the experts who manage it, ensuring our customers' protection.

Huntress now secures more than 6M endpoints and 16M identities worldwide. Those numbers keep growing because more businesses rely on us to help carry the load and operate with more confidence. Every day, you can see that commitment in how we stand with our customers and how we show up for each other.

Reports to: Manager, Technical Account Management

Location: Remote US

Compensation Range: $160,000 to $170,000 OTE (80/20 split) plus equity

The Huntress team is looking for a highly motivated and collaborative Technical Account Manager with excellent communication skills and the ability to think and act quickly. TAMs at Huntress constitute the primary technical liaison post-sales. The TAM is responsible for ensuring customer satisfaction through its duties of providing high-quality post-sales technical support with a consultative approach. Their goal is to help our customers and partners maximize the value from the Huntress Platform, troubleshoot product break-fix issues, and improve the partner/customer experience by coordinating with internal Huntress teams to deliver solutions that drive long-term, healthy partner/customer relationships.

Develops an understanding of customers’ business needs and educates them on how they can improve their security posture with Huntress
