jobs.title: Personnel Security Team Lead
jobs.description:
Clarity Innovations is a trusted national security partner, dedicated to safeguarding our nation’s interests and delivering innovative solutions that empower the Intelligence Community (IC) and Department of Defense (DoD) to transform data into actionable intelligence, ensuring mission success in an evolving world.

Our mission-first software and data engineering platform modernizes data operations, utilizing advanced workflows, CI/CD, and secure DevSecOps practices. We focus on challenges in Information Warfare, Cyber Operations, Operational Security, and Data Structuring, enabling end-to-end solutions that drive operational impact.

We are committed to delivering cutting-edge tools and capabilities that address the most complex national security challenges, empowering our partners to stay ahead of emerging threats and ensuring the success of their critical missions. At Clarity, we are people-focused and set on being a destination employer for top talent, offering an environment where innovation thrives, careers grow, and individuals are valued. Join us as we continue to lead innovation and tackle the most pressing challenges in national security.

Position Summary

The Personnel Security Team Lead is responsible for leading, coordinating, and overseeing the daily execution of personnel security operations supporting classified government contracts, facilities, and mission requirements.

This position serves as the organization's senior personnel security subject matter expert, ensuring the accurate, timely, and compliant administration of security clearance processing, personnel eligibility verification, access management, government reporting, security briefings, visit authorizations, and personnel security recordkeeping.

The Personnel Security Team Lead provides operational leadership and technical guidance to security team members, establishes standardized workflows, monitors workload distribution, and drives process improvements to ensure efficient and consistent security support across multiple facilities, CAGE codes, and mission verticals.

Working closely with the Director of Security, Facility Security Officers (FSOs), Contractor Special Security Officers (CSSOs), Contractor Program Security Officers (CPSOs), Human Resources, Recruiting, Program Management, and government security representatives, this position ensures personnel security requirements are effectively integrated into employee onboarding, contract staffing, program access, and organizational growth initiatives.

The successful candidate will be a highly organized, proactive, and solutions-oriented security professional who demonstrates strong technical expertise, exceptional customer service, sound judgment, and the ability to lead personnel security operations in a dynamic government contracting environment.

Role Expectations

Personnel Security Operations Management

• Lead and coordinate daily personnel security activities supporting assigned cleared facilities, contracts, and government customers.

• Oversee the full lifecycle of personnel security processing, including clearance initiation, eligibility verification, investigation tracking, access coordination, periodic vetting requirements, and personnel out-processing.

• Ensure personnel security actions are completed accurately, efficiently, and in compliance with applicable government regulations and customer directives.

• Develop, implement, and maintain standardized personnel security workflows, checklists, tracking tools, and operating procedures.

• Monitor personnel security requests, establish priorities, and coordinate assignments among security team members.

• Maintain visibility into pending actions, processing timelines, outstanding requirements, and operational bottlenecks.

• Identify opportunities to improve personnel security processes, reduce administrative delays, and enhance customer support.

• Provide regular status updates, workload assessments, and recommendations to the Director of Security.

Security Clearance Processing and Eligibility Management

• Oversee personnel security processing using authorized government systems, including the Defense Information System for Security (DISS), National Background Investigation Services (NBIS), and other applicable platforms.

• Coordinate initiation and tracking of security clearance investigations, reinvestigations when applicable, and Continuous Vetting (CV) requirements.

• Review personnel security submissions for administrative accuracy and completeness within authorized FSO or security designee responsibilities.

• Monitor investigation and eligibility statuses and coordinate follow-up actions with appropriate government authorities.

• Verify security clearance eligibility prior to coordinating classified access.

• Maintain accurate clearance and access records and ensure appropriate system updates.

• Coordinate personnel security actions involving transfers, separations, changes in affiliation, and contract transitions.

• Identify and resolve administrative discrepancies that could delay personnel onboarding or program access.

• Ensure eligibility and access actions remain within delegated organizational and government authority.

Personnel Access, Indoctrinations, and Visit Management

• Oversee the administration of personnel access requirements supporting collateral, SCI, and SAP programs, as applicable.

• Coordinate initial security briefings, classified access acknowledgments, nondisclosure agreements, indoctrinations, and debriefings.

• Ensure personnel meet applicable clearance eligibility, access authorization, need-to-know, and customer approval requirements.

• Manage or oversee classified visit requests and visit certifications through DISS and applicable customer-directed systems.

• Coordinate access actions with FSOs, CSSOs, CPSOs, and government security representatives.

• Ensure timely removal or modification of access when personnel separate, transfer, or no longer require access.

• Maintain appropriate documentation of access actions and security briefings.

• Support onboarding and offboarding processes to minimize delays while maintaining regulatory compliance.

Regulatory Compliance and Personnel Security Reporting

• Ensure personnel security processes comply with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM), applicable Security Executive Agent Directives, and customer-specific requirements.

• Administer and monitor reporting requirements associated with SEAD 3, adverse information, foreign travel, foreign contacts, and other reportable activities.

• Ensure identified reportable information is promptly elevated to the designated FSO or other authorized security official.

• Coordinate preparation and submission of required reports through approved government reporting channels.

• Maintain appropriate documentation of reportable activities, actions taken, and required follow-up.

• Support DCSA security reviews, annual self-inspections, and government customer assessments.

• Identify personnel security compliance gaps and recommend corrective actions.

• Assist with development and maintenance of personnel security policies, SPPs, and reporting procedures.

• Monitor regulatory changes and recommend updates to internal processes.

Security Request and Workflow Management

• Oversee intake, triage, assignment, tracking, and resolution of personnel security requests submitted through approved organizational systems.

• Ensure requests are assigned to appropriate security personnel based on responsibility, expertise, priority, and workload.

• Maintain accurate status information in approved security management platforms and master tracking systems.

• Establish internal service-level expectations for common personnel security actions.

• Monitor overdue requests, identify recurring delays, and implement corrective process improvements.

• Coordinate with Recruiting, Human Resources, Program Management, and other stakeholders to resolve processing issues.

• Ensure employees and requestors receive timely and professional updates regarding their requests.

• Develop dashboards and reports that provide leadership visibility into security workload, processing efficiency, and outstanding actions.

Required Qualifications

Education and Experience

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in personnel security or industrial security, preferably within a DoW and/or Intelligence Community government contracting environment.

• Demonstrated experience administering personnel security processes under the National Industrial Security Program.

• Advanced working knowledge of 32 CFR Part 117, applicable SEAD requirements, and government personnel security procedures.

• Extensive hands-on experience with DISS, NBIS, and other applicable government personnel security systems.

• Experience coordinating security clearance investigations, eligibility actions, access administration, and personnel security reporting.

• Demonstrated experience supporting collateral and/or SCI personnel security operations.

• Experience leading personnel security workflows, mentoring team members, or coordinating operational assignments.

• Experience supporting DCSA inspections, security self-assessments, and compliance reviews.

• Strong knowledge of personnel security records management, privacy requirements, and sensitive information protection.

• Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and high-volume security processing requirements.

• Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

• Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and resolve complex personnel security issues.

• Demonstrated commitment to exceptional customer service and operational excellence.

• Ability to obtain and maintain applicable customer-specific accesses

Salary Range: $111,700 - $189,900

Pay Range

The posted pay range reflects the national salary range for this position and is provided to give candidates a general understanding of the compensation opportunity. The actual salary offered will be determined based on the requirements of the position and a variety of job-related factors, which may include geographic location, applicable Federal Government contract labor categories and wage rates, relevant experience, skills and competencies, education, certifications, and the scope and responsibilities of the role.

Because this position may be performed in multiple locations and may be subject to different contract requirements, the salary ultimately offered may vary based on the applicable location and contract. The posted range is not a guarantee of a specific starting salary or an indication that an offer will be made at any particular point within the range.

Total Rewards

In addition to competitive base pay, Clarity provides a Total Rewards package designed to attract and retain exceptional professionals committed to excellence. Our benefits reflect the value we place on skilled individuals who drive our impact in critical digital missions.

At Clarity, a career means joining a high-performing team advancing vital work in the digital landscape. We encourage you to consider the total value of joining us—competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and resources that support your growth and impact.

Our Total Rewards package includes performance-based bonuses, extensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan with company match, substantial paid time off and holidays, flexible work arrangements where possible, and a range of income protection benefits. We are committed to supporting your well-being, professional growth, and ability to contribute to essential digital missions.

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Marketing Operations Manager
jobs.description:
We're looking for a technical, data-driven Marketing Operations Manager to own HubSpot, our marketing automation platform, and serve as a key operational partner to our Director of Growth Operations. You'll be the go-to person for how marketing data moves through our systems, how campaigns get built and measured, and how our reporting stays accurate and trusted.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who likes building systems as much as running them. We're especially excited about candidates who use LLMs and AI agents in their daily work to automate repetitive tasks, speed up analysis, and scale what one person can deliver.


WHAT YOU'LL DO


HUBSPOT OWNERSHIP

 - Serve as the primary administrator of HubSpot, owning configuration, user management, properties, lifecycle stages, lead scoring, workflows, lists, and forms.

 - Build and maintain scalable automation for nurture programs, lead management, and campaign execution.

 - Own data hygiene in HubSpot: deduplication, field governance, naming conventions, and documentation.

 - Evaluate and roll out new HubSpot features, and keep the platform clean, well-documented, and ready to scale.

 - Run the HubSpot website (CMS) operationally, including programs, forms, and list clean-up.


CAMPAIGN OPERATIONS

 - Partner with the Director of Growth Operations and campaign owners to build, QA, and launch campaigns: emails, landing pages, forms, workflows, and webinar integrations.

 - Set up campaign tracking, UTM standards, and attribution so every program can be measured from the start.

 - Troubleshoot campaign and integration issues quickly and document the fixes.


DELIVERABILITY & ORCHESTRATION

 - Own email and SMS orchestration across HubSpot and SendGrid, including sending domains, domain health, and spam-flag monitoring.

 - Diagnose deliverability issues and coordinate fixes with IT and vendors.


REPORTING & ANALYTICS

 - Support marketing and campaign reporting, including funnel metrics, channel performance, and pipeline contribution.

 - Build and maintain dashboards in HubSpot and Salesforce that give stakeholders reliable, self-serve visibility.

 - Investigate data discrepancies across systems and resolve them at the source.

 - Trace what happened across HubSpot, Salesforce, calls, and contract records when something goes wrong, such as a customer question about what we sent, when, and why, and own the answer.

 - Turn data into clear takeaways and recommendations for marketing leadership.


SYSTEMS & INTEGRATIONS

 - Maintain the HubSpot–Salesforce sync, including field mapping, sync rules, and lead/contact handoff to Sales.

 - Work with RevOps on lead routing, lifecycle definitions, and funnel integrity across the GTM stack.

 - Support integrations with tools such as 6sense, Zoom and other webinar platforms, and enrichment providers.


SALES SUPPORT

 - Be the first line for BDR and AE system issues: triage, fix, and document.

 - Own lead routing rules and SLAs with RevOps, and persona coverage on target accounts.


AI AGENTS & PROCESS AUTOMATION

 - Own the marketing ops agents in production: monitor runs, QA output, fix failures, and raise each agent's level of autonomy as its record allows.

 - Use LLMs and agent-building tools to automate workflows, speed up QA, accelerate analysis, and draft documentation.

 - Identify manual, repetitive processes across marketing ops and build AI-assisted solutions to replace them.

 - Share what works so the broader team can adopt it.


WHO YOU ARE

 - 4–6+ years in marketing operations, with at least 3 years as a hands-on HubSpot administrator.

 - Deep knowledge of HubSpot Marketing Hub: workflows, lead scoring, lifecycle management, segmentation, and reporting.

 - Working knowledge of Salesforce, including objects, campaigns, reports, and how marketing data flows into the CRM.

 - Familiarity with 6sense or other intent and ABM platforms.

 - Demonstrated, practical use of LLMs (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT) and experience building agents or AI-assisted workflows to improve your own output. Be ready to show us examples.

 - Strong analytical skills, with comfort working in spreadsheets, dashboards, and messy data.

 - A technical mindset: you're comfortable with APIs, integrations, and troubleshooting across systems.

 - Hands-on experience with email deliverability (sending domains, authentication, SendGrid or similar) and SMS tools.

 - Highly organized, with a habit of documenting what you build.

 - Clear communicator who can explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with Marketo, especially migrating between or running alongside multiple MAPs.

 - HubSpot certifications (Marketing Hub, Operations Hub) or Salesforce Administrator certification.

 - Experience with ON24 or other webinar platforms, enrichment tools (e.g., ZoomInfo), or BI tools.

 - SQL, Python, or scripting skills.

 - B2B SaaS experience, ideally in a regulated or compliance-focused industry.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

First 90 days: You've audited HubSpot, documented how it's configured, fixed the highest-impact data and automation issues, and you run day-to-day marketing ops independently.

First 6 months: Campaign launches run on a repeatable, QA'd process; reporting is trusted; and you've shipped at least one AI-assisted workflow that saves the team real time.

First year: HubSpot is a scalable, well-governed system, marketing leadership makes decisions from reporting you own, and the ops agents run with an owner, monitoring, and a clean run record.


ABOUT US

At Foley, we’re reimagining how safety-sensitive industries hire, stay compliant, and manage risk. We’ve evolved into a modern SaaS company with an all-in-one, AI-ready platform that helps transportation, construction, distribution, and utility businesses operate faster, smarter, and safer.

As we continue to grow, we’re looking for curious, strategic thinkers who thrive in complexity, are motivated by making an impact, and want to join a team that’s passionate about building great products and supporting customers. Our core values — Teammateship, Grit, and Innovation — guide everything we do. Whether we’re collaborating internally or helping customers, we approach every challenge with optimism, humor, and a shared commitment to success.  

Benefits
Foley offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company match, paid time off and holidays, wellness programs, and an employee assistance program.

Equal Employment Opportunity 
Foley is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

jobs.title: Office & Operations Manager
jobs.description:
MAKING THE METALS POWERING THE WORLD

Solcoa is building the next generation of American metalmaking, starting with rare earths — the metals of power and motion. We've developed a new chemistry that converts rare earth oxides into high-purity metals — the materials inside every EV, fighter jet, wind turbine, and data center — cleaner, cheaper, and faster than any conventional process. Now we're scaling it to thousands of tonnes of annual production.




THE ROLE — OFFICE & OPERATIONS MANAGER

Keep a fast-moving industrial startup running. You'll own the day-to-day operations of our facility — office, vendors, purchasing support, onboarding, events. You'll be the first person many candidates, customers, and investors meet, and the person the whole team relies on to make problems disappear.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Run daily office operations: supplies, deliveries, food program, facilities requests, and vendor relationships.

 - Own purchasing support—place and track orders for parts, equipment, and consumables; chase lead times; reconcile receipts against POs.

 - Coordinate onboarding for new hires: workspace, equipment, badges, accounts, and first-week logistics.

 - Manage calendars, travel, and logistics for the leadership team; schedule interviews and customer/investor visits.

 - Plan team events, all-hands, and visits from customers, investors, and government stakeholders.

 - Support HR and finance operations, insurance paperwork, invoice processing, and expense management.

 - Keep the office and common areas organized, stocked, and presentable—and build the systems so it stays that way.
   
   


WHAT YOU BRING


REQUIRED

 - 3+ years in office management, operations, or executive support—startup or industrial environment preferred.

 - Ruthless organization: you keep many threads moving without dropping any, and you document as you go.

 - Strong written and verbal communication; comfortable dealing with vendors, candidates, and executives alike.

 - Proficiency with Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, and comfort picking up new tools (purchasing, HR, expense systems).

 - Bias to action—you see a problem and fix it before anyone asks.
   
   


PREFERRED

 - Experience at a hardware, manufacturing, or lab-based company.

 - Exposure to purchasing/receiving, light bookkeeping, or HR administration.

 - Experience supporting founders or executives directly.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Competitive base salary

 - Equity (stock options)

 - Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Company-provided lunch daily

jobs.title: Senior Sales Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
Who we are

At CarGurus (NASDAQ: CARG), our mission is to give people the power to reach their destination. We started as a small team of developers determined to bring trust and transparency to car shopping. Since then, our history of innovation and go-to-market acceleration has driven industry-leading growth. In fact, we’re the largest and fastest-growing automotive marketplace, and we’ve been profitable for over 15 years.

What we do

The market is evolving, and we are too, moving the entire automotive journey online and guiding our customers through every step. That includes everything from the sale of an old car to the financing, purchase, and delivery of a new one. Today, tens of millions of consumers visit CarGurus.com each month, and ~30,000 dealerships use our products. But they're not the only ones who love CarGurus—our employees do, too. We have a people-first culture that fosters kindness, collaboration, and innovation, and empowers our Gurus with tools to fuel their career growth. Disrupting a trillion-dollar industry requires fresh and diverse perspectives. Come join us for the ride!

Role overview

The Senior Sales Operations Analyst is a senior individual contributor responsible for resolving complex, high-impact Sales and Service issues and strengthening the processes that support the revenue organization. This role operates at the intersection of day-to-day support, Salesforce and CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote) operations, change management, and cross-functional problem solving.

The position serves as a senior technical and operational anchor. In addition to supporting individual accounts and escalations, this individual leads the investigation and resolution of systemic issues, large-scale account or contract work, product and process changes, and emerging exceptions that require judgment beyond the standard support queue. The role partners closely with Sales, Enterprise Applications, Product, Finance, Commissions, Legal, and other stakeholders to protect business continuity, reduce dealer and seller impact, and convert recurring workarounds into scalable solutions.

What you'll do

• Lead resolution of complex, ambiguous, and high-impact Sales issues, including large account or contract rebuilds, revenue attribution issues, system configuration changes, and product or process launch support.

• Triage systemic issues and emerging patterns; assess business impact, determine appropriate ownership, and coordinate resolution across Sales, Enterprise Applications, Product, Finance, Commissions, Legal, and vendor partners.

• Serve as a subject matter expert for Salesforce Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, and CPQ processes, including accounts, opportunities, quotes, quote lines, approvals, fulfillment, validation rules, permissions, and related operational workflows.

• Lead operational change management for new products, system releases, policy updates, and process changes; assess readiness, define operating procedures, coordinate stakeholder communication, and ensure changes are adopted effectively.

• Design and maintain scalable processes, controls, playbooks, and exception documentation that make complex work repeatable and reduce dependence on informal knowledge.

• Identify opportunities to eliminate manual work through process standardization, automation, and AI-enabled solutions; partner with technical teams to ensure operational requirements are captured and measurable.

• Act as a consultative and proactive business partner to Sales and Service leaders, providing guidance on best practices, policy interpretation, risk, and operational tradeoffs.

What you'll bring

• 5 years of experience in Sales Operations or Analyst function.

• 3+ years of experience using Salesforce or other CRM software to develop business solutions (certifications preferred).

• Proficient in GSuite applications.

• Experience with bulk data management tools such as G-Connector and Salesforce Data Loader, including controlled updates, data validation, and maintaining data integrity.

• Proven ability to leverage analytical and problem-solving skills in a fast-paced environment.

• Detail-oriented individual with the ability to quickly ramp up on new projects, the needs of the business, and technologies.

• Strong presentation, communication (written and verbal) skills, and interpersonal skills.

• Demonstrated flexibility and willingness to support urgent revenue escalations.

The displayed range represents the expected annual base salary / On-Target Earnings (OTE) for this position. On-Target Earnings (OTE) is inclusive of base salary and on-target commission earnings, which applies exclusively to sales roles.

Individual pay within this range is determined by work location and other factors such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

This annual base salary forms part of a comprehensive Total Rewards Package. In addition to benefits, this role may qualify for discretionary bonuses/incentives and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs).

Position Pay Range

$84,000—$105,000 USD

Working at CarGurus

We reward our Gurus’ curiosity and passion with best-in-class benefits and compensation, including equity for all employees, both when they start and as they continue to grow with us. Our career development and corporate giving programs, as well as our employee resource groups (ERGs) and communities, help people build connections while making an impact in personally meaningful ways. A flexible hybrid model and robust time off policies encourage work-life balance and individual well-being. Thoughtful perks like daily free lunch, a new car discount, meditation and fitness apps, commuting cost coverage, and more help our people create space for what matters most in their personal and professional lives.

CarGurus may require in-person interviews as part of our hiring process, particularly for positions based in our Boston and Dublin offices. Candidates selected for an in-person interview will be notified in advance. Please be aware that travel expenses are the responsibility of the candidate.

We welcome all

CarGurus strives to be a place to which people can bring the ultimate expression of themselves and their potential—starting with our hiring process. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, or sexual orientation. We foster an inclusive environment that values people for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. That’s why we hope you’ll apply even if you don’t check every box listed in the job description. We also encourage you to tell your recruiter if you require accommodations to participate in our hiring process due to a disability so we can provide the appropriate support. We want to know what only you can bring to CarGurus. #LI-Hybrid

jobs.title: Delivery Associate
jobs.description:
About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

As a Delivery Associate, your primary responsibility will be to successfully facilitate the delivery of customer vehicles, ensuring vehicle readiness prior to the customer appointment and completion of all required documentation. On the day that customers receive their vehicles, you will walk owners through all the key features and functions of their Lucid vehicle. Deliveries should be tailored to the owner’s needs through asking the appropriate questions to deliver on an exceptional customer centric experience.  The Delivery Associate also assists in facilitating lease-end vehicle returns, scheduling grounding appointments and ensuring all documentation is properly completed and logged.

Who we are looking for:

You are an enthusiastic and engaging quick learner with a fondness for providing memorable and enjoyable experiences. You will seek to understand the customer, learning preferences and personalizing the experience. You are highly organized, personable, and thrive in a dynamic work environment.

The Role

Customer Facing:

• Manage a pipeline of assigned deliveries through regular communication with Sales Specialist to align on delivery readiness

• Conduct pre-delivery conversations with customers to confirm delivery details and set clear expectations

• Guide customer through the key features and functions of their Lucid vehicle and tailoring the experience to their needs, whether at a delivery center, virtually, or an offsite location

• Conduct post-delivery conversations with customers to address any questions which may arise after the day of delivery

• Manage a pipeline of lease-end customers to schedule grounding of their vehicle upon lease maturation, scheduling appointments to ensure timely return of vehicles

• Conduct lease-end vehicle intake appointments

• Represent Lucid by articulating our technological, design, and quality advantages over competitors to benefit the customer’s purchasing decision

• Utilize Salesforce to document essential details such as inbound/outbound activity, information during the delivery ceremony, and delivery specifications

• Show a commitment to refining and adapting your approach to continuously enhance the customer experience, using feedback and customer delivery outcomes as guideposts

Operational:

• Manage vehicle readiness for all customer deliveries in your pipeline, including final quality check prior to vehicle handoff

• Prep and stage vehicles in delivery area prior to customer appointments

• Accurately complete required paperwork and collect necessary documents to finalize delivery or complete grounding of a lease return

• Book and track final mile transport as necessary, coordinating with the customer and carrier

• Assist with daily operations as needed

Qualifications:

• 2-5 years of customer facing professional experience.

• Excellent interpersonal and organizational skills with the ability to relentlessly prioritize and problem solve

• Comfortable navigating ambiguity

• Experience in a luxury retail or hospitality environment preferred.

• Comfort with using Salesforce or equivalent CRM system.

• A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business, sales, or related discipline.

• Ability to engage with all customers and members of the Lucid community in an authentic and courteous manner.

• Demonstrates a passion and enthusiasm for Lucid products and technological advances.

• Ability to gauge customer's requirements and interests to deliver a personalized and relevant interaction.

• Possesses strong relating skills including strong oral and written communication, empathy, and active listening ability.

• Ability to continually refine and adjust engagement approach to improve customer experiences through feedback and review of customer delivery outcomes.

• Ability to prioritize and schedule tasks independently that places the delivery experience at the center of their decision making.

• Takes ownership and responsibility for studio assets, including high-value Lucid customer vehicles.

• Demonstrates a passion for electric vehicles and premium vehicle markets.

• Is responsible for introducing our customers to their vehicle and creating a memorable orientation experience.

• Manages and overcomes customer feedback in a cordial and calm manner.

• Acts with urgency and champions excellence in all company objectives.

• Available to work weekends, evenings, nights, and holidays as needed.

• Valid driver’s license with no suspensions within the past year. Drivers under 21 must have maintained a Driver’s License for a minimum of 3 years and successfully complete Lucid Training upon hire

• Deliveries may occur both in Lucid facilities or at a remote location, so both local and overnight travel will be required on occasion

• Physical requirements include the ability to twist, bend, squat, reach, and stand for extended periods of time with or without reasonable accommodation.

At Lucid, we don’t just welcome diversity - we celebrate it! Lucid Motors is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, national or ethnic origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity and expression, marital status, and any other characteristic protected under applicable State or Federal laws and regulations.

Compensation & Benefits: Lucid offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance; life and disability coverage; paid time off; paid holidays, paid sick leave; and a 401(k) retirement plan. Hourly/non-exempt employees accrue up to 120 hours paid time off, and salaried/exempt employee accrue up to 160 hours paid time off.  Eligible employees may also participate in Lucid’s equity program and/or a discretionary annual cash incentive program. Incentive and equity awards, if applicable, are determined based on individual performance, role scope, market considerations, and overall company results, in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans.

jobs.title: Compensation Analyst II (Programs & Partnerships)
jobs.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

About the People Team

The People team helps Affirmers cultivate a high-performing, inclusive organization. We focus on three core areas: attracting talent aligned to our mission, enabling growth through people and team development, and retaining employees through thoughtful experiences and rewards. We develop Affirm’s people programs and systems to create a workplace where all employees can thrive and contribute meaningfully. By investing in our people, we create a long-term advantage for the business.

About the Role

The Compensation Programs & Partnerships (P&P) team designs, executes, and maintains some of the people programs and partnerships that enables Affirm to provide thoughtful experiences and rewards to Affirmers. We are seeking a detail oriented, collaborative Compensation Analyst who is passionate about delivering compensation programs and partnerships that helps drive Affirm’s success. In this role, you will report to the Senior Manager of Compensation and work closely with the Senior Manager and broader Compensation team to strategize, build, refine, maintain, and implement various programs and initiatives. You will also work closely with the team to help provide partnership and support for the Technology and Business functions as well as other cross functional partner groups.

What You’ll Do

• Lead the end to end project management of the mid-year and annual compensation cycles in close alignment with the Compensation team and other key People team partners including: proactive and ongoing project planning, creating timelines, building training / enablement resources, facilitating project meetings, creating communications, and providing ad-hoc support during the cycles.

• Leverage existing tools and sources (such as Sigma Dashboards, the Radford Global Compensation Database, and Pave) to provide team ad-hoc compensation analyses and story-building support, translating data elements into sound recommendations and insightful presentations. This could include conducting robust research to prepare analyses on actual vs. market pay positioning, leveling distributions vs. market practices, offer and candidate trends, retention risk, spans / layers, or other workforce related priorities.

• Partner with the Compensation Programs & Partnerships team to provide ongoing partnership support for various business related initiatives across Affirm’s Technology and Business functions.

• Partner with the Senior Incentive Compensation Manager to provide operational support for the incentive compensation design process (which can include coordinating kickoff meetings, facilitating focus group feedback sessions with leaders, creating and / or updating incentive plan documents).

• Engage in ongoing processes and special projects to refine and uphold Compensation’s programmatic frameworks.

• Serve as subject matter expert, alongside other compensation team partners, to provide education and consultation to stakeholders on our compensation structure, guidance, and various compensation programs.

• Maintain our standard job architecture catalog in Workday and internal team documents.

• May participate in sessions with external survey companies (such as AON) to stay up to date on market trends and share insights that can help the team maintain competitive rewards structures and programs.

What We Look For

• 5+ years of experience in compensation with the ability to demonstrate an understanding of core compensation concepts and programs.

• Experience with leading and managing projects from start to finish using a standard project management lifecycle approach.

• Strong team orientation with the ability to work effectively and collaboratively across the internal team and cross functional partners.

• Strong relationship management skills with the proven ability to consult, influence, and maintain positive relationships with business stakeholders.

• Passion for working with data elements and compiling analysis to “tell the story” and create solutions. Proficient with Google Sheets and Google Slides.

• Someone who can pay close attention to detail with the ability to multitask across several deliverables at the same time while maintaining a proactive approach to work assignments in a fast paced environment.

• Ability to be flexible and adapt to using different methods by embracing innovation and experimentation.

• Experience working within the technology industry is a plus.

Equity Grade - 4

Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills. Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include equity rewards, monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents.)

All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.

jobs.title: Category Manager Electronics
jobs.description:
About Re:Build

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.

We operate an advanced, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.

The way we operate is as important as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and contribute to the communities where we operate. (link to The Re:Build Way principles)

Who We Are Looking For

We are seeking an experienced Category Manager, Electronics to lead strategic sourcing for electronic and electromechanical components across Re Manufacturing's family of companies. In this role, you will develop sourcing strategies, build supplier partnerships, and help ensure our businesses have reliable access to the components they need to support manufacturing operations and continued growth.

You bring a strong background in strategic sourcing, category management, and supplier negotiations, ideally within electronics or advanced manufacturing. You understand how to balance cost, quality, lead times, and supply chain risk while developing long-term relationships with manufacturers and distributors. You're comfortable navigating complex supplier agreements, analyzing data, and collaborating with engineering, operations, and business leaders to make informed sourcing decisions.

This is an opportunity to take ownership of a critical sourcing category, influence supply chain strategy across multiple businesses, and help shape how Re approaches procurement. You'll also collaborate with our Digital and AI teams to explore how automation and emerging technologies can improve sourcing decisions, supplier performance, and overall efficiency.

What You Get To Do

• Develop and lead the long-term sourcing strategy for electronic and electromechanical components, including wire and cable, connectors, terminals, sensors, printed circuit boards, and batteries.

• Build and lead strategic relationships with component manufacturers and distributors to improve cost, quality, availability, lead times, and supply chain flexibility.

• Lead supplier negotiations and establish long-term agreements covering pricing, delivery commitments, inventory programs, and commercial terms.

• Identify opportunities to reduce costs, improve supply continuity, and mitigate supplier and contractual risks across Re businesses.

• Partner with engineering and operations teams to develop sourcing solutions for specialized components, long-lead materials, and evolving manufacturing requirements.

• Evaluate sourcing strategies involving SKU rationalization, minimum order quantities (MOQs), tooling investments, and non-recurring engineering (NRE) costs.

• Establish and monitor supplier performance metrics, including on-time delivery, material availability, and inventory efficiency, to drive accountability and continuous improvement.

• Collaborate across functions, including Engineering, Operations, Finance, Legal, and Supply Chain, to align sourcing strategies with business priorities.

• Explore AI and automation opportunities in partnership with Re's Digital and AI teams to improve supplier selection, sourcing decisions, and working capital management.

• Provide strategic guidance on electronics sourcing initiatives, helping business leaders make informed decisions that support long-term growth.

What You Bring To The Team

• 7+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, or category management, preferably with electronic or electromechanical components.

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Finance, or a related field.

• Experience developing category strategies, negotiating contracts, and building strong supplier partnerships.

• Knowledge of electronic components, including wire and cable, connectors, printed circuit boards, sensors, or similar products.

• Ability to evaluate supplier performance, manage supply chain risks, and identify cost-saving opportunities.

• Experience with ERP systems, contract management tools, and data-driven decision-making.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across Engineering, Operations, Finance, and Supply Chain teams.

• Ability to balance competing priorities, solve problems, and drive results in a dynamic environment.

• Interest in using AI, automation, and emerging technologies to improve sourcing processes.

• Willingness to travel domestically 10–25% as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience leading electronics categories, including wire harness components, connectors, printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs), or other specialized electromechanical components.

• Experience in regulated manufacturing environments, particularly aerospace, defense, or government contracting.

• Familiarity with FAR/DFARS, ITAR/EAR, and contractual flow-down requirements.

• Master's degree or MBA.

• Professional certifications such as CSCP, CPIM, or CPSM.

The base salary range for this position is $120,000 – $180,000 per year. This range represents the Company’s good faith estimate of the base compensation for this role at the time of posting.  Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to relevant experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for annual incentive compensation and/or long-term incentives, subject to Company plans. The Company offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, and other benefits.

The BIG payoff

We are a company who is going to make a difference in the industries and the communities in which we choose to operate.  Every employee of Re:Build will share ownership in the company and will share in the financial rewards of the success we achieve together, at all levels of the company!

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT US 


QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors.

With VIO, we are paving the way for the hyper-scale quantum computers that will change the world. And delivering on that vision demands people who don’t shy away from tackling the hardest challenges of our time. That’s where you come in! 



Join us as a Technical Program Manager in our new Project Management Office (PMO), reporting to the PMO Lead. You will own day-to-day program management for one to two development programs, keeping schedules, responsibilities and risks visible across development and production departments. Working in a highly technical, fast-moving environment, you will build the habits and practice of program discipline that the whole company will adopt as the PMO scales.



What you'll be doing

 - Ownership and responsibility
   
   - Own top level execution and delivery of assigned programs.
   
   - Partner with project and discipline leads on cross-department programs to ensure execution on schedule and within budget.
   
   - Manage the day-to-day execution of the assigned programs including handoffs across departments.
   
   - Lead the program-management activities for your assigned programs: schedule build, baselining, gate reviews, etc.

 - Manage uncertainty and risk
   
   - Identify risks and bottlenecks early
   
   - Plan for potential failure modes and contingencies
   
   - Escalate risks and blockers to the relevant stakeholders promptly.

 - Support growth and development of the team
   
   - Mentor junior program managers in program execution and collaborative leadership.
   
   - Support the PMO Lead in rolling out common language, product lifecycle, team rhythms for programs.
   
   - Support general program management training across the organization.



Your Profile

 - Leadership experience
   
   - Over 6 years of experience, including more than 4 years managing the delivery of complex, research-intensive chip hardware projects in a program management role.
   
   - Lead programs coordinating across functions and departments.
   
   - Proven ability to work with highly specialised technical experts.
   
   - Experience working in a fast-moving start-up or scale-up environment balancing hands-on technical leadership with growing a team, as a strong plus.

 - Approach
   
   - Learn quickly in a highly technical, low-maturity field, without needing a deep technical background in quantum computing on day one.
   
   - Translate a long-term strategy into an execution plan for your program teams.
   
   - Strong analytical skills with the ability to make pragmatic, informed decisions under uncertainty.
   
   - Bring together world-class technical experts and project leads to execute on highly complex programs.



 - Technical Background
   
   - MSc, PhD, or equivalent experience in physics, electrical engineering, microwave/RF engineering, semiconductor technology, or a related field.
   
   - Understanding of the development lifecycle for chip-level technologies; experience with superconducting qubits or cryogenic systems is a strong plus.

 - Communication
   
   - Excellent communicator who can motivate teams, facilitate alignment, adept at communicating program management ideas to highly technical people.
   
   - Collaborate with stakeholders and colleagues across the organization - Product, Research and Development, Operations, Management team, etc.
   
   - Communicate fluently in English.
   
   

Don't tick every box? Apply anyway! Research shows women often self-select out if they don't meet every requirement. Here's our take: nobody ticks every box. This is a description of our ideal candidate, not a filter. If most resonates and you're keen to learn the gaps, apply. We hire for trajectory, not perfection. 

What We Offer:

At QuantWare, you’ll be part of a high-performing team of world-class experts in an ambitious, fast-moving environment. From day one, you’ll have the trust, tools, and support to do your best work. Here’s what you can expect:

Competitive salary - A salary that reflects the impact and importance of the role (and of course 8% holiday allowance)

Pension that’s built to last - A generous and future-proof pension plan that includes partner and dependent coverage.

Flexibility built on trust - We focus on outcomes. Work flexibly, in a hybrid setup, with an open vacation policy that lets you manage your time

Personal growth - We invest in your L&D, with a budget available to each team member, dependent on their individual ambitions, development needs, and performance

A connected team - We make space to celebrate wins together, with team events, offsites, and spontaneous moments that bring us closer

Diversity & Inclusion at QuantWare

We’re an ambitious company, not only for our goals but also to become an even more diverse and inclusive team. We know great candidates don't always follow a straight path, and we value diverse experience, perspectives, and ways of thinking. We know this helps us make better decisions, drives more innovation, and strengthens our culture.

We believe independent restaurants deserve the same advantages as big chains without giving up their independence.

Ilir Sela started Slice in his family’s pizzerias, where he saw firsthand what it takes to run a local shop. Now we’re taking everything we’ve learned beyond pizza, to taquerias, delis, burger joints, and other neighborhood staples.

We put technology, marketing, buying power, and support to work for more than 15,000 restaurants, so owners spend less time on admin, marketing, and order management and more time growing their business. They remain independent, but never alone.

We’re growing our team to help bring this next chapter to life. That’s where you come in.

The Challenge to Solve

Every new Slice Register starts with a box of hardware that has to arrive on time and ready to go. As one of the first members of our new hardware fulfillment site, you’ll make sure thousands of kits a year are configured, packed, and shipped accurately to independent restaurants across the country.

The Role

Your day will be fast-paced and will include the following tasks:

• Receive, inspect, and put away inbound hardware, logging any damage or discrepancies, and accurately scanning and recording all inventory movements.

• Utilize handheld scanners, laptops, and apps to pick hardware, building materials, and supplies accurately from shelves.

• Pick, pack, and ship orders to meet strict carrier cutoffs (including expedited and drop-ship orders).

• Build and configure register kits and peripherals to exact specifications, including Mobile Device Management (MDM) enrollment and device checks.

• Pack items securely, stage orders for pickup or delivery, load products into vans, and handle high-value items in strict accordance with secure storage procedures.

• Participate in regular cycle counts, resolve count variances with the team

• Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.

The Team

As a member of the Hardware Fulfillment team, you will work with other associates to complete needed tasks, and report to our Bellmawr Hardware Fulfillment Operations Manager.

The Winning Recipe

These are the core competencies this role calls for:

• 1+ years of experience in a warehouse, fulfillment, or inventory environment

• High accuracy and attention to detail, with comfort using barcode scanners and inventory systems

• Basic proficiency with digital inventory tools, handheld scanners, and everyday technology

• Computer proficiency (comfortable operating both MacBooks and Windows PCs)

• Basic technical comfort with device setup and configuration (comprehensive training provided)

• Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, and lift heavy items (frequently 40 to 50+ pounds) throughout a full shift

• Reliable attendance, including flexibility to accommodate expedited orders and Saturday shipping needs

• Prior experience processing point-of-sale (POS) hardware preferred, but not required

jobs.title: IT Systems Administrator (Linux Admin)
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, Seattle, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview:

CHAOS Industries is looking for a Senior IT Systems Administrator with deep Linux expertise to design, build, secure, and operate the Linux infrastructure our engineering and program teams depend on. You will keep servers, services, and cloud workloads reliable, patched, and compliant in a defense environment where uptime and data protection are both non-negotiable. As a senior member of the IT organization, you will act as a technical lead for Linux systems engineering: setting standards, owning the hardest problems, and mentoring teammates, while partnering with cybersecurity, service desk, engineering, and program teams.

• Team mandate: keep the Linux platforms running reliably, securely, and predictably, and automate everything repeatable so the team can spend its time on improvements. You will be the escalation point for complex systems issues and a trusted advisor on infrastructure decisions.

• Ownership: technical ownership of the Linux server environment, including architecture, configuration management, patching, monitoring, backup and recovery, and hardening, plus leadership of infrastructure projects such as platform migrations, new site standups, and environment consolidations as the company grows.

Responsibilities:

• Architect, administer, and maintain Linux server environments (physical, virtual, and cloud), including provisioning, configuration, patching, monitoring, and lifecycle management across Red Hat-family and Debian-family distributions.

• Design and maintain automation and configuration management using Ansible, shell, and Python to standardize builds, enforce configuration, and streamline patching, reporting, and routine administration.

• Build and maintain hardened, standardized server images and templates aligned to security baselines such as DISA STIG and CIS benchmarks, including SELinux, auditd, and FIPS-validated cryptography where required.

• Manage Linux storage and networking, including LVM, file systems, NFS, DNS, firewalls, and system tuning for performance and capacity.

• Integrate Linux systems with enterprise identity services (Active Directory, LDAP, Kerberos, SSSD) and enforce SSH key management, sudo policy, MFA, and privileged access controls.

• Deploy and manage Linux workloads in virtualized and cloud environments, including Azure and AWS virtual machines, and support containerized workloads where applicable.

• Serve as technical lead and final escalation point for complex incidents; perform root-cause analysis and drive permanent fixes.

• Mentor and coach junior systems administrators and service desk staff, and set technical standards, best practices, and peer review for the team.

• Lead infrastructure projects from planning through delivery, including platform migrations, site buildouts, and the integration of newly acquired environments.

• Own backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity design for Linux systems, including regular restore testing and recovery objectives.

• Monitor system health, logs, and performance with centralized monitoring and logging tools; remediate vulnerabilities in partnership with cybersecurity.

• Support compliance requirements (such as CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, and FedRAMP) by maintaining configuration documentation, logs, and access reviews, and providing evidence for audits.

• Review technical designs and changes, follow the change control process, and communicate maintenance windows and impacts to stakeholders.

• Evaluate and recommend tools and technologies, and contribute to the infrastructure roadmap, capacity planning, and budget inputs.

• Create and maintain system documentation, runbooks, and architecture diagrams.

• Participate in an on-call rotation and occasional after-hours maintenance windows for critical systems.

• Travel: minimal, up to roughly 10% (occasional trips to company offices and new sites).

• Physical demands: primarily sedentary work at a computer; occasional lifting of equipment up to 25 lbs and work in server or network rooms.

Minimum Requirements:

• Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or another related field or equivalent work experience

• 3+ years of progressive experience administering enterprise Linux server environments (such as RHEL, Rocky, CentOS, Ubuntu, or Debian).

• Expert command-line and troubleshooting skills, with deep knowledge of systemd, networking, storage (LVM, file systems, NFS), and performance tuning.

• Strong scripting and automation skills in Bash and Python, and experience with configuration management tools such as Ansible.

• Experience hardening Linux systems and remediating vulnerabilities in a regulated environment, including SELinux, auditd, DISA STIG or CIS baselines, and NIST SP 800-171 or CMMC requirements.

• Experience integrating Linux with enterprise identity (Active Directory, LDAP, Kerberos, SSSD) and managing SSH, sudo, and privileged access.

• Experience owning patch management, monitoring, and backup and disaster recovery, including testing restores and meeting recovery objectives.

• Track record of leading infrastructure projects and mentoring other engineers, with strong documentation and communication skills.

• U.S. person status, as required for access to CUI and export-controlled data (ITAR/EAR).

Preferred Requirements:

• Experience running Linux in Azure, AWS, or Azure Government and Microsoft GCC High environments, including hybrid and multi-cloud designs.

• Experience with containers and orchestration (Docker, Podman, or Kubernetes) and with virtualization platforms such as KVM or VMware.

• Linux or cloud certification such as RHCSA, RHCE, LFCS, or Azure or AWS Associate-level; security certification such as Security+ or CISSP.

• Experience with infrastructure as code and CI/CD tooling (Terraform, Git-based workflows, or pipelines).

• Experience supporting CMMC, NIST 800-171, or FedRAMP assessments, and an active U.S. government security clearance or the ability to obtain one.

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $140,000 - $200,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations.

Recruiting Agencies: CHAOS Industries does not accept unsolicited resumes or outreach. Unsolicited submissions will not be reviewed or compensated.

jobs.location: Houston, Texas, United States; Miami, Florida, United States; Reston, Virginia, United States
jobs.description:
ON.energy is setting the standard for large load interconnection. ON’s patented AI UPS™ is a medium-voltage UPS that serves as a firewall, protecting the data center from the grid, and the grid from the data center. With multiple gigawatts currently under construction, we are enabling grid-safe data centers.

Vice President, Product Management
Miami, Florida; Washington, DC; or Remote (U.S.)

ON.energy is building the power infrastructure that makes the AI era possible. As AI demand surges past what the grid and traditional data centers can support, ON.energy provides a new class of power technology proven at gigawatt scale and trusted by the world’s leading cloud and AI companies. Our systems are already deployed across 2.5 GW of hyper-scale campuses, validated by top U.S. national labs, and certified for grid-safe operation by major utilities. With real products in the field, we’re scaling faster than the grid can, transforming power from a bottleneck into a competitive advantage for the companies building the future.

ON.energy is seeking a Vice President of Product Management to lead and own the product roadmap for our medium-voltage UPS systems serving the data center power market. This role is responsible for defining product direction, translating market needs into actionable requirements, and establishing the business case and prioritization framework for what we build next.

Building on ON.energy’s customer-informed product development to date, the VP of Product Management will establish a clear, well-supported roadmap for the next 12–24 months, balancing customer value, competitive differentiation, technical feasibility, regulatory and certification requirements, delivery timing, and financial outcomes. Reporting to the SVP of Engineering and working closely with the CTO and senior leadership, this leader will build and lead a small, focused product management team while staying hands-on in roadmap, requirements, and customer work.

Key Responsibilities

• Product Strategy & Roadmap: Develop and maintain a product roadmap with clear priorities, business cases, milestones, and measurable outcomes, and provide a sound commercial rationale for roadmap decisions.

• Market & Customer Discovery: Engage with customers, channel partners (as applicable), and industry stakeholders to identify emerging requirements and trends in data center power infrastructure.

• Product Requirements & Go-to-Market Inputs: Translate market insights into product requirements, including target pricing, certification and compliance needs, and planned launch timing.

• Technical Direction: Partner with R&D and Engineering to assess technology options and recommend the most effective solutions based on feasibility, risk, and expected customer value.

• Scope & Customization Strategy: Determine when customer-specific features justify investment versus when they should be standardized and incorporated into the broader product offering.

• Commercialization: Partner with Sales on pricing and packaging, and with Marketing on positioning, product narratives, and launch planning.

• Execution Alignment: Provide clear product direction to program management and engineering teams throughout development and delivery, ensuring the released product meets its original intent.

• Team Leadership: Build, lead, and develop a small, high-performing product management team, setting clear expectations and coaching team members while remaining a hands-on contributor.

• Operating Model: Establish a durable product management operating model and repeatable processes that can scale as the business grows.

• External Representation: Serve as a product and strategy representative with customers and at relevant industry events.

First 12–24 Months

• Validate existing assumptions regarding customer demand, market trajectory, competitive landscape, and product differentiation.

• Develop a prioritized roadmap with business cases, target outcomes, and delivery timelines.

• Establish repeatable product management processes that connect customer insight to requirements, investment decisions, and execution alignment.

• Hire and onboard a small product management team aligned to roadmap priorities.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, or a related technical discipline; equivalent experience will be considered.

• 10+ years of product management experience, including at least 5 years in a product leadership role managing people and owning a multi-product roadmap.

• Experience leading small, hands-on product teams, balancing people leadership with individual contribution.

• Significant experience in product management for complex electrical hardware, systems, or mission-critical infrastructure.

• Demonstrated ability to bring technical products to market, including requirements definition, pricing strategy, and launch planning.

• Strong understanding of the data center industry and the buyer/user needs that shape critical power infrastructure decisions.

• Experience in UPS and/or critical power infrastructure (particularly low- or medium-voltage systems) is highly relevant.

• Sufficient technical depth to collaborate effectively with R&D and engineering teams and to assess technical tradeoffs and risks.

• Working knowledge of relevant standards and certification pathways (e.g., UL 1778, IEC 62040, IEEE, NFPA 70/NEC) and their impact on product cost, design, and launch timing.

• Strong commercial judgment regarding demand forecasting, pricing, value proposition, and the economics of customization.

• Track record of using data, including market sizing, win/loss analysis, customer feedback, and field performance, to drive prioritization and investment decisions.

• Experience managing the full product lifecycle, including sustaining engineering, cost reduction, and end-of-life decisions.

• Experience engaging hyperscale, colocation, and enterprise data center operators, as well as EPCs, consulting engineers, and other specifiers who influence purchasing decisions.

• Proven ability to form independent viewpoints and communicate them clearly to customers and executive leadership, including presenting business cases and articulating technical requirements in customer-facing contexts.

• Proficiency with product management and roadmapping tools (e.g., Jira, Aha!, or equivalent) and experience working within a stage-gate or similar development process.

• Experience in a high-growth or venture-backed company, with comfort operating amid ambiguity and limited resources.

• Familiarity with power electronics, energy storage and battery technologies, and utility/grid interconnection considerations is preferred.

• Prior experience building or scaling a product management function is a plus.

• MBA not required; prior product leadership impact is the primary criterion.

Location & Travel

• Preferred locations: Miami, FL or Washington, DC.

• Fully remote candidates will be considered, with preference for U.S.-based candidates.

• Travel: approximately 40–50% for customer meetings, industry events, and onsite collaboration.

• Candidates based outside the U.S. should expect additional travel to Miami and Washington, DC.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, AI Platform (US  - Remote or Calgary)
jobs.description:
Do you want to empower organizations to build smarter compensation strategies while ensuring fair pay for all employees?

Syndio is the leading pay governance and compensation intelligence platform. We help organizations make better pay decisions at every stage of the compensation lifecycle, from leveling and offers to promotions and merit. Our platform gives HR, compensation, and finance leaders the data and decision support they need to govern pay fairly, compliantly, and with confidence. We partner with many of the world’s most recognized and respected enterprises, helping them implement leading-edge compensation solutions with expert guidance and analyzing pay for over 10 million employees across the world.

Join us in our mission to help companies make smarter pay decisions they can trust!

About the Role:

Syndi is Syndio's AI platform — one shared agent experience (in-product chat, Slack, Teams) serving our product lines, built on syndi-api: an agent runtime owning orchestration, tool calling, memory, RAG, evals, and observability, live in production today. The platform is young (v1 shipped this quarter), moving fast, and designed around a clear operating model: product teams contribute domain content through APIs, evals, and knowledge — the platform owns the experience.

We're hiring a staff-level engineer to take ownership of major runtime surfaces and grow into a technical owner of the platform. This is a high-autonomy role on a small team (3–4 engineers): you'll design, ship, and operate systems end-to-end, and you'll work directly with product-team owners through the platform's contribution seams.

What You'll Work On

• Core runtime surfaces of syndi-api: the agent loop, tool execution and registry, memory, context management (Python, Postgres, Claude on Vertex, GCP).

• The eval system — offline gates and online detector/judge evals written onto production traces — and its growth as product teams adopt it.

• Production operation: observability (Datadog LLM Obs), incident response, the reliability of an agent surface real customers use.

• The platform's contribution seams: reviewing product teams' tool wrappers and evals, evolving the GET /tools registry and drift-detection contract.

• Clarifying, designing, and implementing compliance and legal requirements for Syndi.

What We're Looking For

• 5+ years building production backend systems; deep comfort with Python, relational stores, and cloud infra (we're on GCP/Kubernetes).

• You've built LLM-powered systems in production — an agent loop, tool-calling integration, RAG, or eval infrastructure — and have opinions from the scar tissue.

• You design for operability: legal compliance, tracing, evals, and kill switches are part of the feature, not afterthoughts.

• You can own a technical domain with light supervision: propose direction in writing with clear API specs, take review, ship, and carry the pager for what you shipped.

• Strong written communication — our operating model runs on design docs and PR review across team boundaries.

• Nice to have: experience being the platform side of a platform/product relationship; SSE/streaming systems; compliance-adjacent engineering (data minimization, auditability); prior Staff scope.

Why you'll love it here:

• 💰 Competitive Compensation. For this role our salary is targeted at $205-225k USD or $180-200k CAD per year. Final offer amounts are determined by factors such as experience and expertise.

• 🏆 Syndio Equity. So you can share in Syndio’s success

• 🏝 Flexible Vacation Policy. We encourage our team to recharge when they need to (up to 20 days PTO in Canada) plus paid sick & safe time, compassion leave, and voting leave.

• 🩺 Medical, Dental, Vision. Syndio pays 90% of employee premiums, and 50% for dependents.

• 🏥 Life Insurance & Disability. Syndio covers the full premium.

• 📍Remote-first in US + Alberta; in Calgary, non-mandatory office available #LI-Remote

Role Progession

• First 30 days: Focus on onboarding, mastering our core agent runtime surfaces, and shipping a small-scale contribution to understand the platform's contribution seams.

• First 60 days: Independently manage core runtime surfaces, troubleshoot complex issues, and start co-owning a consumer team's integration from API design to eval sign-off.

• First 90 days: Concretely ship a major runtime capability end-to-end (e.g., multimodal input or a new channel surface), take on-call for the platform, and co-own a consumer team's integration from API design to eval sign-off.

The interview overview

Below you'll find an outline of the interview plan for our Staff Software Engineer (AI Platform) position. Please note that this is what we expect the process to look like; we may ask you for supplemental information or require an additional step before making a final decision.

• Recruiter Screen (25 min)

• Meet the Hiring Manager (60 min)

• Technical Discussion (90 min)

• Product Interview (30 min)

• Executive Interview (30 min)

At Syndio, we're building a diverse team that values candor, curiosity, and community. If you share these values and are interested in joining us, we'd love to talk with you even if you don't 100% meet the "about you" listed here. We don't expect anyone to have all the answers, as long as you're willing to learn and grow with us.

Syndio is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are building an inclusive and collaborative workplace as we grow, and we welcome team members regardless of gender/identity, sexual orientation, race or cultural background, religion, physical disability and age.

We're looking for a smart, ambitious and organized student to get exposure to and support business operations in our West Chester office: recruiting engineers, onboarding new hires, keeping the office running, and taking on projects for our partners. Apply through the link with your resume and a 3-5 sentence answer to this question: tell us about something you kept organized that other people depended on. We review applications as they come in and plan to make an offer by November 20. Offers depend on a background check.
