jobs.title: Vice President, Associate General Counsel
jobs.description:
ROLE OVERVIEW

As HealthVerity’s Vice President, Associate General Counsel, you will partner with our EVP & General Counsel to evolve our legal, compliance and contracting functions across the recently combined HealthVerity and Symphony Health businesses. You will become the person our sales, partnerships, real world data, people, contracts and privacy and compliance teams turn to first, trusting the legal expertise, clarity and practical judgment you bring to complex issues. You will join HealthVerity at a particularly exciting moment. You will be the second in-house lawyer with regular interactions across our organization and with our executive leadership team as we work to integrate the HealthVerity and Symphony Health businesses. This role offers the rare opportunity to shape both our legal function and the integration from the ground floor, building the culture, process and structure that will drive the combined organization forward for years to come.

WHAT YOU WILL ACTUALLY DO

• Data Licensing and Commercial Contracts: Draft and negotiate healthcare data and software licenses (inbound and outbound), master services agreements and other commercial agreements

• Privacy: Advise on federal and state laws governing the collection, de-identification, licensing and use of U.S. healthcare and consumer data – and help our commercial teams understand what it all means for our products, services and operations

• Compliance: Maintain and strengthen our compliance program – think policies, training, risk assessments and audit responses

• Contracting Workflow: Support our contracts team to improve how we get deals done across contracting processes, escalation paths, template governance, playbook strategy and AI-enabled workflows

• Commercial Partnerships: Shape how our commercial teams understand and value legal and compliance, partnering with internal and external stakeholders to drive win-win outcomes and build long-standing commercial relationships

• Culture and Mentorship: Mentor and develop team members as our legal, compliance and contracting functions collaborate to build a culture where people do their best work

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

• J.D. with active bar admission in at least one U.S. jurisdiction

• 7+ years of combined law firm and in-house experience (healthcare information/technology background a plus)

• Familiarity with how life sciences and healthcare organizations use de-identified data (you don’t need to be an expert on day one)

• Experience drafting and negotiating software and data licensing agreements

• Comfort navigating privacy laws and de-identification standards

• Familiarity with contract lifecycle management (CLM) tools across legal, sales ops and finance (prior CLM implementation experience a plus)

• Experience integrating acquired businesses

• Familiarity with AI-enabled legal tools and workflows

• Ability to manage cross-functional demands in a fast-paced environment with collaboration and respect

• Strong written and verbal communication skills to make complex legal issues understandable to non-lawyers while balancing commercial objectives

• A team-first attitude with humility, empathy and humor

Base salary for the role is commensurate with experience and can range between $265,000 - 325,000 plus annual bonus and equity participation.

Hiring Locations

Our main office is located in Center City, Philadelphia, where we operate on a hybrid model with in-office work required three days a week for local employees. We believe collaboration is most effective when teams come together, which is why we prioritize hiring in the Philadelphia area.

For certain roles, we also hire from hub locations—regions where we have an established presence with multiple team members working remotely. jobs.title: Founding Community and Events Lead
jobs.description:
FOUNDING COMMUNITY AND EVENTS LEAD




WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS



Jack & Jill is changing how companies hire. We’re ~25 people headquartered in London and building fast. We just raised $40M Series A, led by Air Street Capital with participation from Creandum and Madrona. Read more here https://www.jackandjill.ai/blog/series-a

 

We launched in San Francisco earlier this year and now we need someone to make the Bay Area’s startup world stop and pay attention.


This is a role for a true superconnector: someone who can throw a room-stopping event and turn it into content that reaches ten times the people who showed up. Every event is two things at once: a real-life moment and a content asset.

You run it, you capture it, you amplify it. That’s the loop, and you own it end to end.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN



You’ll design and execute high-impact events (career fairs, founder dinners, meetups, and new formats nobody’s tried yet and we haven’t thought of) that put Jack & Jill in front of the people we most want to reach. 

Then take each event and make it travel: recaps, clips, photos, and posts across LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram, and X that grow our audience and pull the next crowd through the door.



Events without amplification waste the moment. Social without real events behind it rings hollow. You’ll do both, and you’ll build the playbook as you go.




WHAT YOU’LL DO



 - Own events end to end (concept, logistics, guest lists, day-of execution, follow-up) at real volume.

 - Turn every event into social content that extends its reach far beyond the room, and grow a following around it.

 - Activate your SF network from day one and keep widening it: founders, VCs, and operators who show up because your event is the one to be at.

 - Connect the dots from events and content to awareness and pipeline, and measure what’s actually working.

 - Operate independently in a distributed team (we’re 8 hours ahead in London), you’ll report to our GTM Lead, Kaoru and work closely with the SF GTM team.




YOU’LL THRIVE HERE IF YOU



 - Have run event series at high volume and amplified them on socials with real, measurable reach. You’ve lived both halves of the loop.

 - Come from an events, community, or content role at a startup, fintech, or VC-adjacent company, ideally right here in SF.

 - Are a recognised connector in the SF ecosystem: people seek you out for intros and access, and they discover you through your content.

 - Have built something from zero (a community, a meet-up, an event series, a social following) as a hands-on doer, not from a management seat.

 - Can see the line from a great dinner to a warm pipeline, and you’re comfortable being measured on it.

 - Love the scrappy, high-ownership, 0-to-1 reality of an early-stage startup and want equity upside to match.




BONUS POINTS



 - You’ve run events or communities at a VC fund or accelerator and amplified founder dinners, demo days, or portfolio moments on social media.

 - You were the first community/events/partnerships hire somewhere and built the function from scratch.

 - You’ve tied community work to sign-ups, acquisition, or partnerships with numbers to show for it.

 - You’re genuinely excited about AI and the future of hiring.




THE DETAILS



 - Type: Individual contributor. You do the hands-on work yourself, not through a team.

 - Location: San Francisco, hybrid / in-office. This is an SF role and your network needs to be SF-real.

 - Compensation: $100–160k base plus meaningful equity.

 - Work authorization: US right to work strongly preferred. Visa sponsorship is possible in exceptional cases but will slow the process.

Fourmile Veterinary Clinic is hiring a full-time Vet Assistant to work alongside our team of experienced veterinarians, skilled technicians, and devoted support staff to ensure each animal receives the best possible care during their stay with us. We also offer large/farm animal care and pulmonary arterial pressure (PAP) testing.

jobs.title: Human Resources Generalist
jobs.description:
Voyager is an innovative space, defense, and national security technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart.

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

Position Description

Voyager Technologies is seeking a practical and solutions-oriented Human Resources Generalist to deliver broad HR support for an assigned site, function, or employee population. The Generalist independently handles recurring employee relations, manager guidance, HR operations, and program delivery while partnering with the HRBP on complex, high-risk, or strategic matters. This role requires strong execution, growing business judgment, and the ability to translate policy and People programs into a consistent employee and manager experience.

This role will be hybrid in Reno, NV with some travel to other sites as needed.

Reporting Structure & Location

This role reports to an HR Business Partner supporting our Lines of Business and sits within the People department. The position may support multiple sites and partners closely with People Centers of Excellence.  Must be able to travel between multiple sites, as needed.

What You'll Do

Employee Relations & Manager Support

• Provide day-to-day HR guidance to employees and managers on policies, performance expectations, attendance, workplace concerns, and employee lifecycle matters.

• Conduct or support routine employee relations reviews, including fact gathering, documentation, and recommended next steps; escalate complex, high-risk, or precedent-setting matters to the HRBP or senior HR leadership.

• Coach managers on clear communication, documentation, and consistent application of company expectations.

• Support the administration and coordination of leaves of absence, reasonable accommodation requests, interactive process requirements, workers compensation matters, and compliance processes in partnership with HR Leadership and the Centers of Excellence.

• Respond promptly and accurately to employee questions on HR policies, benefits, pay, leave and procedures, and escalate or follow up on complex issues until resolved.

Talent & Performance

• Support workforce planning, recruiting, onboarding, performance management, talent reviews, engagement, retention, and employee development for assigned groups.

• Partner with managers to improve role clarity, team effectiveness, and execution of People programs.

• Identify recurring capability or employee experience themes and recommend practical actions.

HR Operations, Data & Compliance

• Manage employee lifecycle transactions and ensure HR data, documentation, and records are accurate, timely, and audit-ready.

• Interpret and apply company policies and established HR practices consistently; identify issues requiring policy clarification or legal review.

• Own the payroll process, including input review, processing, and issue resolution, while supporting benefits administration in partnership with the appropriate Centers of Excellence.

• Generate and analyze workforce reports to identify trends, data issues, and operational priorities.

Programs & Change Support

• Lead or coordinate site and business-unit delivery of People programs, including annual HR cycles, employee communications, training, and change activities.

• Partner with HRBPs and Centers of Excellence to translate enterprise programs into practical local execution.

• Develop tools, templates, standard work, and process improvements that strengthen consistency and employee experience.

HR Team Partnership

• Provide day-to-day guidance and quality review for HR Coordinators; may lead defined projects or workstreams.

• Build productive relationships with employees, managers, site leaders, and cross-functional partners.

• Maintain appropriate escalation paths while taking ownership of issues within the role’s scope.

Qualifications

Required

• Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, a related field, or equivalent work experience.

• 4+ years of progressive HR experience with meaningful exposure to employee relations, manager support, HR operations, and employee lifecycle processes.

• Working knowledge of federal employment law and applicable state employment requirements; ability to recognize when escalation is needed.

• Experience supporting employees and managers in California, including familiarity with California employment law and HR compliance requirements.

• Experience using an HRIS such as Workday, ADP, or a similar platform.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including the ability to organize data, use common formulas, identify discrepancies, and prepare clear reports.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, and professional discretion.

• Ability to balance employee experience, business needs, policy consistency, and compliance.

Preferred

• PHRca or SHRM-CP certification.

• Experience supporting a technical, engineering, manufacturing, or multi-site workforce.

• Experience in government contracting, defense, aerospace, or national security.

• Familiarity with DCAA, OFCCP, ITAR/EAR, Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulations Supplement (DFARS) or other regulated-environment requirements.

• Experience supporting change management, investigations, performance management, or workforce reporting.

The good faith base salary range for this role is $85,000-$100,000 at the time of this posting. Where you fall within the range depends on your experience, skills, and location. This range reflects base salary only and does not include benefits or bonus/incentive. This range may be adjusted in the future.

Voyager offers a highly competitive total compensation package designed to support the well-being, growth, and success of our employees. Employees benefit from a flexible and comprehensive rewards program that supports both professional and personal well-being.

• Flexible Time Off (FTO), empowering employees to take the time they need to recharge and maintain a healthy work-life balance

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their families, with a significant portion of premiums covered by the company and many benefits paid at 100% for employees

• Flexible, affordable gym memberships with 12,700+ options nationwide, including 24 Hour Fitness, EoS Fitness, Crunch Fitness, Anytime Fitness, Blink Fitness, Chuze Fitness, and more! No long-term contracts and FREE on-demand workout videos before you enroll

• 401(k) retirement plan with a 50% company match on contributions up to 8%, supporting long-term financial security

• Company wellness programs that support physical and mental well-being

jobs.title: Co-Op, Bayesian Methods for Complex Decision Making
jobs.location: Cambridge, MA USA; San Francisco, CA USA
jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences builds AI systems that accelerate discovery across the physical and life sciences. Within Physical Sciences AI, we work with experimental teams to build autonomous discovery agents that decide which experiments Lila's AI Science Factories should run next.

Real scientific campaigns rarely look like textbook optimization problems. A single campaign can mix large discrete choices (which components, which recipe) with continuous settings (amounts, temperatures, times), pursue several objectives under hard constraints, and draw on evidence from literature and characterization data. Every experiment costs real time and materials. Off-the-shelf methods often struggle here, and they ignore the domain structure that could guide the search.

As a Bayesian Methods Co-Op, you will work alongside research scientists and engineers on a focused project within one broad question: how AI systems can make better experimental decisions. Depending on your background, that could mean building agents that choose the next experiment, testing when in-context learners can be trusted as decision-makers, or developing Bayesian strategies for tight experimental budgets. Your methods will be tested against live campaigns.

What You'll Be Building

• Design and benchmark experiment-selection strategies that balance exploration and exploitation under realistic budgets

• Build autonomous discovery agents that propose the next experiment from surrogate models

• Develop in-context learning approaches inspired by Bayesian inference, evaluating calibration and robustness

• Run retrospective and live evaluations on active campaign data with clear baselines and metrics

• Present findings to ML and experimental teams, with the option to contribute to a publication

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Pursuing a Master's or PhD in statistics, ML, CS, operations research, applied math, or a quantitative science

• Solid grounding in Bayesian inference and decision making, including priors and posterior predictive distributions

• Research experience in Gaussian processes, Bayesian optimization, bandits, reinforcement learning, or probabilistic modeling

• Strong Python skills with PyTorch and probabilistic libraries such as Pyro, PyMC, or BoTorch

• Comfort working with small, noisy, and heterogeneous datasets

• Clear communication with both ML and experimental collaborators

Bonus Points For

• Applying these methods to real problems in materials science, chemistry, or another physical science

• Familiarity with in-context learning as implicit Bayesian inference, meta-learning, or prior-data fitted networks

• Optimization over categorical or combinatorial spaces, including mixed-variable, multi-objective, or batch settings

• Reinforcement learning for sequential decision making or Bayesian experimental design

• Training models on multimodal scientific data such as text, images, spectra, or simulations

About LILA

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai.

Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Co-Op, SCADA Engineer
jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila's SCADA system spans cloud and on-premise infrastructure: Ignition gateways on EC2, a historian on RDS PostgreSQL, MQTT brokers, and edge nodes at each site. Today no single view shows the health of all of it, so the team learns about failures from users rather than from monitoring.

As a co-op on the Hardware & Controls Engineering team, you will build that view: a live connectivity diagram showing how every piece connects and which links are up, backed by dashboards covering database, gateway, and edge node health. The work is read-only end to end, with read-only AWS access and SELECT-only database access, so you can explore the full system safely.

You will be based at our Alewife site in Cambridge, working alongside controls engineers and the IT/OT team. Expect wide exposure across AWS, Linux, industrial networking, Ignition, and data visualization, and a clear picture of how an industrial SCADA system fits together end to end.

• Build a live topology view of edge nodes, brokers, gateways, and databases with per-link status and last-seen timestamps

• Monitor on-premise edge nodes for reachability, uptime, resource use, and last publish time

jobs.description:
About CoLab

At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.

We build AI for engineers designing cars, medical devices, and jet engines. Products this complex aren't sketched and sent to production. Teams spend months on iterations, reviews, and tests, predicting how every part performs before anything is built. CoLab is where those reviews happen, and we capture the rationale behind every change. Other tools show what changed between versions. Only CoLab knows why. That's how our AI helps manufacturers like Bobcat, Triumph Motorcycles, and GE Appliances make better decisions, eliminate rework cycles, and get to market faster.

Proudly based in St. John’s, Newfoundland, CoLab started with one customer in 2018. Since then we’ve raised a $72M Series C, been named the 57th fastest growing company in North America by Deloitte (Fast 500™), signed multi-year AI partnerships with companies like Bombardier, and grown to a team of 250+.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Software Forward Deployed Engineer to embed within our strategic customers and deliver on high-impact, technically complex customer projects. This includes scoping, building, and deploying complex integrations, product features and AI product features that connect customer systems to CoLab, accelerate adoption and increase customer return on investment.

You’ll own delivery of key customer initiatives, working closely with our customer success, product, design and engineering teams, as well as leadership team stakeholders to remove blockers and deliver results.

Unlike a traditional software development role, FDEs must manage significant ambiguity, external team dynamics, and timeline pressure. If you like working directly with customers and shipping code to solve real, complex user problems with a high level agency and autonomy, then you will thrive in this role.

What You’ll Do

• Own delivery of strategic customer projects, from technical discovery through to production deployment and success measures

• Build and deploy complex system integrations, backend services, and data pipelines

• Interface with enterprise systems, including data lakes, identity management and access controls solutions, and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solutions

• Stand up CoLab integrations and organize incoming data to enable use in features like AutoReview and Operator

• Collaborate directly with customers to understand needs, propose solutions, and guide adoption

• Develop targeted solutions that meet the specific Customer's requirements whilst ensuring solutions are designed and developed with our broader customer base in mind.

• Bring your extensive knowledge of our Customer's requirements back to the development team for learning.

Our Ideal Candidate

• You're based in Cincinnati and are comfortable working on site with our customers

• You’ve delivered complex technical solutions for projects where requirements were not clearly defined

• You write clean, production-grade code in a variety of languages and consider yourself language agnostic

• You’re comfortable working in unfamiliar environments - both technically and organizationally

• You’ve worked with enterprise systems (e.g., data lakes, IdP, PLM, ERP, etc)

• You can break down ambiguity, sequence work, and adjust scope without losing momentum

• You’re confident leading deeply technical conversations with customer engineering or IT teams

• You care about delivering outcomes, not just writing code

• You have a “go figure it out” mindset and can roll with the punches when things shift

Bonus Experience

• Prior work embedding within customer environments as part of enterprise SaaS deployments

• Experience building or integrating AI-powered features

• Familiarity with manufacturing or engineering data, processes, or systems

• Experience with API-first products or developer platforms

You set the standard for how 3D strategy works at GMR.

Why GMR? Because we're not here to do what's already been done. We're inventors. Curators of the future. At this level, your 3D vision shapes entire campaign strategies. You're a creative partner—not just a renderer. You'll collaborate with Design Directors, Creative Directors, and production specialists as an equal, pushing what's possible in spatial design.

A portfolio or work samples are required to be considered for the role.

REQUIRED SKILLS

• Lead the spatial vision. You’ll lead 3D design for major projects, transforming briefs into compelling spatial narratives that move from concept to built reality. You’ll develop spatial systems, architectural concepts, and material palettes that can flex across environments, campaigns, and multiple brand touchpoints.

• Make the vision feel real. You’ll create photorealistic renderings that capture the full experience, including lighting, materials, human scale, atmosphere, and brand narrative. Your work doesn’t simply visualize an idea; it makes people believe in it.

• Shape the creative direction. You’ll partner with Creative Directors and Design Directors to translate ideas into space, challenge assumptions, and push concepts into new territory. You understand that spatial design is more than aesthetics. It shapes how people move, interact, experience, and remember a brand.

• Take ideas all the way to reality. You’ll move ambitious concepts into production through technical development, production documentation, fabrication, and installation. You understand what happens when a design leaves the screen and enters the physical world, and you know how to design for that moment. A deep understanding of materials, fabrication methods, environmental design, and real-world performance is essential.

• Build cohesive experiences. You’ll collaborate with 2D and Motion Designers to connect spatial design to the larger visual system, creating brand experiences that feel considered and cohesive from every angle.

• Present with confidence. You’ll lead complex client presentations, communicate spatial concepts clearly, and make a compelling case for your creative decisions. You know how to bring people into the vision and take them along for the ride.

• Master your tools and keep exploring. You bring expert level proficiency in Cinema 4D, SketchUp, AutoCAD, and/or Rhino, along with experience using rendering plugins and AI enabled workflows. You also have strong command of Adobe Creative Suite, including Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, and Acrobat. You’re curious about emerging technology and know how to use new tools to make the work smarter, faster, and more ambitious.

• Own complex projects. You have extensive professional 3D design experience in an agency, experiential, architectural, or related environment. You’ve managed projects from concept through fabrication and understand how to balance creative ambition with timelines, technical realities, and other real-world constraints.

• Bring a point of view. You have strong spatial instincts, strategic thinking, and a portfolio that demonstrates conceptual depth, diverse project experience, and exceptional craft. Most importantly, your portfolio shows work that has actually been built.

Why This Role Will Define Your Career: You're moving from practitioner to strategist. Your spatial vision will anchor campaigns. You'll partner with top Creative Directors on culture-shifting work. You'll build a body of work—both digital and built—that defines what experiential design can be.

The annual range for this role varies between $68,000- $80,000 and may vary depending on the candidate’s experience. You are also eligible to participate in disability, life insurance, FSA/HSA plans subject to the terms and conditions of such benefit plans.

jobs.title: SaaSOps Engineer ($80,000/year USD), @CXT Software
jobs.description:
Are you a cloud engineer who runs production SaaS on Azure and AWS and owns it end-to-end, from the Terraform code to the RCA?
CXT Software provides the technology backbone for delivery processes, empowering courier, route delivery, and healthcare companies to maximize operational potential. Our customers run their daily delivery operations on our platform, so uptime is what they buy from us.
We are looking for a SaaSOps Engineer to own a production SaaS platform across several product lines and two clouds, Azure first and AWS second. You will write the infrastructure code, build the pipelines, run the Windows and SQL Server estate, own the alerts, and lead the response when something breaks, from provisioning a customer environment to writing the RCA after an incident. You will work daily with Engineering, Support, and Security, in Terraform, GitHub Actions, Grafana Cloud, Azure Monitor, Application Insights, CloudWatch, incident.io, Jira, and Confluence. Reporting to the Director of SaaSOps, you will shape how the platform is built, changed, and monitored.
If you want whole-platform ownership, hold a high bar on every change, and are ready to carry on-call for the systems you run, we would love to hear from you.
 
 
Responsibilities
*Build and change Azure and AWS infrastructure in Terraform.
*Build and maintain GitHub Actions pipelines for application and infrastructure deployments.
*Provision, upgrade, and tear down customer environments.
*Operate Windows Server (Remote Desktop Services, IIS, Active Directory, Group Policy) and SQL Server / Azure SQL: patching, backups, restores, and performance.
*Automate repeat operational work in PowerShell.
*Carry on-call: keep alerts paging on customer impact, respond to incidents, fix the cause, and write the RCA.
*Enforce least-privilege access, collect SOC 2 evidence, and keep runbooks current.
 
Requirements
*5+ years as a cloud engineer running production workloads (compute, managed databases, identity, networking) on Azure or AWS.
*You have deployed and changed production infrastructure with Terraform through CI/CD pipelines you built or maintained.
*You write PowerShell automation used in production.
*You have run SQL Server or Azure SQL in production: backups, restores, and performance troubleshooting.
*You have carried production on-call and taken incidents from evidence to a single root cause and a written RCA a teammate can act on without follow-up questions.
*You work 08:00–17:00 ET, Monday to Friday, and join the after-hours on-call rotation.
*Professional English at C1 level or above, spoken and written.
*You can be engaged as an independent contractor and can start within one month of an offer and no later than December 31, 2026.
 
Nice to have
*Production experience on Azure.
*Windows Server administration in production (Remote Desktop Services, IIS, Active Directory, Group Policy).
*AZ-104, AZ-305 or AZ-400, or AWS Solutions Architect Associate or SysOps Administrator Associate.
*Experience preparing SOC 2 audit evidence.
*Uses AI-assisted coding and operations tools at work.
 
Benefits
More than just perks, they're the essential components of a rewarding career at CXT Software.
*100% Remote and Global: Enjoy the freedom to live your best life from anywhere in the world.
*Flexible Work Environment: Work at times that suit you best. We prioritize results and customer satisfaction over rigid schedules.
*Dedicated Growth Path: Receive consistent, meaningful feedback and support tailored to help you achieve your personal career goals.
*Access to Leading Tools and Technology: Enhance your skills with the latest tools, playbooks, and technology.
*Engaging Community Activities: Participate in coffee chats, happy hours, cooking classes, book clubs, and more!

Customer Success Engineer, Scandit USA

Imagine the what. Build the how.

Scandit gives people superpowers. Whether enabling delivery drivers to make quicker deliveries, matching a patient with their medication, or allowing retailers to make store operations more efficient, our technology automates workflows and provides actionable insights to businesses in a variety of industries.

Your opportunity

We're seeking a Customer Success Engineer to join our US team and support a portfolio of key enterprise accounts.

This is a more technical Customer Success role than most.

You’ll be the technical partner customers’ engineers rely on: building demos, sharing code to unblock integrations and guiding implementation, while owning adoption, renewal and growth. This is not an account management or sales role.

Travel and location setup

Travel: c.20% on average, sometimes at short notice, usually 1 to 3 day trips to customer sites and Scandit events.

Timezone requirements: Central or Eastern time zone. You'll work US business hours, with overlap with our European colleagues in the morning.

Working arrangements: If you are near Boston, you can work from our office 2 to 3 days a week; alternatively, this position can be done remotely if you are not near our Boston office.

What you'll do

• Own a portfolio of key US enterprise accounts and drive adoption, retention, and growth

• Become a deep expert in Scandit's products and SDKs, and guide customers through technical decisions

• Lead discovery conversations and translate customer needs into feasible Scandit solutions

• Build tailored demos and share code snippets and small integrations to unblock customers

• Run workshops, adoption reviews, and QBRs with technical and business stakeholders

• Spot at-risk accounts early and expansion opportunities, and partner with Sales to act on them

• Be the voice of the customer inside Scandit, working with Product, Engineering, and Support

• Use AI tooling (Claude Code, etc.) to speed up customer-facing technical work

Must have

• 2+ years in a customer-facing technical pre-sales, post-sales or support role at a B2B software company e.g. Customer Success Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Technical Account Manager, etc.

• A solid technical foundation and coding experience in any language: you have written or debugged code, scripts or integrations, ideally using SDKs or APIs

• Strong written and verbal communication, and you can present to both business and technical audiences and explain a technical problem clearly and concisely

• Strong strategic thinking and analytical skills

• A solid understanding of enterprise IT architectures

• You build strong relationships with customers and colleagues, and you are likeable, humble and fun to work with

• You learn quickly and act on feedback and coaching

Nice to have

• Strong discovery skills: translating customer requirements into feasible technical solutions

• A track record running workshops, adoption reviews or QBRs

• Experience working with Product, Engineering, Sales and Marketing

• Background as a software engineer, mobile developer, solutions engineer or solutions consultant

• Mobile development experience (iOS, Android, React Native or Flutter)

• Industry experience in retail, transport and logistics, computer vision, or mobile data capture

• Salesforce and a CS platform such as Planhat (what we use) or Gainsight

• Comfort using AI development tools such as Claude Code

How we hire

• A 30 to 45 minute call with our Talent Acquisition Manager

• A 30 to 45 minute conversation with the hiring manager

• A 1-hour technical interview with a member of the team (no preparation needed)

• A 1-hour panel presentation of a case study, sent at least 5 days before

Why Scandit

• Certified "Great Place to Work" in 7 countries

• Smart, people-first culture

• Flexible office, hybrid, or home working

• Individual equity plan in a high-growth company

• Learning and development opportunities

• Offices in Zurich, London, Tampere, Warsaw, Boston, and Tokyo

jobs.title: Lending Completions Officer
jobs.description:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Role Description

This is a key role in delivering a fast, accurate and well-controlled lending journey. You will manage a portfolio of cases from offer and post-sanction administration through to drawdown and completion, making sure every case is progressed efficiently and every condition is properly satisfied.

Commercial mortgages will be a core part of the role, alongside other commercial lending products such as GGS loans, overdrafts, business loans, asset finance, non-property-backed lending and unsecured lending. You will work closely with Relationship Managers, Underwriting, legal and valuation partners and other teams across the bank.



Principal Accountabilities

 - Manage a pipeline of lending cases from offer to completion, meeting service levels, quality standards and expected completion timelines.

 - Deliver post-sanction administration, including releasing communications, instructing legal and valuation partners and coordinating payments.

 - Review and satisfy Conditions Precedent and other completion requirements, escalating risks, gaps and delays early.

 - Coordinate drawdown and completion activity accurately, ensuring the right approvals, documentation and controls are in place.

 - Build effective working relationships with Relationship Managers, Underwriting, solicitors, valuers and other internal and external stakeholders.

 - Maintain clear, accurate and audit-ready case records, including sanction audit trails, customer records and updates to the core banking system.

 - Communicate relevant information clearly so that colleagues and decision-makers understand the position, risks and actions required.

 - Work in line with bank policies, procedures, regulatory requirements, Conduct and Treating Customers Fairly expectations.

 - Support wider lending and Operations activity, including cross-skilling, issue resolution, quality improvements and change initiatives.
   
   

Personal Attributes & Experience

 - Experience in lending, credit operations, mortgage completions, loan administration or a similar financial services environment.

 - A practical understanding of the commercial lending journey and pipeline management, ideally including commercial mortgages.

 - Strong attention to detail and the ability to analyse information, identify issues and make sound, timely decisions.

 - A customer-focused approach and a track record of delivering a high standard of service in a fast-paced environment.

 - Good financial and commercial awareness, with an understanding of the importance of risk, controls and accurate record keeping.

 - Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to build relationships and have constructive conversations.

 - Strong organisation and IT skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and maintain momentum across a live pipeline.

Working at Allica Bank

At Allica Bank we want to ensure our employees have the right tools and environment in which to succeed in their role and in support of our customers.

Our employees are at the heart of everything we do, so our benefits are designed with you in mind:

 - Full onboarding support and continued development opportunities

 - Options for flexible working

 - Regular social activities

 - Pension contributions

 - Discretionary bonus scheme

 - Private health cover

 - Life assurance

 - Family friendly policies including enhanced Maternity & Paternity leave



Don’t tick every box?

Don’t worry if you don’t have all the skills or requirements listed on the job description. If you think you’ll be a good fit, we’d still love to hear from you!

Flexible working

We know the ‘9-to-5’ isn’t right for everyone. That’s why Allica Bank is fully committed to flexible and hybrid working. Please let us know what is best for you and, if we can, we will do our best to accommodate.

Diversity

We’re a diverse bunch here at Allica, with all kinds of experiences, backgrounds and lifestyles. Our openness and differences make us stronger, and we want everybody to feel comfortable bringing as much of themselves to work with them as they like.

jobs.title: Mechanical Forward Deployed Engineer - Cincinnati
jobs.description:
About CoLab

At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.

We build AI for engineers designing cars, medical devices, and jet engines. Products this complex aren't sketched and sent to production. Teams spend months on iterations, reviews, and tests, predicting how every part performs before anything is built. CoLab is where those reviews happen, and we capture the rationale behind every change. Other tools show what changed between versions. Only CoLab knows why. That's how our AI helps manufacturers like Bobcat, Triumph Motorcycles, and GE Appliances make better decisions, eliminate rework cycles, and get to market faster.

Proudly based in St. John’s, Newfoundland, CoLab started with one customer in 2018. Since then we’ve raised a $72M Series C, been named the 57th fastest growing company in North America by Deloitte (Fast 500™), signed multi-year AI partnerships with companies like Bombardier, and grown to a team of 250+.

About the Role

This is a high-impact role that helps define how CoLab delivers technical value to its most strategic customers in Aerospace and Defence. CoLab is a category-creating product, which means adoption isn't just a rollout. It's a change in how the organization works.

In this role, you'd act as a trusted advisor, leveraging people, process, and technology to help teams rethink how they manage feedback, data, and decision-making across design and PLM. That means getting deep into customer workflows, testing new ways of working, and building repeatable methods the rest of the team can scale.

You'll work alongside a Customer Success Manager, and use what you learn on the front line to help shape product direction. This role isn't about selling or pitching. It's about deeply understanding engineering problems and solving them alongside the customer.

We are looking for a candidate in Cincinatti to work regularly on-site with a local CoLab customer.

Our Ideal Candidate

You’re a mechanical engineer by trade and have worked as a designer in an A&D company. You also understand the full product development life cycle: how design, manufacturing, quality, and engineering leadership depend on each other, and where collaboration breaks down. You can coach those teams toward working together better.

You know how to improve that life cycle with technology. Maybe you’ve championed internal tools or created automation or scripts.

You also know a process that makes sense on paper won’t get adopted on its own. You can meet people where they are, including the stakeholders who don’t want to change.

You don’t need to be the loudest voice in the room, but you can run a sprint and lead a cross-functional project. If the average person might find this job too undefined or complex, that probably excites you.

Job Responsibilities

• Mapping a customer's current-state design review and engineering workflows, and defining the target-state process their teams will actually adopt.

• Deploying and tuning CoLab's AI capabilities against a customer's own standards, drawing checklists, and design guidelines, and diagnosing what's working and what isn't.

• Providing mechanical engineering expertise to validate AI-generated results and ensure engineering rigor.

• Investigating and solving complex engineering data and integration challenges across PLM, ERP, QMS, and traditional design feedback tools.

• Expanding adoption into new teams, programs, and sites within the account, partnering with the Customer Success Manager on where the next opportunity sits.

• Collaborating with product teams to identify feature gaps, improve capabilities, and refine AutoReview.

Qualifications

Must-haves:

• Background in mechanical design engineering, ideally in a medium- to large-sized organization.

• Strong understanding of PLM & ERP systems and enterprise engineering data architecture.

• Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects and cross-functional collaborations.

• Experience working directly with customers or internal stakeholders to solve technical problems.

• Comfort working in fast-changing, ambiguous environments.

• Strong written communication and documentation skills.

• Working knowledge of high-level AI architecture, specifically LLMs.

• Familiarity with APIs, data integrations, and enterprise architecture concepts.

Nice-to-haves:

• Experience with internal tool development, scripting, or automation.

• Exposure to AI/ML tools applied to engineering workflows.

• Prior work in design consulting or product development at scale.

Travel Expectations

While this is a fully remote role, travel is a consistent part of the job. There are two primary types of travel you can expect:

• Team Weeks: Once per quarter, the sales team or entire company gets together in person. These typically involve traveling out on a Monday and returning on a Thursday or Friday. Two of these each year are held at our headquarters in St. John's, Newfoundland, and the others take place in more central locations that evolve as the team grows.

• On-sites: This role will work closely with a local customer with expectations to be on site with that customer, so there will likely be far less travel than our typical MFDE roll. That being said, in the event the local customer were to no longer work with us, the following is our standard MFDE travel expectations: “For most of our large deployment customers, we will visit on-site during kick-off and key expansion opportunities. Most on-sites involve 2-3 days with the customer, with travel on either side. Travel is primarily within North America, and you can expect 4 customer on-sites per quarter.”

Extra Details

• This is a full-time, permanent position with a competitive compensation package that includes stock options.

• Unlimited paid vacation, extended health benefits, and 401k matching.

Equity Note

Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic and apply even if you don't meet every single qualification. Your potential is what matters most to us.

Your personal data will be processed for the purposes of managing Controller’s recruitment related activities, which include setting up and conducting interviews and tests for applicants, evaluating and assessing the results thereto, and as is otherwise needed in the recruitment and hiring processes. Such processing is legally permissible under Art. 6(1)(f) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation) as necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the Controller, which are the solicitation, evaluation, and selection of applicants for employment.

Your personal data has been shared with Greenhouse Software, Inc., a cloud services provider located in the United States of America and engaged by Controller to help manage its recruitment and hiring process on Controller’s behalf. Accordingly, if you are located outside of the United States, your personal data has been transferred to the United States. Because the European Union Commission has determined that United States data privacy laws do not ensure an adequate level of protection for personal data collected from EU data subjects, the transfer was subject to appropriate additional safeguards under [either the standard contractual clauses or the Privacy Shield]. You can obtain a copy of the standard contractual clauses by contacting us at careers@cortland.com

Your personal data will be retained by Controller as long as Controller determines it is necessary to evaluate your application for employment. Under the GDPR, you have the right to request access to your personal data, to request that your personal data be rectified or erased, and to request that processing of your personal data be restricted. You also have to right to data portability. In addition, you may lodge a complaint with an EU supervisory authority.

jobs.title: Behavior Technician
jobs.description:
We are looking for enthusiastic individuals to join our team as Behavior Technicians. As a Behavior Technician, you will have the opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of children with autism.

In this role, you will work one-on-one with children, implementing individualized behavior intervention plans under the guidance of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). You will use evidence-based techniques to teach communication, social, and daily living skills while reducing interfering behaviors.

We are looking for candidates who are passionate about helping children with autism reach their full potential. You will need to be patient, compassionate, and able to work well in a team environment. We will provide comprehensive training so that you are equipped and empowered to help each child, even if you don’t currently have experience. Children can be unpredictable and potentially confrontational, so this role is not for the weak of spirit, mind, or body. Part of the joy of working with kids is exercise! Our clients move, so you need to be comfortable standing, walking, sitting, grasping, reaching, bending, kneeling, crouching, squatting, lifting, and at times carrying children or objects that weigh up to 50 pounds.

At the end of each day, you will go home knowing that you have made a meaningful impact on the life of a child and their family. Join us and become a part of a dedicated team that is changing lives for the better. Apply now to start your journey as a Behavior Technician with us!

Pay Range: $17 - $20

Requirements:

• Passionate about helping children with autism

• Patient, compassionate, and able to work well in a team

• 18+ years of age

• High school diploma or GED

• Ability to obtain a CPR, First Aid Certification and Tuberculosis test (if you haven’t had one in the last year)

• Ability to pass a pre employment background check

• Ability to move in various positions (sit, squat, bend, etc.)

• Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds

Perks of Working at Centria:

• Structured career path in the field of Behavioral Analysis

• Discounts to hundreds of retail partners via our Benefit Hub

• Access to Centria’s Employee Assistance Plan with benefits around mental health and counseling

• Early wage access to employees through Rain - Work today, get paid tomorrow!

• Unlimited opportunities to make an impact in the life of a special needs child

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, Veteran status, or disability status. This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of qualifications, skills, efforts, duties, responsibilities, or working conditions associated with the position. This pay scale range is the full range of potential wages Centria Autism reasonably expects to pay for employees with this job title and this pay scale range varies dependent on job qualifications, performance, experience, and/or seniority. This range should not be interrupted to mean that Centria Autism currently employs any employees with this job title at the bottom or top of the pay scale range. Centria reserves the right to amend this job description at any time, with or without written notice.
