jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
Fin, now part of Salesforce, is on a mission to help businesses provide perfect customer experiences.

Our AI Agent Fin is the highest-performing AI Customer Agent on the market today, enabling businesses to deliver impeccable, always-on customer support across the customer journey, from service, to sales, to ecommerce. Powered by our own AI models, Fin resolves complex customer issues end-to-end across every channel, with minimal set-up and integration. Fin can also be combined with our natively integrated Intercom help desk, giving modern support teams one single system.

Together with Salesforce, the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success, we're building the future of customer experience. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn't a buzzword, it's a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing, and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI.

Ready to level up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You're in the right place. Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

What's the opportunity?

As Fin becomes mission-critical for our most strategic customers, we’re growing our team of Forward Deployed Engineers to help bridge the gap between customer needs and product innovation.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll work hands-on with strategic customers, partnering closely with our R&D and Go-to-Market teams to design and deliver high-impact solutions. You’ll go beyond implementation - helping shape product direction, influence roadmap decisions and ensure Fin delivers real, measurable business outcomes in complex, real-world environments.

If you’re excited by ownership, creativity and solving ambiguous problems, and want to work at the frontier of applied AI while collaborating with Product, Engineering and Go-to-Market teams, this role offers a rare opportunity to combine technical excellence with real customer impact.

What will I be doing?

• Drive adoption of Fin by helping customers unlock the power of our AI capabilities to automate and scale their support operations.

• Embed deeply with strategic customers to understand their business challenges and technical requirements, and provide the insight needed to achieve outstanding results with Fin.

• Work hands-on with customers’ technical teams as a trusted technical expert, coding side-by-side to drive projects through to completion.

• Collaborate closely with Sales, Success and Product teams to ensure seamless customer experiences, successful project delivery and actionable product feedback.

• Contribute to the evolution of Forward Deployed Engineering by codifying best practices and sharing insights from customer engagements to help the team scale and grow.

What skills do I need?

• A strong engineering background and experience building software with real-world usage. Experience building a SaaS product is a plus, but not a requirement.

• Interest in AI and machine learning, and the ability to quickly build an understanding of novel problems, capabilities and architectures - including their trade-offs and limitations.

• Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to navigate organisational boundaries and bring people together to achieve the best outcomes for our customers.

• Deep knowledge of at least one high-level programming language, such as JavaScript, Python or Ruby. It doesn’t need to be a language we use today - great people learn quickly and can introduce us to better ways of working.

• The ability to prototype and ship software quickly while maintaining a high bar for quality and a clear focus on business goals and outcomes.

• Proficiency using and writing REST APIs to integrate systems effectively.

• Strong communication skills. You can comfortably discuss the same topics with engineers and non-technical audiences, adapting the depth and detail as needed.

• Willingness to travel and work on-site with customers to build strong relationships and deeply understand their needs.

*Proof of eligibility to work in the United States is required.

The base salary range for candidates within the San Francisco Bay Area is $180,000 - $237,000. Actual base pay will depend on a variety of factors such as education, skills, experience, location, etc. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. All regular employees may also be eligible for the corporate bonus program or a sales incentive (target included in OTE) as well as stock in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs).

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

In the United States, compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, job level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and benefits. At Fin, we want to give people what they need to do the best work of their careers. Our benefits and programs are designed to support your health and wellbeing, your family, your time away from work, and your financial future. Offerings vary by location in line with local practices and requirements. Learn more about working at Fin and the benefits we offer at fin.ai/careers. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring, Salesforce will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Policies

Fin has a hybrid working policy. We believe that working in person helps us stay connected, collaborate easier and create a great culture while still providing flexibility to work from home. We expect employees to be in the office at least three days per week.

We have a radically open and accepting culture at Fin. We avoid spending time on divisive subjects to foster a safe and cohesive work environment for everyone. As an organization, our policy is to not advocate on behalf of the company or our employees on any social or political topics out of our internal or external communications. We respect personal opinion and expression on these topics on personal social platforms on personal time, and do not challenge or confront anyone for their views on non-work related topics. Our goal is to focus on doing incredible work to achieve our goals and unite the company through our core values.

Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. Recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at Salesforce are fair and based on merit. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.

jobs.title: Field Officer
jobs.description:
Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it

Wave is now the largest financial institution in Senegal, with over 10 million users. We are still in the early stages of our product roadmap and its potential impact on people’s everyday lives.

We are looking for a field officer to manage product rollouts as we launch our business in Guinea. You will also represent Wave, oversee our distribution and marketing, interact with users, and interview people about their needs and problems regarding money transfer and financial services.

In this role, you'll:

• Ensure agent quality and compliance with legal and policy requirements.

• Guarantee the agent network is fully trained on applications, the contents of the contract before signing, rebalancing options, fraud management, etc.

• Collaborate with the BTL team to have a well-branded and equipped agent network.

• Collaborate with the agent liquidity team in monitoring the cash and float availability at agent locations.

• Manage risk through routine visits to report emerging issues and assess agents' performance in your territory.

• Identify underperforming agents, close them, recover Wave items and equipment, and ensure that branding material is removed.

• Be the primary contact for all agency networks acquiring Wave products in your territory.

• Champion excellent customer service among distributors and agents within your territory.

Requirements

• Fluent in English & French, with a good command of Malinke, Soussou and Poular.

• At least 2 years of relevant work experience, specifically managing an agent network in Guinea, including a minimum of 1 year of experience managing field-based teams.

Key details

• Location: This is a field role. You will be based in Conakry and may travel to other field locations across the country as needed for business purposes.

• Contract type: 6 months fixed-term contract.

• Work authorization in the Guinea is required.

You might be a good fit if you

• Are excited about working in the field, as this is a largely field-operations role.

• Detail-oriented and seek to achieve excellence in everything you do.

• Are a clear and proactive communicator, able to independently follow through on tasks and able to manage team priorities effectively.

• Enjoy teamwork, but also know how to work well independently.

• Are intellectually curious, creative in the way you go about tackling problems, and embrace failure as a means to spark innovation and growth.

• Communicate effectively and often, both in writing and in person, to the point of over-communication.

• Demonstrate tenacity and a willingness to go the distance to get something done.

• Are tech-savvy: comfortable navigating Excel and onboarding new tools.

#LI-MS1

Our team

• We have a rapidly growing in-country team in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, The Gambia, Uganda, Niger, Sierra Leone, and Cameroon plus remote team members spread across the world.

• We're deeply passionate about our mission of bringing radically affordable financial services to the people who need them most.

• We foster autonomy for our employees. You'll own your projects at every stage, from understanding the problem to monitoring your solution in production.

• We raised the largest Series A in Africa in 2021. Our world-class investors, include Founders Fund, Sequoia Heritage, Stripe, Ribbit Capital, Y Combinator, and Partech Africa.

• We are on Y Combinator's top companies by revenue.

How to apply

Fill out the form below, and upload a resume in English and a cover letter describing your interest in Wave and the role.

We review applications frequently and recommend that you apply to the role that most closely aligns with your skills, experience and career goals.

Wave is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Field Officer – Internal Audit (Fixed-Term), Kitui, Kenya
jobs.description:
About GiveDirectly

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

• Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.

• Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.

• Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.

• Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.

• Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.

• Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.

• Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.

• Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.

If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.

Want to learn more? Read and listen:

We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

Overview:

The Internal Audit Field Officer will play a critical day-to-day role in ensuring that GiveDirectly is able to deliver cash transfers to recipients safely. The Field Officer will be part of the team that is responsible for preventing, detecting, mitigating, and investigating field-based risks for GiveDirectly.

The role will reward high-quality judgment on operational questions and challenges, a strong work ethic, effective communication skills, attention to detail, a strong sense of independence, and a strong commitment to GiveDirectly’s mission and model. In essence, the Internal Audit Field Officer will be expected to audit the work of the enrolment team, whose core responsibility is surveying households and enrolling them in our programs.

Due to the sensitive nature of the work done by the internal audit team, we require all in-country internal audit staff to remain firewalled from the rest of the staff. This means operating discretely and independently, with interactions strictly limited to just the colleagues within the same team. The role holder will be expected to carry out day-to-day audit tasks with an absolute level of discretion, impartiality, neutrality, and independence.

Duty Station: Kitui Sub-County

Note: Fresh graduates are highly encouraged to apply.

Key Responsibilities

Recipient engagement (60%):

• Conduct in-person household visits for all individuals selected for enrollment to check and determine their safety for enrollment, assess vulnerabilities, and flag any pre-enrollment risk indicators to the management for proactive resolution.

• Directly engage with high-risk recipients to provide them with the necessary support so that they receive their transfers safely

• Directly engage with recipients to identify any corrections or improvements in field processes that are needed.

• Investigate and resolve any recipient cases that have been flagged to the Internal Audit team.

• Identify and escalate key risks associated with GD’s programs in the community.

Risk monitoring (30%):

• Work with the IA AFM to undertake risk monitoring activities within the community

• Work with the IA AFM to verify the quality and the risk level of the partner data pre-enrollment

• Measure the quality of data received from the field teams against set data quality standards, reporting any cases of inconsistency.

• Report any cases of fraud and bribery by GD staff and or recipient(s) that are identified through the appropriate escalation channels.

• Utilise technology to flag any abnormalities in operation.

Other (10%)

• Support the IA AFM in the onboarding processes of new team members

• Assist the IA AFM with hosting visitors to the project location

• Assist with response to “crisis” events (e.g., refusal spikes, government shutdown, coordinated fraud, etc.)

• Promote effective team culture by encouraging recognition of positive achievements, planning team events periodically, and other team-building initiatives

Required Qualifications

• Bachelors degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.

• Having a Fraud Investigation experience is an added advantage.

• Has the ability to audit cash transfer recipients by conducting in-person or virtual surveys and associated processes.

• Proficiency in Kamba language is a MUST.

• Fluency in English and Kiswahili

• Good computer and mobile device data entry and assessment ability or experience.

• Possess critical thinking ability and good judgment in resolving operational glitches.

• Possesses a high-quality problem-solving work ethic.

• Good time-management skills

• Strong interest in the mission of GiveDirectly and commitment to advancing GD’s distinctive values.

• Physical fitness and the ability to cope with difficult weather conditions or terrain.

• Have the ability to exercise patience and good judgment in resolving recipient problems.

Working at GiveDirectly

GiveDirectly is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to the person’s race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Flagging for US applicants: We invite you to "Know Your Rights" as an applicant.

Commitment to Safeguarding

As a global organization working with communities to eliminate extreme poverty, GiveDirectly takes the safeguarding of its recipients, staff, and partners seriously. To that end, GiveDirectly is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and will systematically check with previous employers about any abuse or misconduct related matters involving potential new hires. We may also employ other robust pre-hire screens, including in-depth reference checks, criminal background checks, and sanctions screens.

These efforts help us continue to build and maintain trust with the communities we work with, and prevent abuse to our recipients and staff.

**GD is committed to observing all local, national and international laws that protect people and basic human rights of all. GD is committed to a policy of “zero tolerance when it comes to preventing,  reporting, or responding to any form of abuse or  exploitation.” and expects anyone who works for GD to uphold the protection and safeguarding of our recipients as a priority.**

Reasonable Accommodations

We are committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible work environment. If you require any accommodations during the application or interview process, or to perform the essential functions of the role, please email us at careers@givedirectly.org with the email subject “Accommodation Needed”. We will work with you to ensure reasonable accommodations are made to support your needs.

Want to put your best foot forward on your GiveDirectly application? Take a look at our Candidate Application Prep Guide!

Referrals

Know the right person for this role? Please consider referring them. We offer a reward of $3,000 for a Senior Manager or above role, and $500 for a Manager role, paid if we end up hiring your referral. Thank you for sending great people our way!

jobs.title: Lead Product Data Scientist, Forecasting
jobs.description:
At Klaviyo, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives each Klaviyo (we call ourselves Klaviyos) brings to our workplace each and every day. We believe everyone deserves a fair shot at success and appreciate the experiences each person brings beyond the traditional job requirements. If you’re a close but not exact match with the description, we hope you’ll still consider applying. Want to learn more about life at Klaviyo? Visit klaviyo.com/careers to see how we empower creators to own their own destiny.

Lead Product Data Scientist, Forecasting

About the Team

Klaviyo's Product Data Science team plays a critical role in shaping how we understand, measure, and improve business performance. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, and Go-to-Market teams to turn complex data into actionable insights that inform product strategy, financial planning, and long-term growth.

As Klaviyo continues to scale its platform, expand its product portfolio, and introduce new AI-powered capabilities, the ability to accurately forecast business outcomes and understand the drivers behind them has never been more important.

Our team combines rigorous statistical modeling, advanced analytics, and deep business understanding to help leaders make better decisions. We believe data science should be embedded in the product development lifecycle, influencing strategic investments, identifying opportunities, and enabling teams to move quickly and confidently.

About the Role

We're looking for a Lead Product Data Scientist, Forecasting to own and advance Klaviyo's forecasting capabilities, combining deep technical expertise with strong business judgment to influence some of our most important product and strategic decisions.

This is a highly visible, hands-on technical leadership role at the intersection of data science, product strategy, and business performance. You'll lead the development of sophisticated revenue forecasting models, establish rigorous evaluation standards, and help the organization better understand how customer behavior, product investments, pricing decisions, and market dynamics influence business outcomes.

This isn't just about building accurate models or reporting on historical trends. We're looking for someone who can connect advanced statistical methods to real business questions, challenge assumptions, investigate unexpected outcomes, and translate complex findings into clear recommendations that shape decisions.

You'll work closely with Product, Finance, Engineering, and Go-to-Market leadership to build scalable forecasting systems and self-service analytical capabilities. You'll also help define the technical direction of forecasting at Klaviyo, mentor other data scientists, and establish the methodologies and standards that make forecasting a trusted, repeatable practice across the company.

How You'll Make a Difference

• Own revenue forecasting end to end, from problem framing and data preparation through model development, evaluation, deployment, and ongoing monitoring, ensuring forecasts serve as trusted inputs to business planning and product decisions.

• Build sophisticated forecasting models across multiple time horizons and levels of granularity, leveraging hierarchical forecasting, probabilistic and Bayesian methods, classical time series techniques, machine learning, and emerging time series foundation models.

• Establish forecasting standards and governance by defining how the organization measures accuracy, bias, calibration, and uncertainty, creating consistent and rigorous approaches to model evaluation and performance.

• Lead the technical direction of forecasting, evaluating modeling approaches, reviewing technical designs, mentoring other data scientists, and raising the bar for statistical methodology, code quality, and analytical rigor.

• Connect forecasting to business strategy by partnering with Product, Finance, Engineering, and Go-to-Market teams to support scenario planning, evaluate strategic investments, and translate ambiguous business questions into actionable analytical plans.

• Uncover drivers of customer and product performance through advanced statistical research, including mixed effects models, clustering, time series analysis, and other techniques that reveal meaningful patterns and inform product strategy.

• Lead root cause investigations when actual business performance diverges from forecasts, identifying whether changes stem from data quality, model limitations, customer behavior, product or pricing decisions, or external factors.

• Build scalable root cause analysis frameworks through repeatable methodologies, templates, and dashboards, enabling other data scientists and business stakeholders to investigate performance consistently and efficiently.

• Develop self-service forecasting and analytics capabilities that empower product managers and cross-functional leaders to explore business trends, evaluate scenarios, and make informed decisions independently.

• Partner with Data Engineering to build reliable data pipelines and dbt models that provide clean, well-structured, and trustworthy data for forecasting and downstream analysis.

• Evaluate emerging AI and forecasting technologies, identifying opportunities to leverage new modeling techniques, time series foundation models, and AI-powered tools to improve accuracy, efficiency, and decision support.

• Influence decisions across the organization by communicating complex statistical findings and business implications clearly and persuasively to stakeholders ranging from individual contributors to executive leadership.

Who You Are

• You have 10+ years of experience in data science, product analytics, applied statistics, or a related quantitative discipline, including significant hands-on experience building and deploying forecasting solutions in production.

• You bring deep expertise in time series forecasting, statistical modeling, and model evaluation, with experience applying methods such as hierarchical forecasting, probabilistic or Bayesian approaches, and machine learning to complex business problems.

• You're highly proficient in SQL and Python or R, with experience developing production-quality analytical solutions and familiarity with dbt and modern analytics engineering practices.

• You've demonstrated technical leadership by setting direction on complex projects, mentoring other data scientists, reviewing modeling approaches, and influencing technical standards across teams.

• You combine statistical rigor with strong business intuition and understand how product development, customer behavior, pricing, and strategic investments translate into measurable financial and business outcomes.

• You're comfortable owning complex analytical problems from initial exploration through production deployment, ongoing monitoring, and continuous improvement.

• You can translate ambiguous business questions into well-defined analytical approaches, establish meaningful success metrics, and deliver actionable recommendations.

• You're a compelling communicator who can explain sophisticated statistical concepts and modeling tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical audiences, including senior executives.

• You thrive in cross-functional environments and enjoy partnering with Product, Finance, Engineering, and business leaders to influence strategic decisions and improve customer outcomes.

• You're comfortable operating in ambiguity, move with urgency, and know how to balance analytical rigor with the speed and iteration required in a high-growth product environment.

• You bring an AI-first mindset, with curiosity and familiarity around emerging technologies such as time series foundation models, LLMs, and agentic tools that can improve forecasting, analytical workflows, and decision support.

jobs.description:
At Klaviyo, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives each Klaviyo (we call ourselves Klaviyos) brings to our workplace each and every day. We believe everyone deserves a fair shot at success and appreciate the experiences each person brings beyond the traditional job requirements. If you’re a close but not exact match with the description, we hope you’ll still consider applying. Want to learn more about life at Klaviyo? Visit klaviyo.com/careers to see how we empower creators to own their own destiny.

Lead Product Data Scientist, Agents

About the Team

Klaviyo's Product Data Science team plays a critical role in shaping how we understand, measure, and improve product and business performance. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, and Go-to-Market teams to turn complex data into actionable insights that inform product strategy, customer experience, and long-term growth.

As Klaviyo continues to expand its AI-powered capabilities, intelligent agents are becoming central to how businesses engage with their customers. Composer, Klaviyo's AI marketing agent, helps marketers analyze, build, and execute their marketing strategies, while Customer Agent enables brands to engage shoppers and answer questions across channels including chat, email, SMS, and WhatsApp.

These products are evolving rapidly, creating new opportunities and challenges in understanding agent performance, measuring customer value, and connecting AI-driven experiences to meaningful business outcomes.

Our team takes an AI-first approach to data science, leveraging emerging technologies and agentic tools to accelerate analytical workflows, improve decision-making, and focus our efforts on the complex questions that matter most to customers and the business.

About the Role

We're looking for a Lead Product Data Scientist, Agents to own and advance Klaviyo's measurement and data science strategy across Composer and Customer Agent, combining deep technical expertise with strong product and business judgment to influence some of our most important AI investments.

This is a highly visible, hands-on technical leadership role at the intersection of data science, AI product development, and business strategy. You'll define how we measure the adoption, engagement, quality, cost, and business impact of our AI agents, establishing the analytical foundations that help teams understand what creates meaningful customer value.

This isn't just about building dashboards or tracking traditional product metrics. We're looking for someone who can tackle emerging measurement challenges, develop rigorous approaches to evaluating agent performance, and determine whether AI-powered experiences are genuinely improving customer outcomes. You'll combine experimentation, causal inference, and advanced analytics to help leaders make informed decisions in an environment where established measurement frameworks are still evolving.

You'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, and executive leadership to shape product strategy, evaluate pricing and monetization opportunities, and translate complex analytical findings into actionable recommendations. You'll also help define the technical direction of agent analytics at Klaviyo, mentor other data scientists, and establish the shared metrics, methodologies, and data foundations that enable teams to make confident, data-driven decisions.

How You'll Make a Difference

• Own agent measurement end to end across Composer and Customer Agent, developing comprehensive measurement frameworks that connect adoption, engagement, agent performance, customer value, and revenue impact.

• Define what successful agent performance looks like by partnering with Product and Engineering to establish meaningful measures of agent effectiveness, task completion, customer outcomes, failure rates, and the trade-offs between quality, cost, and business value.

• Build scalable agent evaluation frameworks by combining conversation data, agent traces, tool-call outcomes, human evaluation, and LLM-based classification to assess quality, identify failure patterns, and understand how changes to models and agent behavior influence product performance.

• Measure causal impact and incremental value through experimentation and advanced statistical methods, including quasi-experimental approaches such as difference-in-differences, matched comparisons, staged rollouts, and synthetic controls, to determine how AI agents influence customer behavior, retention, and revenue.

• Connect agent performance to business strategy by partnering with Finance and Product teams to evaluate usage-based pricing, packaging, credit economics, model costs, conversion, and the financial implications of product investments.

• Establish trusted metrics and analytical standards by defining consistent measurement methodologies, governed data models, and evaluation practices that enable teams to make informed decisions as AI products and underlying technologies evolve.

• Lead with an AI-first approach to analytics, leveraging coding agents, LLMs, and emerging tools to accelerate SQL development, data modeling, dashboard creation, conversation classification, and analytical workflows while maintaining rigorous validation and quality standards.

• Build scalable, self-service analytics capabilities that empower product managers and cross-functional stakeholders to independently explore agent performance, evaluate customer outcomes, and identify opportunities for improvement.

• Partner with Engineering and Analytics Engineering to develop reliable instrumentation, data pipelines, and dbt models that capture agent interactions, support robust evaluation, and maintain data quality as new capabilities are introduced.

• Lead the technical direction of agent analytics, reviewing analytical approaches, mentoring other data scientists, establishing best practices, and raising the bar for statistical rigor, measurement quality, and AI-native ways of working.

• Influence product and executive decisions by translating complex analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations, aligning cross-functional stakeholders on meaningful metrics, and communicating uncertainty and trade-offs effectively.

• Shape the future of AI product measurement by continuously evaluating emerging methodologies, challenging existing assumptions, and prioritizing the analytical questions that matter most as Klaviyo's agents and AI strategy evolve.

Who You Are

• You have 10+ years of experience in data science, product analytics, applied statistics, or a related quantitative discipline, including recent hands-on experience measuring AI, machine learning, or LLM-powered products in production.

• You bring deep expertise in product measurement, experimentation, statistical modeling, and causal inference, with the ability to select and defend rigorous analytical approaches when traditional randomized experiments aren't feasible.

• You have experience evaluating AI systems in production, including designing evaluation frameworks, analyzing agent interactions or conversations, leveraging human labeling or LLM-as-judge methodologies, and understanding how model, prompt, and tool changes influence product outcomes.

• You're highly proficient in SQL and Python or R, with experience developing production-quality analytical solutions and familiarity with dbt and modern analytics engineering practices.

• You take an AI-first approach to your work, actively leveraging coding agents, LLMs, and emerging tools to accelerate analytical workflows while understanding their limitations and ensuring the accuracy and reliability of their outputs.

• You've demonstrated technical leadership by setting direction on complex analytical initiatives, mentoring other data scientists, reviewing methodologies, and influencing technical standards across teams.

• You combine statistical rigor with strong product and business intuition, understanding how customer engagement, AI product performance, usage-based pricing, and unit economics translate into meaningful customer and business outcomes.

• You're comfortable tackling ambiguous, emerging problems where established metrics or methodologies may not yet exist, and can develop practical frameworks that balance analytical rigor with business needs.

• You have a track record of influencing senior stakeholders, aligning cross-functional teams around shared definitions and priorities, and translating complex findings into clear recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences.

• You're a compelling communicator who can explain sophisticated analytical concepts, challenge assumptions constructively, and communicate uncertainty and trade-offs with confidence.

• You thrive in fast-moving product environments, adapt quickly as priorities evolve, and know how to balance analytical depth with the urgency and iteration required to build and improve AI-powered products.

• You have a degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Finance, Engineering, or another quantitative discipline, or an MBA with a quantitative emphasis. Equivalent hands-on experience in applied data science is equally valued.

Nice to Have

• Experience measuring and optimizing AI agents, conversational AI, or LLM-powered products in a high-growth B2B SaaS or product-focused technology company.

• Hands-on experience with agent observability and evaluation platforms such as Braintrust, LangSmith, or Arize, including working with agent traces, tool-call data, and evaluation pipelines.

• Experience with usage-based or consumption-based pricing, credit models, AI infrastructure costs, or LLM unit economics.

• Experience building governed metrics, semantic layers, metric trees, or standardized measurement frameworks used across multiple product teams.

• Experience applying classification, clustering, or other advanced analytical methods to large volumes of unstructured text, customer conversations, or agent interactions.

• Experience developing internal AI agents or AI-powered analytics tools that improve team productivity and decision-making.

• Familiarity with marketing attribution, incremental measurement, or evaluating the impact of AI-driven customer engagement.

• Background in marketing technology, ecommerce, CRM, customer-service software, or other data-driven SaaS products.

Why This Role Matters

AI agents are central to Klaviyo's product strategy and the future of how businesses engage with their customers. As Composer and Customer Agent become increasingly sophisticated, understanding whether these products are delivering meaningful value, how effectively they perform, and where to invest next will be critical to their long-term success.

In this role, you'll help establish how Klaviyo measures the effectiveness and business impact of AI agents, developing the frameworks, methodologies, and analytical foundations that inform some of our most important product, pricing, and investment decisions. Your work will directly influence how we improve agent quality, understand customer outcomes, and connect AI innovation to measurable business value.

jobs.title: Field Officer – Internal Audit (Fixed-Term), Magarini, Kenya
jobs.description:
About GiveDirectly

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

• Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.

• Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.

• Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.

• Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.

• Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.

• Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.

• Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.

• Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.

If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.

Want to learn more? Read and listen:

We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

Overview:

The Internal Audit Field Officer will play a critical day-to-day role in ensuring that GiveDirectly is able to deliver cash transfers to recipients safely. The Field Officer will be part of the team that is responsible for preventing, detecting, mitigating, and investigating field-based risks for GiveDirectly.

The role will reward high-quality judgment on operational questions and challenges, a strong work ethic, effective communication skills, attention to detail, a strong sense of independence, and a strong commitment to GiveDirectly’s mission and model. In essence, the Internal Audit Field Officer will be expected to audit the work of the enrolment team, whose core responsibility is surveying households and enrolling them in our programs.

Due to the sensitive nature of the work done by the internal audit team, we require all in-country internal audit staff to remain firewalled from the rest of the staff. This means operating discretely and independently, with interactions strictly limited to just the colleagues within the same team. The role holder will be expected to carry out day-to-day audit tasks with an absolute level of discretion, impartiality, neutrality, and independence.

Duty Station: Magarini Sub-County

Note: Fresh graduates are highly encouraged to apply.

Key Responsibilities

Recipient engagement (60%):

• Conduct in-person household visits for all individuals selected for enrollment to check and determine their safety for enrollment, assess vulnerabilities, and flag any pre-enrollment risk indicators to the management for proactive resolution.

• Directly engage with high-risk recipients to provide them with the necessary support so that they receive their transfers safely

• Directly engage with recipients to identify any corrections or improvements in field processes that are needed.

• Investigate and resolve any recipient cases that have been flagged to the Internal Audit team.

• Identify and escalate key risks associated with GD’s programs in the community.

Risk monitoring (30%):

• Work with the IA AFM to undertake risk monitoring activities within the community

• Work with the IA AFM to verify the quality and the risk level of the partner data pre-enrollment

• Measure the quality of data received from the field teams against set data quality standards, reporting any cases of inconsistency.

• Report any cases of fraud and bribery by GD staff and or recipient(s) that are identified through the appropriate escalation channels.

• Utilise technology to flag any abnormalities in operation.

Other (10%)

• Support the IA AFM in the onboarding processes of new team members

• Assist the IA AFM with hosting visitors to the project location

• Assist with response to “crisis” events (e.g., refusal spikes, government shutdown, coordinated fraud, etc.)

• Promote effective team culture by encouraging recognition of positive achievements, planning team events periodically, and other team-building initiatives

Required Qualifications

• Bachelors degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.

• Having a Fraud Investigation experience is an added advantage.

• Has the ability to audit cash transfer recipients by conducting in-person or virtual surveys and associated processes.

• Proficiency in Giriama language is a MUST.

• Fluency in English and Kiswahili

• Good computer and mobile device data entry and assessment ability or experience.

• Possess critical thinking ability and good judgment in resolving operational glitches.

• Possesses a high-quality problem-solving work ethic.

• Good time-management skills

• Strong interest in the mission of GiveDirectly and commitment to advancing GD’s distinctive values.

• Physical fitness and the ability to cope with difficult weather conditions or terrain.

• Have the ability to exercise patience and good judgment in resolving recipient problems.

Working at GiveDirectly

GiveDirectly is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to the person’s race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Flagging for US applicants: We invite you to "Know Your Rights" as an applicant.

Commitment to Safeguarding

As a global organization working with communities to eliminate extreme poverty, GiveDirectly takes the safeguarding of its recipients, staff, and partners seriously. To that end, GiveDirectly is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and will systematically check with previous employers about any abuse or misconduct related matters involving potential new hires. We may also employ other robust pre-hire screens, including in-depth reference checks, criminal background checks, and sanctions screens.

These efforts help us continue to build and maintain trust with the communities we work with, and prevent abuse to our recipients and staff.

**GD is committed to observing all local, national and international laws that protect people and basic human rights of all. GD is committed to a policy of “zero tolerance when it comes to preventing,  reporting, or responding to any form of abuse or  exploitation.” and expects anyone who works for GD to uphold the protection and safeguarding of our recipients as a priority.**

Reasonable Accommodations

We are committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible work environment. If you require any accommodations during the application or interview process, or to perform the essential functions of the role, please email us at careers@givedirectly.org with the email subject “Accommodation Needed”. We will work with you to ensure reasonable accommodations are made to support your needs.

Want to put your best foot forward on your GiveDirectly application? Take a look at our Candidate Application Prep Guide!

Referrals

Know the right person for this role? Please consider referring them. We offer a reward of $3,000 for a Senior Manager or above role, and $500 for a Manager role, paid if we end up hiring your referral. Thank you for sending great people our way!

Role:  Security Monitoring Associate, Part Time

Location: Pittsburgh, PA

Part Time

We are Growers, We are Wholesalers, We are Producers, We Are Budtenders, We are Retailers, We are Partners, and We are Hiring

Your Impact:

• Watch our security cameras during the day to help keep the team, our stores and facilities, and products safe. Watch for anything unusual or out of place and communicate concerns effectively.

• Welcome and check in visitors using our iPad system and make sure all doors are secure. Ensuring that all visitors are authorized to be in the building.

• Keep logs up to date — including scanned IDs, visitor sign-ins, and daily security notes.

• Notify management of issues with cameras, alarms, or internet connectivity. whether it’s a technical issue with the cameras or suspicious activity — report it to leadership right away so it can be handled quickly and properly.

• Ensure all activity aligns with company policies and state/local cannabis regulations.

• Help keep the space clean, safe, and support the team with other tasks when needed.

Your Strengths:

• You're alert, observant, and take pride in keeping people and property safe.

• You have experience with security systems and CCTV monitoring and know how to spot when something’s off.

• You have strong communication skills and can stay calm and clear under pressure.

• You work well with all kinds of people and help create a respectful, secure environment for both staff and visitors.

• You’re reliable, flexible, and can handle multiple tasks without missing a beat — whether it’s monitoring cameras, logging visitor info, or responding to alerts

jobs.title: Office Assistant - Kitui
jobs.description:
About GiveDirectly

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

• Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.

• Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.

• Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.

• Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.

• Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager North America
jobs.description:
Hi, I'm Elodie https://www.linkedin.com/in/elodieorourke/, VP Customer Success at FeedbackFruits. 👋

More than 200 universities and colleges use FeedbackFruits to make good teaching possible at scale, and my team's job is to make sure that actually happens on their campuses, long after a contract is signed. We're reshaping Partner Success so it can grow with our partners, and a big part of that is building a real presence in the Americas. This role is the first step there, and the person who takes it will help shape what that region becomes.

I'm looking for someone to own our US partnerships from the first training all the way to renewal. You'll work with instructors, instructional designers and university leadership, helping them get value from our tools and building the kind of relationships where people tell you early when something isn't landing. Adoption in higher education takes patience, because budgets are tight, the academic calendar sets the pace and our product rewards the time people put into learning it. The people who do well in this role stay steady through that and keep finding ways to move an account forward.

You'll be based in the US and work fully remotely, with the rest of the team spread across Europe and APAC and our headquarters in Amsterdam. That comes with a lot of autonomy and a lot of trust. You'll run your own book, travel to partner campuses and conferences, and have direct influence on our product and on how universities teach. If you want to help build a new region with a VP who will back you while you do it, I'd love to hear from you.



What you'll do:

 - Own a portfolio of US partner institutions and run their renewals end to end, from the proposal through contract negotiation and working with our Legal team

 - Keep a close eye on adoption health and turn usage data into adoption plans and reports that partners can act on

 - Run trainings and demos for faculty and instructional designers, and advise on pedagogy and product so our tools get used well

 - Build relationships across each institution, from instructors to C-level, and grow internal champions who carry FeedbackFruits forward when you're not in the room

 - Spot upsell and cross-sell opportunities and lead expansion conversations together with our US Account Executive

 - Visit partners on campus and represent us at events and conferences, for up to 20% of your time

 - Bring partner feedback to our Product team with the evidence behind it

 - Keep HubSpot accurate, so your renewal forecast and at-risk accounts are always clear to the team



What you bring:

 - You have at least 3 years in account management, customer success or partner management, and you've landed renewals you can walk someone through in detail, including the hard ones

 - You're as comfortable with a professor as with a provost, and you run those conversations on your own

 - You pick up complex software quickly, enjoy digging into data, and can explain an LMS integration without losing your audience

 - You drive your own book. You prioritise, spot risk early and get moving without waiting for someone to check in

 - You negotiate with confidence and stay calm when a renewal gets tricky, because you've brought the evidence with you

 - You stay resilient when progress is slow, and you can tell the difference between "this isn't working" and "this hasn't worked yet"

 - You say things clearly and early, whether that's a risk on an account or a well-reasoned no

 - You might already know Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle or D2L Brightspace, or how procurement, accessibility and the academic calendar work in US higher ed. That helps a lot here, as does HubSpot experience

jobs.title: Senior Talent Partner (GTM)
jobs.description:
Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.

 

Rising costs, wage increases, labor shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organizations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.

 

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here https://www.sona.ai/careers.

 

About the Role

 

As our founding US teams in New York, San Francisco and Austin begin to scale, we're hiring a Talent Partner to build out the US hiring function. You'll be the first dedicated Talent hire in the region, owning how we attract and assess US talent and laying the foundation for our entire US operation.

 

This role reports into the Head of Talent, based in the UK. You'll work closely with our VP of North America Sales and other key leaders based in our San Francisco office. Our US story is early but proven: we've got customers signed, leadership in place, and real momentum, and now it needs scaling.

 

That means high ownership and the freedom to build, but it also means ambiguity, a fast pace, and priorities that shift as the business moves. This role isn't for everyone. If you need a fixed playbook and a settled environment, it won't suit. If building one from scratch is the part that excites you, you'll thrive here.

 

Responsibilities

 

 - Own hiring for US-based roles end to end, across our New York, San Francisco and Austin hubs, from kickoff and briefing through sourcing, interviewing, and offer to signed contract

 - Hire primarily go-to-market roles (sales, marketing), with some Customer and other roles as the team grows

 - Lay the foundations of the US talent and people function as we scale: employer brand, process, ways of working, and ad-hoc people operations

 - Innovate using AI to improve the speed and quality of hiring at Sona

 

Requirements

 

 - An experienced full-lifecycle recruiter, able to support and own end-to-end hiring independently in a high-ambiguity environment

 - A specialist in hiring go-to-market talent into high-bar, fast-moving organisations, who understands what separates a strong hire from an average one

 - A strong sourcer, for whom building an outbound pipeline is a standard part of their rhythm

 - Data-driven and comfortable owning a funnel, using the numbers to troubleshoot, advise, and forecast

 - An advanced user of AI tools to improve the speed, efficiency, and quality of hiring

 - Experience in VC-backed enterprise AI/SaaS preferred

 

Benefits

 

 - Salary: $175,000 - $200,000

 - Hybrid: San Francisco, minimum 3 days a week

 - Share options

 - 20 days PTO + sick days

 - 401k contributions, employer match up to 2%

 - Comprehensive health cover via Aetna

 - Enhanced parental leave & pay

 - Annual all expenses paid team retreats

 - The latest Macbook and equipment budget for your home office

 - Professional development budget

 - Unlimited free books

 

Note: this represents a typical benefits package for a US-based, full-time employee. Exact details may vary based on location and employment type but we try to be as fair as possible to all of our team members. Please ask your contact in the Talent team to clarify the available benefits for you.

jobs.description:
A LITTLE ABOUT US

incident.io http://incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at OpenAI, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.




THE ROLE IN ONE LINE

We're looking for ridiculously smart, ambitious grads who want to break into the startup world. No experience needed. Just serious drive, great instincts, and an appetite to build something big.




WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE DAY TO DAY

If you want to get into startups, this is your foot in the door.

This role sits under our Talent team in SF, working closely with our founders and leaders to find the insane people who will help us build incident.io http://incident.io.

Talent is one of the few roles where you get to work across the entire business. You'll get a front-row seat to how a startup scales, and help us build one of the best teams in the world.

We're growing fast in SF, and we need to find insane talent to make it happen.

We're not a team that posts jobs and waits for applications. We're out hunting for exceptional people, building relationships, throwing events, dreaming up crazy campaigns, and finding creative ways to get incident.io http://incident.io on the map.

You'll have loads of ownership from day one, learn from some of the smartest people around, and get exposure to pretty much every part of building a company.

And where you take it from there is up to you. Talent is an incredible platform for a career in startups, whether you want to become a world-class recruiter, move into another part of the business, or eventually build something of your own.




WHO YOU ARE

 - You're ridiculously driven. You've got big ambitions, you work hard, and you're willing to do what it takes to get there.

 - You're a builder. You've started things, created things, made things happen. Maybe that's a business, a side project, a university society, or something completely different.

 - You're seriously smart. You learn fast, ask great questions, and figure things out quickly.

 - You make things happen. You don't need someone telling you what to do. You're resourceful, proactive, and find a way to get things done.

 - You're great with people. You're confident, curious, and can build relationships with just about anyone.

 - You've got big ideas. You're creative, think differently, and love trying things nobody else has thought of.

We don't care what you studied or whether you've ever worked in startups. We're looking for people with exceptional potential.

Maybe you've built an app, started a business, organised an event, or done something completely unrelated that shows you've got serious drive.

If you're hungry, ambitious, and want to throw yourself into the startup world, we want to hear from you.




SUPPORTING YOU

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

 - Market-leading private medical insurance. The proper kind, so you're never weighing up your health against a bill.

 - Competitive PTO. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

 - First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

 - Enhanced 401k. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

 - Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

 - Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

jobs.title: Chief Engineer (Optical Comms)
jobs.description:
About Apolink

Apolink is building the first-ever backward-compatible data relay constellation in low Earth orbit. By enabling efficient data aggregation and relay through our hybrid RF-optical inter-satellite link (ISL) architecture, we support scalable and resilient space infrastructure across commercial, federal, and defense applications.


About The Role:

The Chief Engineer (Optical) is the company’s technical lead for optical communications across our LEO data relay constellation. They own the optical architecture, requirements, link design, and verification, and lead technical decisions with our optical terminal vendor. The vendor handles terminal manufacturing, while this role remains hands-on with analysis, integration, and testing. This is a sole-contributor leadership role.



Responsibilities:

 - Own optical ISL and feeder-link architecture: wavelength plan, modulation and coding, aperture and divergence sizing, data rate vs range tradespace.

 - Develop and maintain end-to-end optical link budgets, including coherent receiver sensitivity, PAT margin, platform jitter, point-ahead, Doppler, stray light, fade statistics, and BER against realistic FEC.

 - Author optical requirements and ICDs, and manage flowdown to the vendor and to internal bus, flight software, and ground teams.

 - Direct the vendor technically: down-select, diligence, SOW and NRE scoping, design review participation, and accountability for performance and schedule.

 - Adjudicate R&D direction with the vendor; what warrants NRE investment, what is technically unviable, what we buy versus co-develop.

 - May lead a ZR-class coherent transceiver NRE with the optical terminal.

 - Maintain compliance with applicable standards, including CCSDS O3K and SDA OCT where relevant to federal programs.



Qualifications:

 - Direct, hands-on experience with LEO-LEO optical inter-satellite links: designing, building, or verifying crosslink terminals between spacecraft in low Earth orbit.

 - 6+ years in free-space optical communications, coherent optical transport, or spaceborne photonics.

 - MS or PhD in optics, EE, or physics, or equivalent demonstrated depth.

 - Demonstrated experience directing vendor technical performance and NRE programs.

 - Capacity to exercise independent technical judgment as the sole optical authority and be accountable for it.



Preferred:

 - Direct experience with 400ZR, 800ZR, OpenZR+, or OIF coherent pluggables.

 - Flight heritage on an optical comms payload.



Benefits:

 - Competitive salary and benefits package

 - Meaningful early-stage equity

 - Opportunity to own optical for a constellation end to end

 - Medical, dental, vision, 401(k), relocation assistance
   
   Salary: $180,000-$220,000
   
   

Additional Information

To conform to the U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. 


Apolink is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

jobs.title: Sr. Software Systems Safety Engineer
jobs.description:
Apptronik is a human-centered robotics company developing AI-powered robots to support humanity in every facet of life. Our flagship humanoid robot, Apollo, is built to collaborate thoughtfully with people, starting with critical industries such as manufacturing and logistics, with future applications in healthcare, the home, and beyond.

We operate at the cutting edge of Applied AI, applying our expertise across the full robotics stack to solve some of society's most important problems. You will join a team dedicated to bringing Apollo to market at scale, tackling the complex challenges like safety, commercialization, and mass production to change the world for the better.

JOB SUMMARY

Own the safety assurance of the software and AI that run our humanoid robots, from architecture analysis through verification evidence. You will analyze software and AI safety architectures, lead the safety analyses, and assess whether the evidence supports our safety claims. You will draw on IEC 61508-3, ISO/IEC TS 22440, and deep experience with safety-critical software systems.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES or KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

• Collaborate on system-level risk assessments, allocate risk reduction measures to software and AI elements, and own the breakdown of software-domain safety requirements into subsystem and element-level requirements

• Analyze and define the software safety architecture, including partitioning and freedom from interference, watchdogs, diagnostics, plausibility and timing monitoring, communication integrity, startup/shutdown behavior, and fault handling

• Lead software safety analyses, including software FMEA, fault tree analysis, dependent/common-cause failure analysis, and timing and resource analysis

• Specify safety-related software behavior, such as monitors, diagnostics, and safe-state logic, and review software team designs against IEC 61508-3 requirements for the target SIL / SC

• Define the IEC 61508-3 software safety plan and lifecycle, and assess team conformance through reviews and audits, including existing in-house, open-source, and third-party libraries, RTOS, and middleware

• Assess software systematic capability and review verification evidence, including coverage, static analysis, fault injection, and software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop test results, for adequacy against safety claims

• Apply the AI safety lifecycle (ISO/IEC TS 22440) to AI/ML-enabled functions, defining the safety architecture around them, including independence of safety functions from learned components and the safety mechanisms that monitor them

• Assess AI/ML safety evidence against the AI safety lifecycle, including data and model assurance, performance limitations, and operational design domain

• Own software requirements traceability and the software portion of the safety case, including gap assessments against standards

• Support product safety and compliance teams in certification and demonstration of standards conformity

SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS

• Demonstrated experience analyzing and assuring safety-critical software architectures, including software safety analyses and safety case development

• Practical application of the IEC 61508-3 or ISO 26262-6 (automotive) software lifecycle, with depth in software safety activities and qualification of existing software and tools, and experience with IEC 62061, ISO 13849, ISO 10218, ANSI/A3 R15.06, or ISO 25785-1 as relevant

• Strong knowledge of embedded software architectures, including RTOS, mixed-criticality partitioning, watchdogs, communication buses, and diagnostics

• Hands-on experience with FMEA/FMEDA, FTA, and dependent failure analysis, and with reviewing verification evidence such as fault injection, software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop testing, and test coverage

• Working knowledge of safety for AI/ML-enabled systems, such as ISO/IEC TS 22440; familiarity with ISO/PAS 8800, UL 4600, or SOTIF preferred

• Experience with requirements and traceability tools such as JAMA; familiarity with Git, CI/CD, and static analysis; certification or third-party assessment experience preferred

• Ability to work cross-functionally and make sound, risk-based engineering decisions

• Experience with common Product Development Processes / Product Lifecycle management including Agile, CMMI, Waterfall, etc. helping teams to deliver to organizational milestones.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

• Bachelor’s Degree in Systems Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field (or equivalent experience); Master’s preferred

• 8+ years of relevant engineering experience, including substantial responsibility for safety assurance or analysis of safety-critical software in complex electromechanical products

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer

• Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times

• Vision to read printed materials and a computer screen

• Hearing and speech to communicate

The annual salary range is $200,000 - $240,000 base

*This is a direct hire.  Please, no outside Agency solicitations.

Apptronik provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

jobs.title: Design Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE DATA CENTER DESIGN TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

 - Lead the design, development, and execution of 10s to 100s of GWs of data centers this decade.

 - Drive the next generation of liquid cooling and electrical distribution systems.

 - Develop and scale first-of-a-kind modular data centers.

 - Influence behind-the-meter designs and planning for multi-GW campuses.


ROLE SCOPE

 - Own end-to-end project management of concurrent data center design and solution-delivery programs from initiation through construction-ready handoff.

 - Build and maintain integrated master schedules across architectural, structural, MEP, civil, technology, and specialty design disciplines.

 - Establish program governance: milestone gates, design review cadences, change control, and decision logs that create accountability without overhead.

 - Own the template and standard program, build the playbooks, and create the systems that let engineers focus on engineering.

 - Identify risks, interdependencies, and blockers ahead of time so nothing is unforeseen.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c

 - You build integrated master schedules across many design disciplines and hold them.

 - You establish program governance (gates, change control, decision logs) that adds accountability, not bureaucracy.

 - You build playbooks, templates, and systems that let technical teams move faster.

 - You see risks and dependencies before they bite and drive them to resolution.

 - Bonus: Data center or mission-critical design programs. PMP or PgMP. Primavera P6 or MS Project. Owner-side design and engineering PM.


BENEFITS

 - Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

 - Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance.

 - Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.
   

Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

Physical Requirements

 - Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

 - Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.
