jobs.title: Technical Support Engineer, Zero Trust
jobs.description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations: Austin, Texas. You will be expected to work from our Austin office twice a week.

About the Department

The Cloudflare Customer Support Team solves complicated problems and answers technical questions via phone, email, chat and social media. Whether it is a Wordpress blogger using our services for free or a global Enterprise business with petabytes of web traffic, we are always eager to assist. We are the eyes and ears of Cloudflare, acting as the real-time voice of the customer to help communicate their needs and real-world use cases back to the rest of the company - for better service and future product development.

About the role

Do you love solving complex technical issues and interacting with people? Are you passionate about providing premium-level support to customers and are a standout colleague? Cloudflare is seeking an experienced Technical Support Engineer for Zero Trust to join our team. You will work with our largest and most technically sophisticated customers on a variety of technical support issues to ensure they can deploy and operate Cloudflare's Zero Trust solutions with confidence.

Responsibilities

• Serve as a trusted technical advisor, providing advanced support for enterprise customers using Cloudflare’s Zero Trust platform, including products like Access, Gateway, Cloudflare Tunnels, Cloudflare WAN and the Cloudflare One client (formerly known as Cloudflare WARP client).

• Troubleshoot and resolve complex technical issues related to identity, device security, and secure application access.

• Communicating and working directly with the customers via phone, video conference (ie Zoom, Google Meet), chat and tickets in Salesforce

• Work directly with customers to diagnose and remediate configuration and integration challenges with authentication protocols (e.g., SSO, SAML, OIDC) and network security settings.

• Create and maintain knowledge base articles, technical guides, and troubleshooting documentation for internal and customer use.

• Partner with Cloudflare’s Product, Engineering, and Security teams to escalate and resolve advanced customer issues.

• Provide feedback based on customer interactions to drive product improvements and ensure alignment with user needs.

• Assist customers in identifying and responding to security incidents, leveraging Cloudflare’s threat intelligence and security tools.

Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience

• Availability to work the weekend shift (Saturday & Sunday)

• You have a minimum of 3 years experience working as a Support Engineer / Sr. Support Engineer supporting networking or web security products.

• Exceptional troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with the ability to simplify complex concepts for customers.

• Strong customer service orientation and communication skills, both written and verbal.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

• You have experience supporting and troubleshooting multi-factor mechanisms (TOTP, SMS, FIDO, U2F, WebAuth, EMAIL, Push MFA, etc).

• Hands-on experience with identity and access management (IdP, IAM, SCIM) systems, such as Okta, Microsoft Entra, Ping, etc. Strong knowledge of authentication protocols (SAML, OIDC)

• Proficiency in networking fundamentals, including DNS, VPNs, firewalls, and traffic routing.

• Experience supporting cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) and SaaS application integrations.

• You have worked with PostgreSQL, MySQL, MS SQL or other database servers.

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related field (or equivalent experience). This may also include specialized bootcamps.

• Relevant certifications such as Cloudflare Certified Zero Trust Specialist, CISSP, or CCSP.

• Experience with building projects on Cloudflare or using Cloudflare Products.

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1: We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

Please note that applicants who progress to the offer stage of the interview process may be asked to attend an in-person interview within one of the Cloudflare Offices or Cloudflare Hubs.  More details about this will be available at that stage of the interview process.

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations. Please note that any offer of employment may be conditioned on your authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export laws without sponsorship for an export license.

jobs.title: Fiber Engineer
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

FIBER ENGINEER

As a Fiber Engineer at SpaceX, you will work in a complex environment designing and supporting a variety of critical infrastructure. The IT network infrastructure team designs, installs and supports the cable infrastructure used for all types of telecommunications in support of our production facilities, launch infrastructure and spacecraft support systems. This includes the layer 1 fiber and copper data network cabling, operational voice (both wired and wireless systems), video, ground-side vehicle/payload interface RF systems, ground stations, telemetry and optical tracking systems, marine communications, readiness testing, and other systems involved in real-time communications and operations for Falcon, Dragon, Starship, All Recovery Vessels and other missions. Additionally, you will be tasked with designing and overseeing the installation of new cabling infrastructure and processes, with the goal of creating world-class connectivity that can support the mission of enabling life beyond Earth.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Provide engineering support for the design, operation, improvement, and troubleshooting of all fiberoptic and copper supported network infrastructure for multiple IP based systems

• Coordinate downtime activities between maintenance, construction, and production teams to minimize disruptions

• Drive telecommunication projects using design change requests, power monitoring data, and advanced detection methods

• Troubleshoot electrical system problems, conduct breaker coordination, arc flash studies, and track electrical load and capacity

• Coordinate material procurement for large scale projects

• Write, negotiate, and manage construction contracts with subcontractors across multiple disciplines through contract close-out

• Collaborate within interdisciplinary teams to design, optimize, and maintain systems

• Provide telecom engineering support to field technicians to troubleshoot existing equipment

• Oversee equipment installation, operation, and maintenance to meet specified parameters

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• BICSI RCDD (Registered Communications Distribution Designer) certification; or bachelor's degree in a STEM discipline

• 2+ years of experience in industrial electrical engineering and medium or high voltage power systems

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• 5+ years of professional experience with the design or build of commercial or industrial telecommunication systems as LAN/WAN/WIFI/LTE and ISP/OSP structured cabling systems

• Primary experience with structured cabling for high density commercial applications

• Working knowledge of low voltage AC and DC applications required for powering IT and telecom equipment through multiple power sources

• Experience with critical power infrastructure including UPS systems, backup generators, and automatic transfer switches

• Experience creating and implementing process/design solutions with minimal impact to business operations

• Able to quickly assess an issue and assist technicians with troubleshooting and repair instructions

• Ability to work in a high-concentration, high-stress environment, under possible extended work hours and tight deadlines

• Acute attention to detail, ability to see interactions with other systems to avoid problems

• AutoCAD/Revit – beginner to intermediate skill level

• Familiarity with National Electric Code, National Fire Protection Association, and International Building Code

• Understand and ability to design to national cabling standards (ANSI/TIA/BICSI)

• Ability to multi-task, prioritize and work in an extremely fast-paced environment

• Strong understanding of construction project management principles, including scheduling, budgeting, and contractor management

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Physical ability to perform hands-on work in various environments, including heat, cold, rain, and tight quarters

• Must possess or be eligible for Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC)

• Must be able to pass Air Force background checks for Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg

• Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed

Project Morava aims to help build more natural and intelligent voice AI systems by collecting high-quality speech data from native speakers.

- Participate from anywhere within Latvia

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You & the Role

We are hiring a Manufacturing Test Engineer to own electrical, functional, and automated test systems that verify Zipline aircraft, dock, delivery pod, and subassembly hardware at scale. Zipline operates safety-critical autonomous aircraft and logistics systems that deliver medicine and essentials across varied field conditions; production test directly affects fleet uptime, field reliability, and customer deliveries. In this role you will lead end-to-end test system delivery for factory floors that support high-throughput manufacturing and rapid product iterations. You will be expected to prioritize safety, traceability, and measurable improvements in yield and time-to-deploy while working in a fast-scaling production environment with direct consequences for aircraft reliability and delivery network performance.

This opening sits within our manufacturing engineering team; the exact focus will reflect your strengths and the team’s needs. This role is based at Zipline’s South San Francisco manufacturing site, with an onsite-first approach and regular factory-floor presence. Travel to other Zipline sites or vendor locations may be required for launches and validations.

What You’ll Do

• Own assigned electrical, functional, and automated production testers and calibration stations from requirements through internal or vendor build, installation, validation, production release, and sustainment for aircraft, docks, delivery pods, and subassemblies.

• Define test coverage, pass/fail limits, golden-unit strategies, GR&R, capability targets, and release criteria with Design, Firmware, Quality, and Operations.

• Integrate harnesses, DAQ, sensors, actuators, power systems, safety interlocks, and mechanical fixtures to meet throughput and cycle-time needs.

• Build automation and data pipelines using Python, LabVIEW/TestStand, or equivalent tools for reproducible execution, data logging, MES/MFG integration, and dashboards.

• Troubleshoot production escalations on the factory floor under time pressure, including PCBA-level electrical failures, tester instability, fixture issues, software bugs, and product/tester correlation. Distinguish product defects from measurement or tester problems and validate corrective changes before release.

• Improve first-pass yield, false-fail rate, tester uptime, utilization, and per-unit cycle time; set targets and report progress monthly.

• Coordinate assigned launch readiness with Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Technicians, Operations, and vendors, including requirements, validation plans, operator and technician training, calibration schedules, spares, change control, vendor builds, FAT/SAT, and production qualification.

• Evaluate and deploy scalable tester architectures and automation that reduce operator steps, minimize touch time, and standardize interfaces across lines.

• Maintain test procedures, maintenance and calibration plans, validation records, and change-control artifacts required for production readiness and traceability.

What You’ll Bring

• 2+ years building production test systems, automated test equipment, or end-of-line testers for electro-mechanical or mechatronic products is required; demonstrated ownership of multiple shipped tester programs.

• A BS in Electrical, Mechatronics, Mechanical, or Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience.

• Hands-on skill with instrumentation, signal measurement, power delivery, harnessing, connectors, sensors, actuators, and PCBA-level electrical debug.

• Strong test-automation experience: Python preferred; experience with LabVIEW, TestStand, or embedded test frameworks and integrating DAQ, oscilloscopes, DMMs, power supplies, and electronic loads.

• Proficiency with embedded/product interfaces, including CAN, UART, Ethernet, I2C, SPI, and USB, and strategies for validating communications and firmware-hardware interactions.

• A record of improving production metrics such as yield, cycle time, false fails, tester utilization, or GR&R through data-driven technical work, with ownership of metrics reporting.

• Comfort with frequent cross-functional coordination, vendor builds, FAT/SAT, and production qualification.

• Rigorous attention to safety and traceability, decisive technical judgment under production pressure, hands-on test/debug capability, and insistence on measurable outcomes.

• Experience working directly on manufacturing floors during launches and escalations; willingness to spend significant onsite time supporting shifts, debugging, and qualifying equipment.

Nice to Have

• 5–7 years of relevant experience preferred. This is a preference, not an additional minimum requirement.

First-Year Success

• Deliver and validate assigned production tester programs with documented acceptance criteria and production-release evidence.

• Reduce false failures and improve first-pass yield, cycle time, and tester uptime for supported lines against agreed targets.

• Sustain traceable, repeatable test execution and report progress monthly against agreed production goals.

What Else You Need to Know

The starting cash range for this role is $125,000 - $145,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. We are always open to negotiation. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply!

Voluntary Self-Identification

For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - ML Research Engineer, Pre-Training Data
jobs.description:
ABOUT LIQUID AI

Spun out of MIT CSAIL, we build general-purpose AI systems that run efficiently across deployment targets, from data center accelerators to on-device hardware, ensuring low latency, minimal memory usage, privacy, and reliability. We partner with enterprises across consumer electronics, automotive, life sciences, and financial services. We are scaling rapidly and need exceptional people to help us get there.




THE OPPORTUNITY

You'll join the Pre-Training Data team, which decides what Liquid Foundation Models learn from: which data we source, filter, synthesize, and mix, and in what order. Public data sources are plateauing, so model quality increasingly depends on purpose-built datasets and on knowing which data changes actually help.

We treat data as a research problem, not an infrastructure problem. You'll work alongside our pre-training researchers on a small team, run the experiments that settle data questions, and build the pipelines that carry the answers into training runs.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We need someone who:

 - Thinks like a researcher, ships like an engineer: You build the pipelines and you make the model-facing calls about what goes into them. You don't hand off either half.

 - Leads with a hypothesis: Before changing a dataset, you can say what it should do to the model, what you'll measure, and what could fool you, such as contamination or a noisy benchmark. You hold views on pre-training pitfalls, and you test them.

 - Owns problems end to end: You take ambiguous work from open question to shipped result with little direction or process, do the unglamorous parts that get it there, and don't care whose job it was.




THE WORK

 - Source web-scale and public datasets, and build the pipelines that filter, deduplicate, and decontaminate them

 - Design data mixtures and curricula for pre-training and midtraining, and decide what goes into each run

 - Build synthetic data generation systems using LLMs, structured prompting, and distillation to cover what web data can't

 - Run proxy experiments and ablations to measure what each data change does to model quality, and decide what scales up

 - Build evaluation sets you can trust, and keep data lineage clear enough that any training run can be traced and reproduced




EXPERIENCE & CAPABILITIES

What you'll need:

 - Deep, hands-on pre-training data work you did yourself: web-scale sourcing and curation, synthetic data generation, mixing and curriculum design, deduplication and decontamination. This is where depth matters most.

 - The ability to reason from a data decision to its effect on training: how data interacts with model size, architecture, and training dynamics, why more data can hurt, and which changes matter as models scale

 - Experiments you designed to test data changes, such as baselines, scaling ladders, small-scale proxies, and held-out loss, with a clear account of what a change did and why

 - Production data pipelines you built and owned, not only research prototypes

 - Solid ML fundamentals: you've trained, evaluated, and iterated on models in Python (PyTorch preferred)

 - 3+ years of relevant experience with an M.S., 1+ year with a Ph.D., or 5+ years with a B.S.

Helpful, not required:

 - Distillation, long-context, or architecture-specific data strategy

 - Designing evaluation frameworks and benchmarks for pretrained models

 - Data work across both pre-training and post-training

 - Small, efficient models or on-device deployment

 - Startup experience, or a track record of connecting model work to product needs




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (YEAR ONE)

 - You own a critical pre-training data pipeline end to end

 - Data systems you built or improved have measurably moved model performance

 - You've identified and integrated at least one external dataset that moved the needle




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Upstream of every model: Pre-training data shapes every Liquid Foundation Model. On a small team, the mixtures, filters, and synthetic data you build go straight into the models we ship.

 - Compensation & Equity: Competitive base salary plus equity, so you share in what we build. Final offers reflect skills, experience, and location.

 - Time Off: Unlimited PTO, plus company-wide Refill Days, long weekends when the whole company rests together.

 - Health & Wellbeing: Comprehensive health coverage, with details varying by location.

 - Paid Leave: Paid leave for pregnancy, parenting, medical needs, and caring for family.

About You & the Role

jobs.title: A/R Specialist
jobs.description:
Better Companies is a multi-brand financial services organization providing debt relief, tax support, and business funding solutions. We’re strengthening our operations, refining our systems, and building a more cohesive, efficient experience across our brands. Our approach is grounded in transparency, strong operational foundations, and well-structured processes that support reliable execution and scalable growth.

About the Role

Cash flow is the lifeblood of our business, and as our A/R Specialist, you will have complete end-to-end ownership of our order-to-cash process. Operating as our dedicated, single-person accounts receivable powerhouse, you will oversee the full lifecycle from sales order conversion to cash application and subledger close.

Reporting directly to the Accounting Manager, you will serve as the essential bridge connecting Finance, Sales, Billing, Collections, and external lending partners. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, high-trust environment where your contributions are visible and valued. In this role, you will gain hands-on exposure to complex financial cycles like ASC 606 revenue recognition, advanced ERP data architecture, and executive-level reporting—offering you a clear path for professional development and career mobility within our finance organization.

Location: Irvine, CA (Fully In-Office)

Compensation: $41.00 - $46.00 / hour

Job Type: Full-Time (Non-Exempt/Hourly)

What You'll Be Doing

You will balance high-volume transaction processing with high-level reconciliations. Here is how your time will typically be budgeted:

• End-to-End Subledger Ownership & Month-End Close Own the monthly close and reconciliation of the AR subledger within NetSuite, including cash application, unapplied cash, credit memos, write-offs, and bad debt allowance schedules. Prepare detailed supporting schedules and workpapers for the monthly close package and audit preparation. Provide critical AR, billing, and collections data supporting ASC 606 revenue recognition and deferred revenue calculations.

• High-Volume Daily Reconciliations & Cash Flow Tracking Reconcile daily transactions across high-volume merchant processing platforms, special finance entity disbursements, processing fees, ACH transfers, chargebacks, and reserve holdbacks. Match merchant deposits directly against bank statements, investigating batch timing differences, short payments, and discrepancies. Monitor lender portals, reconcile funded disbursements to open receivables, and apply direct wire and cash receipts promptly with complete audit trails.

• Order-to-Billing & Cross-Functional Alignment Manage the order-to-billing pipeline, tracking incoming sales orders and ensuring their conversion into active, billable accounts. Serve as the primary operational contact between Finance, Sales, Collections, Billing, merchant processors, and special finance partners to resolve account inquiries quickly.

• System Optimization & Ad-Hoc Support Act as the internal subject matter expert for the NetSuite AR module, managing customer records, billing schedules, invoices, payments, and saved searches. Troubleshoot module issues alongside NetSuite administrators or consultants to streamline workflows. Partner with the accounting management team on administrative and clerical tasks to maintain smooth operations.

What You Bring

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting (Required) with a solid command of standard accounting principles.

• 5+ years of dedicated accounting experience, with proven success managing an AR subledger end-to-end in a fast-paced, high-volume transaction environment.

• Proven track record reconciling complex merchant processor activity, batch remittances, ACH processing, and chargeback reserves.

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including pivot tables, complex formulas, lookups, and managing large datasets.

• Demonstrated ability to multitask, take initiative on ad-hoc requests, and pivot quickly as operational priorities shift.

• Professional verbal and written communication skills to collaborate effectively across internal teams and external financial partners.

• Hands-on experience navigating NetSuite ERP (customer records, AR module configurations, and custom saved searches) is strongly preferred.

• An active CPA license or progress toward obtaining a CPA is preferred.

• Experience working with third-party consumer lending or special finance entity portals is a plus.

What We Offer

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage options.

• Generous paid time off (PTO) and paid company holidays throughout the year.

• A vibrant team culture featuring regular quarterly social events, team outings, and annual holiday parties.

• 401(k) retirement savings plan options to support your long-term financial health.

• Full autonomy over a vital financial function with direct access to accounting leadership and ongoing exposure to strategic revenue operations.

jobs.title: Project Manager - Facilities
jobs.description:
PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. Victor Peng, our CEO, and co-founder Jeremy O'Brien, now Executive Chairman, lead a team and board that reflects how seriously the world is taking this build, joined this year by Intel's Lip-Bu Tan and Atomico's Niklas Zennström.

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies, including Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical, to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact.

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift, and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we now have the funding, the government validation, and the sites under construction to make it real.

Job Summary:

The Facilities Project Manager organizes, coordinates, and delivers facility construction, renovation, and maintenance projects across one or more sites, ensuring work is completed on time, within budget, and in compliance with safety, environmental, and building regulations. jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description:
About Calm

Calm is the leading mental health brand on a mission to make the world happier and healthier. Known for its flagship consumer app—ranked #1 in its category with over 180 million downloads and availability in ten languages across 190 countries—Calm helps people sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully through content and tools from experts and beloved celebrity voices. Building on this foundation, Calm has created a broader portfolio including evidence-based solutions like Calm Health, offered through employers, health plans and providers, designed to expand access to mental health and sleep support, boost benefits engagement, and drive positive health outcomes. Today, Calm supports more than 3,500 organizations and reaches over 42 million covered lives through Calm Health. Calm has been recognized as a TIME100 Most Influential Company and one of Fast Company’s Brands That Matter. Learn more at calm.com.

What We Do

At Calm we believe in making relaxation, better sleep, and mindfulness accessible to the entire world, and we hope you will help us achieve our mission. The Product & Design team is responsible for delivering Calm to our customers, ensuring that it is easy to use, supports their goals, and maintains a high level of quality across web, iOS, Android platforms.

As a Senior Product Designer on our Consumer team, you'll shape experiences used by tens of millions of people to sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully. People often reach for Calm in their most vulnerable moments, so the craft of what we make (how it looks, moves, and feels) matters enormously.

This is a builder's role in the truest sense: you'll use AI and modern prototyping tools to move from insight to interactive prototype to shipped experience, not as a shortcut on quality, but to spend less time producing and more time on the judgment and detail that make an experience great. When anyone can generate a hundred screens in an afternoon, taste and judgment are the differentiators!

The heart of this role is balancing velocity and craft in service of making our users healthier and happier, and building intuitive, engaging and impactful experiences that drive acquisition, engagement and retention.  You'll partner closely with Product Management, Engineering, Data Science, and Marketing, and set the standard for craft across iOS, Android, and web.  You will be a thought leader in design, helping to establish best practices and setting the bar for exceptional product design at Calm.

What You’ll Do

• Own end-to-end product design initiatives that cover the whole product experience (visual, interaction, motion, brand integration), to create thoughtful, high-quality user-centered mobile experiences.

• Prototype quickly in Figma and with AI and low-code tools like Replit, Lovable, and Claude, so you can get real, testable ideas in front of people early.

• Present your design work clearly and persuasively to cross-functional stakeholders (including senior leadership), give and take feedback well, anchoring your rationale to both user needs and business goals.

• Maintain strong attention to detail and collaboration through engineering implementation (build and QA) and post launch-iterations, to ensure high-quality execution.

• Use data and drive research to inform the experiences you build, and leverage performance insights to evolve your approach.

• Champion system-level thinking (improving how the team works and evolving Calm's design system) so the whole team works faster and smarter.

• Balance multiple projects in a fast-paced environment while maintaining high standards of execution.

Who You Are

• Experienced Product Designer: 7+ years of experience in UX and UI design with 5+ within consumer mobile and web applications.

• AI-native and tooling-fluent: Highly proficient in Figma for design, and already using AI and low-code tools (Replit, Lovable, Claude) to prototype and move fast, with the judgment to know when the output is good enough and when it isn't.

• Technical agility: Comfortable shipping small code changes without engineering support, bridging the gap between design and engineering by personally shipping copy and UI polish directly.

• A builder: Biased toward shipping and iterating over perfect plans. You'd rather put a working prototype in front of people than write a doc about one.

• Data- and research-informed: You fold both qualitative and quantitative insight into your design decisions, and you measure whether the work landed.

• A strong collaborator: A low-ego, trusted partner to Product, Research, and Engineering who makes the people around them better and helps sharpen how the team works.

• High craft standards: A strong advocate for accessibility, consistency, visual storytelling, brand integration, and motion design to create engaging user experiences, while still maintaining velocity.

• A clear communicator: You present your thinking persuasively to stakeholders and senior leadership, give and take feedback well, and champion an experience while staying open to being wrong.

Nice to Haves

• Experience with conversational or AI-native UX.

• Experience working at multiple organizations, ideally including time at a consumer product in a fast-paced startup environment.

• A strong portfolio demonstrating your ability to design and ship beautiful, functional, and user-friendly experiences.

• Comfort shipping small copy and UI changes directly in code, without engineering support.

• A passion for Calm's mission and a point of view on how digital products can support mental health.

Minimum Requirements

• 7+ years in UX/UI design with 5+ within consumer mobile (and web) applications.

• Proven experience driving user testing and research.

• Strong foundation in interaction design, visual design, and usability best practices.

• Experience designing and shipping mobile applications at scale.

• Hands-on proficiency in Figma and modern AI/prototyping tools.

• Ability to work independently while contributing to a larger design vision and strategy.

Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. jobs.title: Senior Technical Recruiter
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:

Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures.

 


WHO WE ARE:

We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy.

 


WHO YOU ARE:

You're not a traditional recruiter, and that's exactly what we're looking for.



You know that hiring exceptional technical talent requires more than posting jobs, running searches, and following established recruiting playbooks. You're creative, resourceful, intellectually curious, and relentless in finding people who are exceptional at what they do, especially when those people are difficult to find and even harder to recruit.



You thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities evolve, ambiguity is the norm, and speed matters. You don't wait for someone to hand you a process or tell you what to do. You figure things out, challenge assumptions, and build better ways of working.



You're a systems thinker who can zoom out to see the bigger picture while obsessing over the details that make a difference. You understand that great recruiting is both an art and a science, combining market intelligence, creative problem-solving, exceptional judgment, and deeply personalized candidate engagement.



You have a high bar for talent and an equally high bar for your own work. You know how to identify rare technical talent, earn the trust of exceptional engineers, and create a white-glove candidate experience that reflects the caliber of the company you're helping build.



Above all, you're energized by the opportunity to help build one of the strongest technical teams in aerospace.




WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Find extraordinary talent. Own full-cycle recruiting for some of our most challenging and business-critical roles, from highly specialized engineers in propulsion, test, and manufacturing to senior technical leaders

 - Go beyond traditional sourcing. Develop creative, unconventional strategies to identify and engage exceptional people who aren't actively looking. Map talent ecosystems, uncover hidden networks, and find candidates others overlook

 - Be a strategic talent partner. Work directly with senior leadership and hiring managers to understand complex technical challenges, define what exceptional talent looks like, and build thoughtful hiring strategies

 - Operate with speed and precision. Move quickly without compromising quality. Anticipate obstacles, solve problems proactively, and create momentum in an environment where hiring exceptional people is a top priority

 - Deliver an exceptional candidate experience. Build authentic relationships with highly sought-after talent through thoughtful, personalized outreach and white-glove engagement. Every interaction should reflect our standards for excellence.

 - Build systems, not just pipelines. Think critically about how we recruit. Identify inefficiencies, experiment with new approaches, and build scalable systems that make us faster, smarter, and more effective

 - Raise the bar. Bring strong judgment and conviction to talent assessment. Challenge assumptions, push for excellence, and help ensure every hire makes the team stronger.

 - Close the hard ones. Understand what motivates exceptional technical talent and craft compelling, individualized approaches to bringing them onboard
   
    


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - 8+ years of recruiting experience, with a track record of hiring exceptional technical talent in fast-growing startups, deep-tech, aerospace, or hardware engineering environments

 - Demonstrated success identifying, engaging, and closing rare, highly sought-after technical talent, particularly in competitive or highly specialized markets

 - A creative, unconventional approach to sourcing and problem-solving. You have examples of searches where you went well beyond traditional recruiting methods to find the right person

 - Strong systems thinking and an instinct for building better processes, tools, and ways of working rather than simply operating within existing ones

 - The ability to thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, exercise independent judgment, and deliver results with minimal direction

 - Exceptional relationship-building skills and the ability to earn credibility with deeply technical candidates, engineering leaders, and executives

 - An obsessive attention to detail and a commitment to delivering a highly personalized, thoughtful candidate experience

 - A high bar for excellence, strong ownership mentality, and genuine pride in your craft

 - A willingness to challenge conventional wisdom, experiment, take calculated risks, and continuously improve

 - Genuine curiosity about aerospace, aviation, and the engineering challenges we're solving
   
    


PERKS & BENEFITS:

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, including Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

 - 401(k) program and transparent stock option plan

 - Self-managed and flexible time-off policy, including PTO, paid holidays, and sick time

 - Flexible work environment
   
    


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role.

Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Contact Technical Recruiter
jobs.description:
About Us

At Arbor Energy & Resources Corporation ("Arbor Energy"), we’re creating technology to power our lives while protecting the planet that sustains them.  Our advanced power systems deliver clean, reliable baseload electricity with zero operating emissions—modular, fuel-flexible, and engineered for the realities of today’s energy demand. At the core is a supercritical CO₂ turbine with integrated carbon capture, designed to bring carbon-neutral power online quickly at meaningful scale.

Our team includes aerospace engineers, combustion experts, and systems thinkers with a shared goal: to build technology worthy of the world we want to live in. While many of us began our journeys looking to the stars, we’re applying that expertise here at home to deliver dependable, emission-free baseload power and a future of lasting abundance.

If you share our values and are drawn to rigorous work with lasting impact, we’d love to learn more about you. Come build what the future will run on.

Steward our planet: We build for tomorrow, ensuring every bolt we tighten and every hand we lend leaves our environment stronger than we found it.

Lead with Love: We champion the success of our people, partners, and planet, nurturing excellence through camaraderie and rigor.

Explore the Uncharted: We embrace the unknown with curiosity, using courage and discipline to transform uncertainty into opportunity.

Role Overview

We are looking for a Contract Technical Recruiter to help build and scale Arbor's engineering team during a critical growth phase.

In this role, you'll focus on full cycle recruiting for complex hardware engineering roles, designing and executing targeted sourcing strategies, engaging passive candidates, and managing the process through offer acceptance.

You’ll work closely with hiring managers and the recruiting team to identify and attract engineers building high-performance systems designed to deliver dependable, emissions-free electricity at scale.

This role is based out of our El Segundo, CA office.

Responsibilities

Search Strategy and Candidate Engagement

• Partner with the talent team and hiring managers to understand role requirements and hiring priorities, translating technical role requirements into effective sourcing and recruiting strategies.

• Build and execute targeted search strategies and talent pipelines for difficult-to-fill technical roles.

• Develop personalized, thoughtful outreach and conduct initial screening conversations with passive technical talent.

Talent Insights and Pipeline Optimization

• Use market insights and competitive talent mapping to refine sourcing strategies.

• Contribute to improving sourcing strategies and recruiting workflows.

• Provide market insights and talent intelligence to shape recruiting decisions.

Team Partnership and Collaboration

• Build trust with hiring managers and the broader team through consistency, responsiveness, and follow-through.

• Communicate clearly and proactively with stakeholders to maintain alignment and momentum across active searches.

• Work collaboratively with the People and Talent team, along with other cross-functional partners to support Arbor’s hiring goals.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree and/or relevant experience.

• 5+ years of technical recruiting experience, with a track record of supporting searches in highly competitive talent markets.

• Must have experience sourcing and recruiting for deep-tech engineering talent from industries such as aerospace, advanced manufacturing, energy systems, or similar.

• Strong research skills and creativity in building candidate pipelines.

• Strong understanding of competitive talent markets and ability to identify relevant target companies and talent pools.

• Highly organized, data-driven, and strong follow-through in a fast-moving environment.

• Excellent written and verbal communication, as well as candidate engagement skills.

• Ability to manage multiple searches simultaneously in a fast-paced environment and remain adaptable to changing priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

• Proven ability to build diverse talent pipelines and connect with candidates from underrepresented backgrounds.

• Comfortable interfacing directly with hiring managers and company leaders.

• Experience supporting early-stage startups or R&D-focused organizations.

Compensation

Base Pay: Contract rate $70.00 - $85.00 USD/hour. The hourly rate is subject to the applicant’s skills, qualifications, and experience.

Our Commitment

Arbor Energy is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, religion, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. Solving global energy challenges requires a wide range of perspectives and experiences, and we are committed to building a team that reflects the world we serve.

Our hiring process is designed to be accessible, fair, and focused on the work that matters most for this role. Reasonable accommodations are available throughout the hiring process and employment—please let us know if you need one.

jobs.title: Process Engineer
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You & the Role

As a Process Engineer, you will turn complex electro-mechanical products into safe, reliable, repeatable production lines for Zipline’s aircraft, docks, and logistics hardware. You will own assigned final assembly and feeder sub-assembly lines from process definition and tooling through validation, production release, and sustainment.

This work connects aerospace-quality manufacturing with reliable field operations and rapid production growth. You will help scale output from tens to thousands of units per week over the next 1–3 years while meeting safety and reliability expectations. Your initial priority is to bring a complex electro-mechanical sub-assembly in-house and validate its production line within months.

This role is based at Zipline’s South San Francisco manufacturing facility, and requires regular on-site presence. Rare travel between sites may be required during ramp and sustainment. Nights or weekends may be needed to support critical production ramps or outages.

What You’ll Do

• Own assigned assembly lines and feeder subassemblies from process definition, tooling, and pilot builds through validation, release, and sustainment.

• Design, procure, install, and commission fixtures, gauges, tooling, workstations, and ergonomic operator flows.

• Define and validate assembly sequences, PFMEAs, control plans, SPC, capability studies, first-article processes, and release criteria.

• Improve first-pass yield, throughput, takt time, equipment reliability, downtime, and cost of poor quality against agreed targets.

• Lead design-for-manufacturing decisions that balance assembly time, inspection, cost, safety, and field reliability.

• Investigate production issues and escapes, validate root causes, and implement corrective and preventive actions.

• Create SOPs, work instructions, and training materials; train and qualify technicians and line leads.

• Coordinate capacity, layouts, equipment, and readiness with Design Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Maintenance, and Operations; deliver a validated pilot line and stabilize production.

What You’ll Bring

• 7+ years of hands-on manufacturing engineering experience with complex electromechanical assembly lines, including experience scaling volume by an order of magnitude.

• A BS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.

• Practical mastery of PFMEA, control plans, SPC, Cp/Cpk, first-article processes, and production validation.

• Experience designing and validating fixtures, jigs, and tooling using 3D CAD; Siemens NX is preferred.

• Experience using MES/ERP and tools such as Minitab, JMP, or Excel to improve yield and process capability.

• End-to-end project ownership, including planning, budgeting, procurement, commissioning, and sustainment with minimal oversight.

• Sound DFM judgment, clear communication, attention to detail, and accountability for safe production and measurable results.

What Else You Need to Know

The starting cash range for this role is $104,000 - $170,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. We are always open to negotiation. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply!

Voluntary Self-Identification

For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

jobs.title: Head of Hardware Engineering
jobs.description:
About Tutor
We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
The Role
Tutor is hiring a Head of Hardware Engineering to lead the team that designs and builds our robots. Mechanical, electrical, firmware and embedded, and manufacturing engineering all report to this role. You set the hardware roadmap with the CTO, you grow the team, and you are responsible for every robot we ship working as designed and building at the rate we need. You report to the CTO.
The hardware organization will grow a lot, in people and in the range of products it covers. The person in this role builds the teams that make that happen, hires the people who lead them, and keeps the whole thing running well as it gets bigger.

jobs.title: Sr Product Manager, Large Ag Autonomy
jobs.description:
We’re Blue River, a team of innovators driven to create intelligent machinery that solves monumental problems for our customers. We empower our customers – farmers, construction crews, and foresters - to implement safer and more sustainable solutions, driving increased profitability with less reliance on scarce labor. We believe that focusing on the small stuff, pixel-by-pixel and task-by-task, leads to big gains.

Blue River Technology works within John Deere’s vision to “innovate on behalf of humanity” by quickly identifying and solving high-value, high-uncertainty challenges in the fields of AI, machine learning, computer vision, and robotics. BRT acts as a research and development flywheel, building not only new products but new platforms that reliably create value for both Deere and its customers. From fully autonomous machines to highly precise farming equipment, BRT & Deere are partnering to create technical breakthroughs across industries like agriculture, construction, and commercial mowing.

Our people are at the heart of what we do. Through cross-disciplinary collaboration, this mission-driven team is eager to define the new frontier of robotics. jobs.title: Process Optimization Manager (Water Treatment)
jobs.description:
Position Purpose:

Lead operational excellence and regulatory strategy across the contract treatment facility portfolio. Combine regulatory expertise with data-driven process operations and management to ensure facilities maintain high standards of compliance and operational effectiveness. Serve as the technical bridge between executive strategy, regulatory requirements, and on-the-ground implementation across multiple projects, driving continuous improvement and empowering operational and water quality compliance teams.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities:

• Technical Guidance: Provide technical consultation on process controls, process troubleshooting, water and wastewater treatment optimization, and regulatory interpretation to elevate the on-the-ground understanding. Key processes to oversee and implement efficiency improvements:Coagulation and flocculation.Oxidation and disinfection.Disinfection byproduct formation.Corrosion control.Distribution water quality.TOC Removal.Sludge management and disposal.Nutrient removal efficiency (wastewater).
• Process Optimization: Conduct and oversee data analytics programs to monitor system performance, identify inefficiencies, and drive operational improvements.
• Regulatory Leadership: Develop and implement regional comprehensive compliance frameworks aligned with our Municipal Services Water Quality and Compliance Team goals, the SDWA, state regulations, and industry best practices. Serve as regional liaison with regulatory agencies, facility operations teams, and executive leadership.
• Continuous Improvement Culture: Instill and lead with a culture of operational excellence across decentralized plant portfolios, steering operational teams to achieve elite, voluntary industry standards like the Area Wide Optimization (AWOP) or Partnership for Safe Water program goals.
• Vendor Collaboration: Partner closely with chemical and equipment suppliers and contractors to evaluate and current treatment technologies that may reduce sludge production, lower chemical consumption, and support O&M budgets.
• Communication Bridging: Deliver technical presentations to executive boards, municipal clients, and on-site utility teams, ensuring all stakeholders are aligned on operational strategies and performance goals.
• Team Collaboration: Network and build relationships with other Municipal Services Teams (e.g. Project Leaders, Technical Leaders, Water Quality and Compliance Directors) to identify gaps, and support implementation at the project level.
• Quality Assurance: Lead, train and support project staff in implementation of the laboratory operations plan (QA/QC), validation of monitoring and reporting protocols and accuracy.
• Strategic Planning: Partner with and assists the Municipal Services Water Quality and Compliance Team on compliance audits, identify skills and gap analyses, and recommend remediation and training initiatives across the facility network.

Work Environment:

• Work is primarily performed in an office and at water and wastewater treatment facilities.
• Occasional travel to facility sites, meetings, and client locations may be required.
• Employees may be exposed to outdoor conditions, industrial equipment, chemicals, and wastewater environments and must follow all applicable safety procedures and use required personal protective equipment.

Education/Experience/Background:

• Bachelor’s degree in a STEM field, such as Environmental Science, Engineering, Chemistry, or a related discipline.
• Minimum 15 years of experience in water/wastewater compliance, regulatory affairs, and technical process operations.
• Experience with data analytics, QA/QC program management, and laboratory oversight.
• Preferred: Advanced degree, such as an MS or MBA; a technical MS is highly preferred.
• Preferred: Background in process operations, engineering, or treatment optimization.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

• Deep knowledge of Safe Drinking Water Act requirements and state and federal regulatory frameworks.
• Demonstrated project management and strategic planning skills.
• Strong communication skills and the ability to translate technical and regulatory concepts for diverse audiences.
• Ability to provide matrix leadership as a technical lead, mentor, and advisor to field operations teams without direct hierarchical authority.
• Preferred: Deep technical expertise in analytical chemistry, laboratory instrumentation data, process control, and data management systems used to optimize active treatment processes.
• Ability to collaborate effectively with regulatory agencies, executive leaders, municipal clients, vendors, contractors, and decentralized facility teams.

Required Certification/Licenses/Training:

• Preferred: Water and wastewater operator licenses, Professional Engineer (PE) license, or other relevant water-industry credentials.

Eligible for up to 10% Annual Performance Bonus

jobs.title: Staff Accountant
jobs.description:
Better Companies is a multi-brand financial services organization providing debt relief, tax support, and business funding solutions. We’re strengthening our operations, refining our systems, and building a more cohesive, efficient experience across our brands. Our approach is grounded in transparency, strong operational foundations, and well-structured processes that support reliable execution and scalable growth.

About the Role

Accurate financials are the foundation of our strategic growth. As our Staff Accountant, you will play a critical role in documenting our financial performance, analyzing data, and ensuring our accounting records are pristine. Reporting directly to the Accounting Manager, you will gain hands-on exposure to everything from month-end close and treasury management to executive reporting and KPI development.

We are committed to your professional development. Whether your goal is to pursue your CPA, advance into a Senior Accountant role, or deepen your analytical expertise, we provide the mentorship and collaborative environment to help you build a long-term career lattice here. We value forward-thinking team players who bring diverse perspectives to our financial operations.

Compensation: $35.00 - $38.00 / hour

Job Type: Full-Time (Non-Exempt/Hourly)

What You'll Be Doing

In this role, priorities can shift rapidly based on reporting cycles, business demands, and strategic needs. Rather than following a rigid routine, you will balance core month-end duties with dynamic cross-departmental projects:

Execute timely balance sheet reconciliations across treasury, revenue, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, intercompany accounts, fixed assets, prepaid expenses, and accrued liabilities. jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Methodologies
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TILT TEAM

At Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. Our mobile-first products and machine learning-powered credit models look beyond credit scores, using over 250 real-time financial signals to recognize real potential. With millions of customers worldwide, we're not just changing how people access financial products — we're creating a new credit system that backs the working, whatever they're working toward.


THE OPPORTUNITY

At Tilt, we're constantly exploring new ways to understand financial behavior and reduce risk. The work you do in this role will go directly into the foundational models we're building for our products.

We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our Methodologies group — a role focused on building and advancing foundational modeling approaches. You'll build and test deep learning methods such as transformers to improve how we understand financial data and make lending decisions.

This is a great role for someone who's deeply curious about new modeling techniques and wants to see their ideas make a real difference. You'll work with a small, experienced team of data scientists and engineers, taking projects from first idea to working model on financial data challenges — from credit decisioning to customer behavior!

You'll also be at the forefront of how data science is practiced in the age of AI agents. Our team builds with agentic tools every day, and you'll use them in your own work and help build the specialized agents that speed up both DS and business workflows.

We're looking for someone who enjoys learning, experimenting, and collaborating — a person who can connect technical exploration to meaningful business impact. If you're excited by applying new methodologies in ways that help people access fairer credit, you'll fit right in.



HOW YOU'LL MAKE AN IMPACT

 - Build, train and evaluate deep learning models on Tilt's financial data.

 - Ship models and model components that plug into Tilt's existing ML pipelines to improve credit modeling and loss prediction.

 - Own your projects end to end, from hypothesis to a model in use, with general direction from the team's leads.

 - Work closely with data scientists, engineers, and product partners to turn your results into practical solutions.

 - Run representation learning experiments — including pretraining and fine-tuning — on real financial data, with a clear design up front and an honest read on what worked.

 - Share findings and help peers pick up new deep learning methods.

 - Measure the impact of your models not just by accuracy, but by how they improve outcomes for Tilt's customers and partners.

 - Use agentic development tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex) to speed up experimentation, feature engineering and model iteration.

 - Build and improve specialized agents that support DS workflows.
   


WHY YOU'RE A GREAT FIT

 - Hands-on experience building and training deep learning models

 - Comfort working with modern ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar).

 - Experience applying ML to real-world problems, ideally in financial services (credit, lending, payments, or banking).

 - Experience taking a project from an open question to a measurable business outcome.

 - Clear, thoughtful communication — you can explain technical ideas in ways others can engage with.

 - Bonus: hands-on experience building with LLMs or agent frameworks, or excitement to learn. You see agents as a way to multiply what a small, senior team can do.



Don’t meet every qualification? We care about potential over your past. If you're bringing ambition and drive to what we're building, we want to hear from you.





WHAT YOU'LL GET AT TILT

 - Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.

 - Competitive pay: We're big on potential, and it's reflected in our competitive compensation packages and generous equity.

 - Complete support: Find flexible health plans at every premium level, and substantial subsidies that stand up to global standards.

 - Visibility is yours: You can count on direct exposure to our leadership team — we’re a team where good ideas travel quickly.

 - Paid global onsites: Magic happens IRL: we gather twice yearly to reconnect over shared meals or kayaking adventures. (We’ve visited Vail, San Diego, and Mexico City, to name a few.)

 - Impact is recognized: Growth opportunities follow your contributions, not rigid promotion timelines.


THE TILT WAY

We're looking for people who chase excellence and impact. Those who stand behind their work, celebrating the wins and learning from the missteps equally. We foster an environment where every voice is valued and mutual respect is non-negotiable — brilliant jerks need not apply. We're in this together, working to expand access to fair credit and prove that people are incredible. When you join us, it's not just another day at the [virtual] office, you're helping millions of hardworking people reach better financial futures.



You’re pushing ahead in your career? We can get behind that. Join us in building the credit system that people deserve.

jobs.title: Unit Coordinator K2
jobs.description:
Nestled in San Francisco's Excelsior neighborhood on a nine-acre campus, the San Francisco Campus for Jewish Living (SFCJL) is the leading senior services organization in Northern California. Our continuum of care includes: the Frank Residences assisted living and memory care; the Jewish Home and Rehabilitation Center, offering long-term skilled nursing, short-term rehabilitation, an acute geriatric psychiatric unit for adults over the age of 65; and our Foundation.

Founded in 1871 and formerly known as the Jewish Home, our legacy grounds us as our vision propels us forward. Today, we've evolved to support more than 2,500 older adults each year through innovative, comprehensive programs rooted in the Jewish values of compassion, community, and excellence. We are equally proud of our inclusive culture, where 950 team members of diverse faiths and backgrounds work together in shared purpose.

WHY WORK WITH US

• Mission-driven nonprofit organization

• Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits

• Meaningful work that positively impacts the lives of older adults every day

• Inclusive community, welcoming to all (you do not need to be Jewish to live or work here)

• Supportive, team-oriented environment

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

• Collaborative leadership focused on enhancing the employee experience
