jobs.title: Material Flow Engineer
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Role

As a Material Flow Engineer on the Manufacturing Engineering team, you will design the factory layouts, work methods, and capacity models that enable Zipline to scale production reliably.

You will connect demand, labor, equipment, space, and capital investment through time studies, standard work, line balancing, and production-system design. Working directly on the factory floor, you will turn observations and production data into practical changes to station loading, operator movement, layouts, and manufacturing capacity.

Your work will help the team determine how much we can build, where the constraints are, and which investments in people, equipment, automation, or space will support the next stage of production.

This role is based in South San Francisco. This opening sits within our manufacturing engineering team; the exact focus will reflect your strengths and the team’s needs.

What You’ll Do

• Improve factory layouts, workstations, operator movement, and material presentation.

• Define WIP, buffer, queue, and rework strategies that protect output while reducing inventory and lead time.

• Partner with Manufacturing, Production, Supply Chain, and Material Planning on line architecture, lineside availability, and replenishment.

• Lead time studies, define standard work and labor models, and balance station loading against takt time.

• Build capacity and capital-investment scenarios for labor, equipment, tooling, shifts, floor space, and future demand.

• Identify current and future bottlenecks and implement improvements in throughput, utilization, cycle time, labor efficiency, and cost.

• Own factory performance and production-system design, connecting individual processes into an efficient end-to-end system.

• Develop factory KPIs, decision tools, make-versus-buy analyses, and investment cases; carry improvements through implementation.

What You’ll Bring

• A bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations Research, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.

• 3+ years in industrial engineering, manufacturing engineering, operations engineering, production systems, or a comparable environment.

• Experience with time studies, labor and capacity models, line balancing, takt time, standard work, factory layouts, and material flow.

• A record of identifying manufacturing constraints and improving throughput, productivity, utilization, lead time, or cost.

• Strong spreadsheet and analytical skills, including work with ERP, MES, labor-tracking, and production data.

• Ability to build operational and financial models for capital investment, automation, make-versus-buy, and factory scaling.

• A hands-on approach, clear communication, and ownership of improvements from ambiguous problemx through implementation

Nice to Have

• 5–7 years of relevant experience.

• Experience scaling complex electromechanical products, expanding factories, or launching new production lines.

• Familiarity with simulation, optimization, SQL, Python, BI tools, manufacturing dashboards, or ERP/MES platforms.

• Experience with Lean manufacturing, Theory of Constraints, PFMEA, value-stream mapping, or automation business cases.

What Else You Need to Know

The starting cash range for this role is $104,000 - $170,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. We are always open to negotiation. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

jobs.title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer
jobs.description:
We’re ALTEN Technology USA, an engineering company helping clients bring groundbreaking ideas to life—from advancing space exploration and life-saving medical devices to building autonomous electric vehicles. With 3,000+ experts across North America, we partner with leading companies in aerospace, medical devices, robotics, automotive, commercial vehicles, EVs, rail, and more.

As part of the global ALTEN Group—57,000+ engineers in 30 countries—we deliver across the entire product development cycle, from consulting to full project outsourcing.

When you join ALTEN Technology USA, you’ll collaborate on some of the world’s toughest engineering challenges, supported by mentorship, career growth opportunities, and comprehensive benefits. We take pride in fostering a culture where employees feel valued, supported, and inspired to grow.

We’re seeking a Senior Embedded Software Engineer to develop the firmware and embedded software layer that sits between our aircraft and ground asset hardware and the higher-level software stack. Working across microcontrollers, embedded Linux, and the buses and peripherals that connect them, you'll bring up new hardware, own the drivers and firmware that make sensors and actuators reliable, and harden the embedded systems our delivery ecosystem depends on for every flight.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with real ownership: you'll own embedded subsystems end-to-end, from board bring up through flight test and regulated change control, working closely with Electrical, Mechanical, and Onboard Software teams. In this role, you will:

• Design, build, test, and maintain firmware and embedded software for Matternet's aircraft and station embedded systems, spanning microcontroller firmware and embedded Linux on ARM

• Own the hardware/software boundary: bring up new boards and peripherals, write and debug device drivers, and integrate sensors and peripherals (e.g. encoders, motors, IMUs, LIDAR/RADAR, and similar)

• Select and integrate microcontrollers, communication buses (CAN, SPI, I2C, UART, BLE), and peripherals appropriate for new features and hardware revisions

• Drive embedded software verification and release, from bench and simulation testing through flight test and deployment across production fleets

• Debug at the hardware/software boundary when needed, including hands-on use of oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, and reviewing board-level schematics and datasheets with Electrical Engineering

• Provide senior technical support, triaging and resolving field and flight-test issues tied to embedded subsystems Sensitivity: C1-Internal

• Collaborate with stakeholders across Electrical, Mechanical, Onboard Software, Operations, Safety, and Production Requirements

• 6+ years of production embedded software/firmware engineering

• Strong C/C++ design and programming skills, with solid software engineering practice across the hardware/software/network development lifecycle (code review, source control, build systems, test-driven development, static analysis)

• Proficiency with embedded Linux for ARM (kernel, device drivers, board support) as well as bare-metal/RTOS firmware development

• Deep functional knowledge of communication protocols (CAN, SPI, I2C, UART, BLE) and experience selecting the right protocol and hardware for a given application • Experience selecting microcontrollers and bringing up new peripherals, sensors, and actuators (motors, encoders, and similar)

• Comfortable reading board-level schematics and datasheets, and debugging at the signal level using oscilloscopes and/or logic analyzers

• Proficiency with version control and peer code review workflows (e.g., Git)

• Excellent technical communication and strong cross-disciplinary teamwork in a fast-paced environment Preferred Qualifications:

• UAV, autonomous robotics, aerospace, or other safety-critical regulated experience

• Experience with Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS)

• Familiarity with an autopilot stack such as ArduPilot or PX4, and UAV/avionics technologies (ADS-B, GPS/GNSS, LIDAR, perception sensors)

• Experience with build systems such as CMake, Make, or Waf, and containerized build/test environments (Docker)

• Experience optimizing C/C++ algorithms for high data throughput

• Experience using AI coding assistants to accelerate development

jobs.title: Manager, Revenue Accounting
jobs.description:
At Anaplan, we are a team of innovators focused on optimizing business decision-making through our leading AI-infused scenario planning and analysis platform so our customers can outpace their competition and the market.

What unites Anaplanners across teams and geographies is our collective commitment to our customers’ success and to our Winning Culture.

Our customers rank among the who’s who in the Fortune 50. Coca-Cola, LinkedIn, Adobe, LVMH and Bayer are just a few of the 2,400+ global companies who rely on our best-in-class platform.

Our Winning Culture is the engine that drives our teams of innovators. We champion diversity of thought and ideas, we behave like leaders regardless of title, we are committed to achieving ambitious goals, and we love celebrating our wins – big and small.

Supported by operating principles of being strategy-led, values-based and disciplined in execution, you’ll be inspired, connected, developed and rewarded here. Everything that makes you unique is welcome; join us and let’s build what’s next - together!

Join our revenue accounting team as Manager, Revenue Accounting. In this role, you will serve as a subject matter expert on ASC 606 technical accounting and manage the subscription revenue process, ensuring rigorous revenue recognition compliance, reviewing complex customer contracts, and supporting our month-end financial close.

You will partner directly with Deal Desk, Sales Operations, and Legal on non-standard enterprise deals, identifying technical accounting considerations and helping structure contract terms to protect revenue and billings.

This role focuses on technical accounting governance and subscription revenue process management. You will author audit-ready technical memos for new revenue streams and products, oversee complex revenue recognition and billing schedules, maintain and update standalone selling price (SSP) allocation models, and evaluate accounting treatment for contract modifications and emerging hybrid/usage pricing models. You will also serve as the primary technical liaison for our external audit team.

This position suits an experienced, detail-oriented technical accountant with strong Big 4 or public SaaS experience who enjoys in-depth contract analysis, rigorous accounting close, and cross-functional deal advisory.

Your Impact

• Month-End Revenue Close Oversight: Oversee monthly revenue close deliverables, including complex revenue schedules, contract assets, deferred revenue rollforwards, customer contract liability reconciliations, bad debt reconciliation, and related journal entries.

• Period-End Commercial Reporting & ASC 606 Disclosures: Lead the preparation, review, and reconciliation of period-end reporting packages for revenue metrics including billings, deferred revenue, and revenue backlog.

• ASC 606 Technical Accounting Memos: Author formal technical accounting position papers documenting revenue recognition treatment for complex multi-element arrangements, non-standard terms, and emerging product offerings in accordance with ASC 606.

• Cross-Functional Deal Advisory: Serve as a technical accounting partner to Deal Desk, Sales and Legal, collaborating regularly during active deal negotiations to provide clear accounting guidance on deal structuring and the implications of non-standard commercial terms such as custom SLAs, acceptance provisions, and termination rights.

• Contract Processing: Process subscription contracts, including contract modifications, ensuring adherence to the revenue guidance and internal bookings policy.

• Standalone Selling Price (SSP) Analysis: Perform annual Standalone Selling Price (SSP) analyses across software subscription tiers, professional services, and usage components, maintaining documented transaction price allocation methodologies.

• External Audit Management: Serve as the primary contact for external auditors on all revenue accounting matters, manage technical PBC requests, lead audit walkthroughs, and defend accounting positions.

• SOX Controls & Financial Governance: Design, maintain, and execute internal controls (SOX) over the OTC process, including contract review, multi-element revenue allocations, and close reconciliations.

• Hybrid & Consumption Accounting Evaluation: Evaluate technical accounting treatment for evolving commercial models, such as minimum commitments, usage-based fees, and prepaid drawdowns, establishing appropriate recognition timing and variable consideration estimates.

Your Qualifications

• Experience: 6 years of progressive accounting experience, with at least 3 years dedicated to technical revenue accounting under ASC 606 in SaaS or enterprise technology environments.

• Education & Credentials: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting; active Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license is preferred; Big 4 experience and national public accounting experience strongly preferred.

• Technical ASC 606 Mastery: Deep command of the ASC 606 5-step framework, distinct performance obligation identification, transaction price allocation (SSP), and contract modification accounting.

• Close Accounting & Balance Sheet Rigor: Hands-on experience managing monthly revenue close, including deferred revenue rollforwards, contract asset/liability reconciliations, and review of complex revenue subledger schedules.

• Complex Contract Analysis: Demonstrated ability to dissect multi-element enterprise contracts, identify non-standard clauses, assess revenue recognition impacts, and communicate those impacts to Commercial Operations.

• Systems & Tooling: Working knowledge of enterprise ERP and revenue management systems (Workday), Salesforce CPQ, and financial modeling in Excel; Anaplan familiarity is a plus.

• Professional Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate technical accounting standards and risks clearly to finance leadership, legal counsel, and commercial teams.

#LI-SP1

$91,000—$130,000 USD

jobs.description:
Join Horace Mann: Empower Educators, Achieve Financial Success

Ready to Make a Difference?

Join Horace Mann today and take the first step toward achieving your career and financial goals while making a meaningful impact on the educators you serve. Together, we can help educators secure their future while empowering you to achieve your own.

jobs.title: Operations Engineer
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Role

As an Operations Engineer on Manufacturing Engineering, you will connect demand, output, staffing, shifts, equipment, space, material flow, process capability, and capital investment. Working with production teams on the factory floor, you will make constraints visible, improve flow, and help leaders scale capacity deliberately.

You will turn production goals into practical factory plans, remove bottlenecks, implement improvements, and establish operating routines that support timely corrective action. Your work will help manufacturing leaders match capacity to demand and sustain improvements in throughput, utilization, lead time, and cost.

What You’ll Do

• Build capacity and capital-investment scenarios for labor, equipment, tooling, shifts, floor space, and future demand.

• Identify current and future bottlenecks and implement improvements in throughput, utilization, cycle time, labor efficiency, and cost.

• Lead time studies, define standard work and labor models, and balance station loading against takt time.

• Own factory performance and production-system design, connecting individual processes into an efficient end-to-end system.

• Improve factory layouts, workstations, operator movement, and material presentation.

• Define WIP, buffer, queue, and rework strategies that protect output while reducing inventory and lead time.

• Partner with Manufacturing, Production, Supply Chain, and Material Planning on line architecture, lineside availability, and replenishment.

• Develop factory KPIs, decision tools, make-versus-buy analyses, and investment cases; carry improvements through implementation.

What You’ll Bring

• A bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations Research, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.

• 3+ years in industrial engineering, manufacturing engineering, operations engineering, production systems, or a comparable environment.

• Experience with time studies, labor and capacity models, line balancing, takt time, standard work, factory layouts, and material flow.

• A record of identifying manufacturing constraints and improving throughput, productivity, utilization, lead time, or cost.

• Strong spreadsheet and analytical skills, including work with ERP, MES, labor-tracking, and production data.

• Ability to build operational and financial models for capital investment, automation, make-versus-buy, and factory scaling.

• A hands-on approach, clear communication, and ownership of improvements from ambiguous problem through implementation

Nice to Have

• 5–7 years of relevant experience.

• Experience scaling complex electromechanical products, expanding factories, or launching new production lines.

• Familiarity with simulation, optimization, SQL, Python, BI tools, manufacturing dashboards, or ERP/MES platforms.

• Experience with Lean manufacturing, Theory of Constraints, PFMEA, value-stream mapping, or automation business cases.

What Else You Need to Know

The starting cash range for this role is $104,000 - $170,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. We are always open to negotiation. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply!

jobs.title: Senior FPGA Development Engineer
jobs.description:
Radar Reinvented.

Echodyne offers the world’s first compact solid-state true beam-steering radar for a wide range of industries and applications. Our high-performance radars work in all weather and are designed for autonomous vehicles, uncrewed aircraft & drones, and security of borders, critical infrastructure, and smart cities. The company combines the patented technology of metamaterials with powerful software to create a radar sensor with unprecedented performance at commercial price points. Echodyne offers its radars to companies working in Automotive, Transportation, Critical Infrastructure Protection, Border Security, Smart Cities, Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS), and Airspace Management including Urban Air Mobility (UTM).

Echodyne is seeking a Senior FPGA Development Engineer – Design and produce radar equipment subsystems composed of Echodyne’s industry-leading radars.

ROLE OVERVIEW

In this role, you will engage with an experienced cross-disciplinary team to create radar systems solutions thought high-performance, secure software solutions.

You will work closely with colleagues to design and build FPGA solutions, mentor junior engineers, and play a key role in shaping the HDL development practices of the team. This role demands technical ownership, systems knowledge, and a strong quality embedded development mindset. You must be responsive, flexible, and able to succeed within a collaborative and fast-paced environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Architect, design, implement, integrate, and test FPGA-based solutions.

• Write efficient, robust, timing optimized, and maintainable VHDL/Verilog code.

• Take responsibility and assume ownership for tasks; seeking guidance when needed.

• Develop and execute a plan of action based on design requirements and constraints.

• Hold and participate in design reviews and peer reviews.

• Work with and support team members, both technical and non-technical. Representing yourself to others with a high level of integrity and professionalism.

• Drive improvements to coding practices and tools across engineering.

• Design and develop reusable cross platform architectures and frameworks.

• Help drive and support testing efforts across teams and projects.

• Work alongside radar, signal processing, and software engineers to implement platform functionality to meet specific system control and signal processing needs.

• Mentor and provide technical direction to junior developers.

REQUIRED SKILLS / EXPERIENCE

• Proficient at communicating your ideas, plans and designs to teammates.

• Skilled at delineating scope, preparing work plans, resolving design conflicts, and overseeing design implementation steps.

• Solid understanding of FPGA architectures (DSP, SoC), their hardware/software interfaces, and memory interfaces (DDR, SRAM, Flash).

• Experienced user of FPGA design tools and methodologies, including: simulators and static code analyzers. Specifically: Vivado, Quartus, QuestaSim, Blue Pearl, design documentation software, configuration management software (JIRA), and version control software (Git).

• Embedded systems debugging, troubleshooting, and code-testing knowledge using JTAG debuggers, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multi-meters, spectrum analyzers.

• Knowledge of Python, tcl, or other scripting languages for development and testing automation.

• Knowledge of software development life cycle, and good coding practices

• Interfacing embedded systems to host computers and peripherals, using common communications protocols (UART, SPI, QSPI, I2C, TCP/UDP IP)

• Experience with common interfaces such as: AXI, AXI-Stream.

DESIRED SKILLS / EXPERIENCE
(Looking for one or more as a complement to the core skills)

• Experience with one or more high speed interfaces (CML, LVDS, JESD, SERDES, Ethernet/UDP, Aurora, PCI-E)

• Working DSP knowledge including: developing HDL for Radar, Electronic Warfare, Cellular, or other Wireless Technology.

• Experience in fixed-point math, implementation, tradeoffs, and modeling (Matlab or scipy is a plus).

• Capable of leading a project team of three or more engineers within the discipline or across disciplines.

• Familiar with continuous integration, HIL testing, and Agentic AI workflows.

QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor of Science degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science or equivalent military / industry experience

• 5+ years of designing, implementing, building, integrate and testing Verilog/System Verilog and VHDL software solutions.

• Working knowledge of hardware/PCB design and embedded software and verification.

Echodyne’s technology is export controlled by the U.S. Government and we must evaluate an applicant’s eligibility to handle export-controlled information or obtain required Government authorizations.  Therefore, we will ask you as part of the application process to identify whether you are a U.S. Citizen or green card holder, or have asylum/refugee status in the U.S.

WHAT WE OFFER

This is an exempt role.
The salary range for this position is $137,196 - $205,382 per year.

If your skills generally align but not perfectly, please apply anyway. There may be another role that’s a great fit for you!

jobs.title: Human Resources Coordinator (Employee Relations)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

HUMAN RESOURCES COORDINATOR (EMPLOYEE RELATIONS)

As a Human Resources Coordinator, you will be responsible for supporting a diverse employee population with crucial services for the full employee life cycle. This position will assist with employee onboarding, HRIS administration, and partnering with the HR team to implement both local and company-wide programs. Success in this role requires superior internal and external customer service, attention to detail, and ability to thrive in a fast-paced and constantly changing environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Support the HR team in employee relations investigations and conflict resolution

• Maintain our HRIS for all employee life-cycle processes

• Respond to employee inquiries, questions and concerns

• Provide information, guidance and direction on HR policies, programs, and processes to employees and managers

• Serve as the onboarding point of contact for the new hire program and support new employees’ transition into SpaceX

• Ensure employee electronic files are accurate and updated, and assist with HR reporting and audit requests

• Assist with the creation, documentation, and implementation of human resources policies, programs, and processes

• Respond to initial unemployment claims and employment verifications

• Provide support to the HR team and deliver core HR services to the workforce

• Assist HR team in identifying department needs, recommending changes, and implementing improvements

• Facilitate site-wide events, such as benefits fairs, volunteer efforts, and team celebrations

• Support the recruitment team with staffing-related support activities

• Maintain standards of strict confidentiality with respect to all matters and documents

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree

• 6+ months of administrative experience (internship experience qualifies)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• 3.5 GPA or higher

• 1+ years of intern or professional experience in a human resources role

• Basic understanding of labor laws and an interest in keeping up with trends and updates in HR

• Demonstrated excellence thriving in a fast-paced environment and embracing change

• Experience using Workday, Greenhouse, and UltiPro is highly preferred

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail

• Experience in HR operations capacity

• Ability to collaborate in a team environment and pitch in as needed

• Ability to work with employees and managers at all levels of the organization

• Customer service-oriented approach to all requests, with a focus on accuracy and timeliness

• Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills

• Experience using PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, and Excel

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• This is not a remote or hybrid position and will require relocation if not already local to the Vandenberg, CA area

• Position requires ability to work overtime hours and/or weekends when needed

• Must be willing to travel to other SpaceX locations (up to 25%)

• Ability to pass Air Force background checks for Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:

Level 1: $27.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

Hometap is hiring a Contract Recruiting Specialist to support the day-to-day operations of our recruiting team. • Communicate interview logistics and expectations to candidates and interviewers

• Draft sourcing messages and research creative ways to reach and attract talent

Recruiting operations

• Assist with the onboarding, configuration, and maintenance of current and new recruiting tools

• Serve as the main point of contact for new hires during onboarding, tracking task completion and answering questions

• Organizational skills to manage multiple schedules, priorities, and requests at once

• Comfort with data entry, reporting, and using spreadsheets to track and analyze information

• Strong attention to detail and a proactive approach to solving problems

• Curiosity that shows up in good questions and a willingness to raise flags when something looks off

• Willingness to learn new systems and tools quickly; experience with AI-assisted scheduling tools such as Goodtime or Guide is a plus

jobs.title: Summer Camp Director, Chicago - West Loop (2027)
jobs.location: Chicago - West Loop, IL, United States
jobs.description:
Galileo is looking for an experienced leader to join our team as a Camp Director. Camp Directors lead our dynamic summer camps for K–8th grade, serving as both site General Manager and the public face of the organization.

You will open and operate a Camp Galileo location serving campers and their families within your community! You will lead a dynamic seasonal team of educators as well as enthusiastic entry-level staff to create joyful, safe environments and ensure smooth daily operations. With a focus on exceptional camper and family experiences, you will uphold program quality, foster creativity, and deliver excellence in customer care, curriculum, and team leadership.

Why This Role Matters

Galileo started in 2002 with a single summer camp in Palo Alto, named for Galileo Galilei, one of history’s great innovators. Today we run 90+ sites across eight states, and Camp Directors are still the people who give each camp its own traditions and magic. Our mission is to develop innovators who envision and create a better world, and at camp, you’re the one who makes that real for campers, families, and staff every day.

You will be Accountable for

Bringing Galileo’s Spirit to Life

• Infuse camp with joy, tradition, and creativity

• Build an inclusive environment where every camper, staff member, and family feels seen, supported, and inspired

Leading with Ownership and Vision

• Own every aspect of your camp’s launch, from preseason planning through end-of-summer wrap-up

• As both operational lead and culture builder, oversee every detail from daily camp operations to parent communication while delivering an exceptional program

Keeping Camp Safe and Running Smoothly

• Prioritize camper safety, family trust, and program fidelity at all times

• Anticipate needs, adapt quickly, and problem-solve on the fly so camp runs seamlessly, even when things don’t go as planned

Developing and Managing Your Team

• Train and mentor a staff of 7 to 40 (depending on site size), including educators and entry-level staff, while actively building your team culture

• Provide clear expectations for instructional and program standards, ongoing feedback, and professional development

• Own core management responsibilities such as training support, scheduling, payroll, and ongoing performance management

Embracing Challenge and Innovation

• Use the Galileo Innovation Approach (GIA) to encourage curiosity and problem-solving

• Lead your team in turning challenges into opportunities, keeping both spirit and operations aligned to Galileo’s mission

• Communicate openly with your Field Program Manager, seek out feedback, and turn it into action

• Take ownership of your own professional development, staying self-motivated to learn, grow, and improve throughout the summer

Building Strong Partnerships

• Serve as the primary face of camp within the community

• Communicate proactively with families, facilities partners, and cross-functional teams

• Collaborate with your Field Program Manager and cultivate trust with community partners, staff, and campers

Location & Work Schedule:

This is a seasonal role running March–September 2027, with a schedule divided into three phases. Exact dates will vary based on hire date and specific site operating dates:

• Phase One: Training & Prep (March–June): 5 to 15 hours per week, depending on tenure and start date — mostly flexible and remote, with some required scheduled and in-person commitments. This phase includes in-person training(s), a Bay Area retreat, scheduled virtual training(s), marketing events, and on-site prep at your camp location during the week leading up to camp. Some events may take place during evenings and weekends.

• Phase Two: On-Site (June–August): On-site hours typically range from 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM (M-F), up to 50 hours per week over 5–8 weeks, depending on camp placement.

• Phase Three: Wrap-Up (Aug–Sept): Up to 5 hrs total, remote, for final admin tasks and staff reviews.

Compensation:

(Year 1 estimate):

• Preseason (Feb–June): Earn hourly pay ($22-24/hour) for flexible, part-time prep and training

• Camp Season (June–Aug): Transition to a weekly salary ($1,400/week plus an additional $50/week for each year of returning tenure in this role) as a full-time, exempt Camp Director during summer operations

• Postseason (Aug–Sept): Wrap up with light part-time work, paid hourly ($22-24/hour)

• Bonus/Commission: Earn an additional $1 per camper-week enrollment, plus potential commission for add-on weeks

Exact compensation may vary and will be based on multiple factors, including geography and Galileo camp director tenure. Our pay practices are guided by a commitment to equity and informed by market benchmarking and internal audits to minimize bias and ensure fairness across all roles.

Perks:

• Free camp for your child(ren) or two giftable weeks (incl. extended care)

• 15% Friends & Family discount

• Priority nomination for financial assistance for someone you know

• 3+ years of experience working directly with students in an education setting (out-of-school time, teaching, education administration, camps/recreation, etc.) is required

• Minimum 1 year of experience managing or supervising adult staff is required

• Proven experience creating safe, inclusive environments for children and building trust with families

• Proven experience setting clear expectations, giving ongoing feedback, and coaching staff to improve

• Demonstrated ability to manage operational details like scheduling, staffing, and payroll

• Track record of staying calm and making sound decisions in fast-paced situations, including safety issues and challenging conversations with families

• Strong written and verbal communication with families, partners, and supervisors

• Experience with hands-on, project-based learning (STEAM, art, design, maker programs) is a plus

• Availability for part-time remote work starting Feb 2026, and full-time on-site work starting June 2026 (dates vary by location)

• Willingness to travel in the region to up to 3 in person marketing events, in the preseason

• Ability to complete all required training before camp begins

• Ability to meet state requirements to work with children, including mandated screenings and Adult & Child First Aid/CPR/AED certification

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences. If you think you have what it takes to be successful in this role, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Industrial Engineer
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Role

As an Industrial Engineer on the Manufacturing Engineering team, you will design the factory layouts, work methods, and capacity models that enable Zipline to scale production reliably.

You will connect demand, labor, equipment, space, and capital investment through time studies, standard work, line balancing, and production-system design. Working directly on the factory floor, you will turn observations and production data into practical changes to station loading, operator movement, layouts, and manufacturing capacity.

Your work will help the team determine how much we can build, where the constraints are, and which investments in people, equipment, automation, or space will support the next stage of production.

What You'll Do

• Own factory performance and production-system design, connecting individual processes into an efficient end-to-end system.

• Improve factory layouts, workstations, operator movement, and material presentation.

• Lead time studies, define standard work and labor models, and balance station loading against takt time.

• Build capacity and capital-investment scenarios for labor, equipment, tooling, shifts, floor space, and future demand.

• Identify current and future bottlenecks and implement improvements in throughput, utilization, cycle time, labor efficiency, and cost.

• Define WIP, buffer, queue, and rework strategies that protect output while reducing inventory and lead time.

• Partner with Manufacturing, Production, Supply Chain, and Material Planning on line architecture, lineside availability, and replenishment.

• Develop factory KPIs, decision tools, make-versus-buy analyses, and investment cases; carry improvements through implementation.

What You'll Bring

• Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations Research, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.

• 2+ years of experience in industrial engineering, manufacturing engineering, operations engineering, production systems, or a comparable environment.

• Strong understanding of production system design, capacity planning, line balancing, takt time, cycle-time analysis, standard work, and manufacturing flow.

• Demonstrated experience performing time studies and translating observations into labor and capacity models.

• Experience designing or improving manufacturing layouts and material-flow systems.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to turn imperfect production data into clear engineering and business decisions.

• Experience identifying manufacturing constraints and driving improvements in throughput, productivity, utilization, lead time, or cost.

• Ability to build financial and operational models that support CapEx, automation, make/buy, and factory-scaling decisions.

• Strong spreadsheet and data-analysis skills; comfort working with manufacturing data from ERP, MES, labor-tracking, and production systems.

• Ability to work directly on the factory floor, understand how production actually operates, and collaborate effectively with technicians, manufacturing engineers, production leaders, quality engineers, supply chain, and design engineering.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to convert complex analysis into simple recommendations and executable plans.

• A high degree of ownership. You are comfortable identifying an ambiguous factory-level problem, defining what needs to be measured, developing a solution, and driving it through implementation.

Nice to Have

• 5–7 years of relevant experience preferred.

• Experience scaling a complex electromechanical product from NPI or low-rate production into higher-volume manufacturing.

• Experience with discrete-event simulation, optimization, operations research, or other production-system modeling techniques.

• Experience with SQL, Python, BI tools, or other methods for analyzing large manufacturing datasets.

• Experience with ERP and MES platforms and developing manufacturing dashboards or operational reporting systems.

• Experience developing business cases for automation or major manufacturing equipment.

• Experience with Lean manufacturing concepts, Theory of Constraints, PFMEA, value-stream mapping, or structured continuous-improvement methodologies.

• Experience supporting factory expansions, new production lines, or greenfield manufacturing operations.

What Else You Need to Know

The starting cash range for this role is $104,000 - $170,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. We are always open to negotiation. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply!

jobs.title: Senior Cost Manager / Quantity Surveyor - Data Center Construction
jobs.description:

The position requires onsite presence Monday through Friday in Rayville, LA. While local candidates or those open to relocation are preferred, a per diem is available for candidates who are unable to relocate.

To be successful in this role, you must have excellent communication skills and be comfortable operating in a client-facing environment. The ideal candidate will be self-motivated, analytical, detail-oriented, and capable of working independently while collaborating effectively with project stakeholders. This position plays a critical role in maintaining the financial health and successful delivery of complex mission-critical construction programs.

• Estimate and evaluate change orders throughout the construction lifecycle.
• Develop and maintain project budgets, forecasts, cash flow reports, and cost control systems.
• Monitor and control project costs to ensure alignment with approved budgets and client objectives.

• Monitor project performance, identify cost risks and opportunities, and develop mitigation strategies.
• Manage cost checks, valuations, and financial validation processes throughout the project lifecycle.
• Support the preparation and negotiation of final accounts.
• Compile and maintain benchmarking data, cost histories, and project financial records.
• Represent Turner & Townsend in client meetings, providing expertise and recommendations on cost control and financial performance.
• Provide leadership and guidance to project teams while promoting best practices in cost management and project controls.
• Identify, coach, and mentor team members to support professional growth and project success.
• Utilize internal systems to manage project financial performance, resource planning, and reporting requirements.
• Implement and maintain Turner & Townsend delivery methodologies, business systems, and cost management best practices.
• Display excellence in leadership and service delivery aligned with Turner & Townsend's values and culture.
• Be a role model who promotes collaboration, accountability, and exceptional client outcomes.

• Bachelor's degree in Quantity Surveying, Construction Management, Engineering, Accounting, or a related field.
• Minimum 5+ years of experience in cost management, quantity surveying, or project controls supporting large-scale construction projects.
• Strong experience in cost control, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, and financial reporting.
• Experience leading cost management activities on medium to large construction projects.
• Experience reviewing contractor estimates, change orders, pay applications, valuations, and final accounts.
• Strong understanding of construction contracts, procurement, contract administration, and commercial management.
• Advanced knowledge of cost control systems, financial forecasting tools, and Earned Value Management (EVM) principles.
• Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills with strong attention to detail.
• Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
• Ability to communicate effectively with clients, contractors, and project stakeholders in a client-facing environment.
• Ability to work collaboratively within cross-functional teams in a fast-paced project environment.
• Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and proactive in identifying issues and driving solutions.
• Construction consultancy experience is strongly preferred.
• Prior experience supporting data center, mission-critical, industrial, or similar large-scale infrastructure projects is preferred.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer, Process Controls
jobs.description:
About Us

We are Sila, a next-generation battery materials company. Our mission is to power the world’s transition to clean energy. To create this future, our team is building a better lithium-ion battery from the inside out today. We engineer and manufacture ground-breaking battery materials that significantly increase the energy density of batteries, while reducing their size and weight. The result? Smaller more powerful batteries that can unlock innovation in consumer devices and accelerate the mass adoption of electric cars to eliminate our dependence on fossil fuels. We're tackling one of the biggest challenges of our time every day, and together we're redefining what's possible. Are you ready to be a part of a team committed to changing the world?

Who You Are

You are a high-level performer who works independently within established guidelines to develop complex materials processing equipment. In your work at Sila, you will execute industrial process controls and instrumentation designs through influence and technical mastery, ensuring systems are safe, reliable, and well-documented. You possess excellent communication skills to harmoniously collaborate across teams and contribute to the growth and development of your teammates.

Responsibilities and Duties

• Execute process controls and instrumentation designs for production-scale synthesis equipment by working collaboratively with other teams to design robust, modular, and well-documented controls.

• Implement control system strategies to execute processes, ensuring designs are incorporated in Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs) according to established standards.

• Create and maintain design documentation—including instrument indexes, I/O lists, alarm lists, cause and effect matrices, and SIL/IPL verification forms—participate in HAZOP reviews, source and select instrumentation, and contribute to project templates.

• Engage successfully with a range of different outside vendors for process controls designs and electrical / instrumentation subsystems.

• Participate in safety reviews following established safety guidelines to ensure safe design of the process, and own closing controls recommendations.

• Assist in bringing online hardware and code.

• Gather feedback from end-users of your work and collaborate to implement actionable modifications, sharing best practices with the team.

Knowledge and Skill Requirements

• Proficiency in control system design principles, including PID control, cascade control, and advanced control techniques.

• Strong knowledge of instrumentation principles and devices (e.g., flow meters, level transmitters, temperature sensors) and industrial communication protocols (e.g., Profinet, Modbus).

• Experience with the full design lifecycle of process control systems, including creating Cause & Effect diagrams, Safety Requirements Specification (SRS), and Alarm Rationalization

• Hands-on experience with PLCs and writing Structured Text and familiarity with other IEC 61131-3 languages.

• Experience designing and programming intuitive and user-friendly human-machine interfaces (HMIs) to enable real-time monitoring and control.

• Experience with ensuring regulatory compliance related to process controls standards, such as, NFPA, UL508A, and IEC 61151.

• 5+ years of industry experience is required. B.S. in Electrical, Mechanical, or Chemical Engineering preferred.

Physical Demands and Working Conditions

• Wear personal protective equipment including, but not limited to, a lab coat, gloves, safety glasses, and steel toe safety shoes

• Move items up to 50 lbs with the assistance of lift equipment and carts

• Move long distances (such as from building to building) and be stationary for extended periods of time

• Reach low shelves or items on the floor

• Climb stairs or over containment walls

• Operate a computer and other office equipment, such as a laptop, copier/printer, etc in a fixed location

• Travel up to 20%

The starting base pay for this role is between $151,000 and $191,000 at the time of posting. The actual base pay depends on many factors, such as education, experience, and skills. Base pay is only one part of Sila’s competitive Total Rewards package that can include benefits, perks, equity.  The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

jobs.title: Ecommerce Specialist
jobs.description:
ABOUT DSC:

In 2011, Dollar Shave Club didn’t just shake up the shaving aisle—we reinvented it. A viral video put us on the map, and our direct-to-consumer model challenged an entire industry by making great razors accessible, affordable, and actually fun to buy.

Since then, we’ve grown far beyond blades. From grooming to personal care, we’ve built a lineup of quality essentials designed to make life easier (and smoother), whether you find us online or in stores near you.

Today, DSC is expanding into new categories and new markets, but our DNA hasn’t changed. We’re still here to cut the BS, deliver real value, and bring a little humor to the everyday routine.

So what are you waiting for? Join the Club.

ROLE SUMMARY:

We’re looking for an Ecommerce Specialist who thrives at the center of the action. You’ll work hands-on in Shopify and across key digital initiatives, taking ownership of tasks within your scope while supporting the broader team: setting up new products and promos, keeping product data accurate, and ensuring our product pages and listings work harder across DTC, marketplace, and retail ecommerce sites.

You like solving problems, looking at the numbers, and finding ways to improve performance. You’ll use performance data to spot opportunities, drive execution, and share feedback and findings to support promotional planning, and day-to-day operations  across the team. You’re excited about AI, open to learning, and already use it in your work. You’ll maintain high QA standards for launches and help build the AI tools and automations that take routine work off the team’s plate.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Product Setup: Create and maintain products in Shopify, including variants, bundles, tags, metafields, pricing and imagery

• Pages and Listings: Keep product pages and listings accurate across our DTC site, marketplaces, and retail partner sites, collaborating with the retail team on updates

• Promos and Launches: Support the setup of promotions and collections, and drive QA checks on pricing, links, imagery, and availability before launches go live

• QA Checklists: Assist in defining QA checklists and standards, keeping processes documented so execution quality improves across all launches

• Automate the Routine: Help build and test AI tools and automations that speed up product setup, content management, and QA

• SEO and Content: Use SEO findings to improve product copy and listings

• Find the Friction: Analyze heatmaps and session replays to spot friction points, supporting CRO test launches and sharing actionable insights

• Reviews: Monitor review syndication to marketplace and retail partners, and share bi-weekly reporting on ratings and volume

• Inventory Watch: Monitor inventory and flag out-of-stock risks to inform promotional planning, forecasting and allocation

REQUIREMENTS:

• Experience: 3+ years in ecommerce merchandising, ecommerce operations or site management

• Shopify Pro: Hands-on Shopify Plus experience with product setup, collections, promotions and product data

• AI Forward: You use AI tools in your day-to-day work, for things like product copy, data cleanup or QA checks, and you check the output before it ships

• Detail Obsessed: You sweat the details customers notice, keeping product data, pricing and every launch accurate so the shopping experience just works

• Data Savvy: Comfortable with GA4, Tableau or Power BI and with heatmap and session replay tools, and able to turn findings into clear recommendations

• SEO Know-How: Experience improving product copy and listings with SEO tools such as SEMrush

• Autonomous Problem Solver: Juggles several workstreams independently in a fast-paced environment, takes ownership of priorities, and supports team goals effectively

• Clear Communicator: Shares open, honest feedback and performance reporting clearly with cross-functional partners while maintaining a team-first mindset

NICE TO HAVE SKILLS:

• Review platforms such as Bazaarvoice or Yotpo

• Shopify Flow or other automation tools

• Basic HTML, CSS or Shopify Liquid

• Experience across more than one brand or Shopify store

• Subscription commerce experience

POSITION TYPE:
This is a full-time exempt position.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:
This position is in-office, working out of our HQ in Durham, North Carolina 3x a week.

SALARY:
Base range of $75,000 - $88,000 plus bonus starting 2027.

BENEFITS:

• Comprehensive benefit plans with low premium options, including medical, dental and vision coverage, along with supplemental coverage options

• Free life insurance, short term disability and long term disability

• 401(k) plan with a company match of 100% of the first 2%, and 50% of up to an additional 4% with no vesting period

jobs.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer - Identity & Trust
jobs.description:
About EarnIn

As one of the first pioneers of earned wage access, our passion at EarnIn is building products that deliver real-time financial flexibility for those with the unique needs of living paycheck to paycheck. Our community members access their earnings as they earn them, with options to spend, save, and grow their money without mandatory fees, interest rates, or credit checks.

We’re fortunate to have an incredibly experienced leadership team, combined with world-class funding partners like A16Z, Matrix Partners, DST, Ribbit Capital, and a very healthy core business with a tremendous runway. We’re growing fast and are excited to continue bringing world-class talent onboard to help shape the next chapter of our growth journey.

POSITION SUMMARY

We're looking for an exceptional Senior Staff Software Engineer to help define and evolve the Identity & Trust platform that enables secure, effortless access and trustworthy customer onboarding across EarnIn's expanding consumer and enterprise ecosystem. This role spans identity, authentication, authorization, identity verification, privacy, data protection, secure document processing, user/entity resolution, and fraud prevention. You'll architect foundational capabilities that are consumed across the company—from establishing that a customer is who they claim to be, to protecting their sensitive information, securely handling identity documents, and ensuring duplicate or abusive identities are detected and prevented.

As a Senior Staff Engineer, you'll operate at both a deep technical and organizational scale. You'll shape multi-year platform strategy, lead architecture across multiple teams, solve ambiguous and high-impact technical problems, and establish engineering patterns that allow teams across EarnIn to build trusted customer experiences safely and quickly. You'll also help define how AI and agentic engineering workflows can safely amplify engineering productivity, while establishing appropriate guardrails for security, privacy, correctness, and operational reliability. The base salary range for this full-time position is $238,660-$341,000 + equity + benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. This position is a remote role.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Set Platform Strategy & Architecture: Define the technical vision, architecture, and multi-year roadmap for Identity & Trust, establishing scalable patterns across authentication, authorization, KYC/identity verification, PII protection, secure document processing, deduplication, and related trust capabilities.

• Lead High-Impact Technical Initiatives: Drive complex, ambiguous initiatives spanning multiple services and teams—from problem definition and architecture through implementation, rollout, and long-term operation.

• Build Secure, Resilient Infrastructure: Design highly available distributed systems and APIs using microservices, event-driven architectures, and technologies such as Kubernetes, Kafka, DynamoDB, and MySQL, with strong emphasis on security, privacy, reliability, and regulatory requirements.

• Evolve Identity & Trust Capabilities: Architect solutions for OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML, RBAC/ABAC, MFA, identity federation, KYC, PII tokenization, data vaulting, secure file ingest/scanning, and user/entity deduplication.

• Create Organizational Leverage: Establish reusable architecture patterns, technical standards, APIs, documentation, and platform primitives that enable product teams to safely consume Identity & Trust capabilities without reinventing foundational security and compliance solutions.

• Drive Operational Excellence: Set the bar for reliability, observability, SLOs, incident response, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and production readiness across critical Trust infrastructure.

• Advance AI-Powered Engineering: Lead the responsible adoption of agentic workflows and multi-agent systems to automate engineering, testing, debugging, operations, and analysis, with appropriate evaluation, security, and human-in-the-loop guardrails.

• Multiply Engineering Talent: Mentor Staff and Senior engineers, influence technical direction across organizations, and raise the bar through architecture reviews, technical RFCs, design reviews, and hands-on technical leadership.

• Partner Across the Company: Work closely with Product, Security, Risk, Data Science, Design, Analytics, Infrastructure, Compliance, and executive stakeholders to translate customer, business, security, and regulatory needs into durable technical strategies.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

• 8+ years of software engineering experience, with demonstrated progression into Staff/Senior Staff-level technical leadership.

• Proven track record defining and executing technical strategy for large-scale distributed systems or platform infrastructure.

• Demonstrated ability to lead architecture and delivery across multiple engineering teams and organizational boundaries, without relying on direct authority.

• Deep hands-on experience designing and operating secure, highly available distributed backend systems at scale.

• Strong expertise across identity, trust, security, privacy, or regulated-data systems, ideally spanning both consumer and enterprise experiences.

• Deep understanding of authentication and authorization protocols and patterns, including OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML, RBAC/ABAC, MFA, identity federation, and token management.

• Experience architecting one or more Trust domains such as KYC/identity verification, fraud or risk systems, PII tokenization, data vaults, encryption, secure document/file processing, identity resolution, or user deduplication.

• Production experience with identity platforms such as Okta, Auth0, Keycloak, or comparable internally developed identity infrastructure.

• Strong proficiency in at least one modern programming language such as Java, C#, Go, Kotlin, Python, or JavaScript/TypeScript, with the ability to work effectively across language boundaries.

• Deep experience with REST APIs, SQL/NoSQL data stores, Kafka or equivalent streaming platforms, Kubernetes, microservices, and event-driven architectures.

• Strong operational instincts, including experience with SLOs, observability, incident response, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and production reliability for critical systems.

• Hands-on experience building AI-assisted or agentic engineering workflows, including orchestration, tool use, evaluation, security boundaries, and guardrails.

• Exceptional architectural judgment and the ability to simplify complex systems while balancing security, privacy, reliability, scalability, developer experience, regulatory requirements, and speed of execution.

• Experience using AI-assisted development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT, or similar tools) as part of your software development workflow

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Success in this role is measured by the technical leverage and trust infrastructure you create across EarnIn, not simply by the services you personally build. You will help establish a cohesive Identity & Trust platform that makes it easier for every product team to build secure customer experiences. You'll create durable architectural foundations for who a customer is, whether they can be trusted, what they can access, and how their most sensitive information is protected.

You'll anticipate scale, security, regulatory, and product challenges before they become organizational constraints; simplify fragmented capabilities into reusable platform primitives; and enable engineering teams to move faster without compromising trust or safety. You'll operate comfortably from deep technical implementation to company-level strategy—diving into code and production systems when necessary, leading architecture across teams, mentoring senior technical leaders, and establishing technical direction for some of EarnIn's most critical foundational capabilities.

At EquipmentShare, we’re not just filling a role — we’re assembling the best team on the planet to build something that’s never been built before. We’re on a mission to transform an industry that’s been stuck in the past by empowering contractors and communities through innovative technology, real-time support, and a team that truly cares.

That means our proprietary T3 platform doesn’t just run our business — it also makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you’re behind the wheel, under the hood, leading a branch, or closing deals — tech supports you, and you drive us forward.

We’re a team of problem-solvers, go-getters, and builders. And we’re looking for teammates who take pride in doing meaningful work and want to be part of building something special.
