jobs.title: Senior SAP Technical Consultant, Professional Services - SAP
jobs.description:
Application deadline: Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis

The Amazon Web Services Professional Services (ProServe) team is seeking a skilled Senior SAP Technical Consultant to join our team at Amazon Web Services (AWS). You will own the technical architecture and engineering strategy for SAP engagements across ABAP development, BTP extensibility, BASIS operations, and integration delivered within customer environments. You will lead multidisciplinary delivery teams of ABAP developers, BTP engineers, and BASIS professionals on complex SAP S/4HANA RISE migrations and modernization programs, establishing the technical standards, governance, and delivery mechanisms that produce secure, scalable, and maintainable SAP outcomes for AWS customers.

This role requires someone who moves fluidly between enterprise architecture decisions and hands-on technical problem-solving. You will evaluate solution alternatives, define development and extensibility patterns, resolve complex technical risks mid-delivery, and ensure ABAP, BTP, and BASIS workstreams operate as one integrated engineering organization across AWS teams, customer teams, and SI partners.
The AWS Professional Services organization is a global team of experts that help customers realize their desired business outcomes when using the AWS Cloud. We work together with customer teams and the AWS Partner Network (APN) to execute enterprise cloud computing initiatives. Our team provides assistance through a collection of offerings which help customers achieve specific outcomes related to enterprise cloud adoption. We also deliver focused guidance through our global specialty practices, which cover a variety of solutions, technologies, and industries.

Key job responsibilities
Own the SAP technical architecture across ABAP, BTP, BASIS, integrations, extensibility, and platform operations on active customer engagements

Lead and develop multidisciplinary delivery teams across BASIS, ABAP, and BTP disciplines, establishing clear ownership, priorities, standards, and delivery expectations on every program

Define technical patterns and guardrails for SAP configuration, custom development, workflows, forms, reports, interfaces, conversions, enhancements, and extensions and enforce them across customer and partner teams

Establish and defend clean-core principles on every engagement, determining when requirements are addressed through standard SAP functionality, in-app extensibility, side-by-side BTP extensions, or custom ABAP and holding that line under commercial pressure

Own BTP architecture decisions including account and subaccount design, environments, connectivity, identity, security, application services, integration services, development standards, and lifecycle management

Lead BASIS architecture and operational design across system landscapes, environments, transports, upgrades, patching, performance, capacity, availability, disaster recovery, monitoring, and production support

Establish software development standards covering solution design, coding, peer reviews, automated testing, documentation, source control, CI/CD, transport management, and release governance and embed them into customer delivery teams that will own them post-engagement

Partner with functional architects, customer product teams, and SI partners to convert business requirements into scalable technical designs and accurate delivery estimates

Review and approve technical designs across workstreams, ensuring solutions meet requirements for performance, scalability, security, controls, resilience, supportability, and cost

Develop technical roadmaps, architecture documents, SOW inputs, decision materials, and executive updates that communicate priorities, risks, trade-offs, and required investments to both customer and AWS leadership

Evaluate emerging SAP and generative AI capabilities including Kiro, ABAP Accelerator, and agentic testing frameworks and identify opportunities to improve engineering productivity, user experience, automation, monitoring, and support on active engagements

What Makes This Role Different

You are not maintaining a system. You are building the technical foundation customers rely on after AWS leaves. Every architecture decision, every standard you set, and every pattern you enforce becomes the customer's operational reality. The bar is high, the engagements are complex, and the impact is permanent.

Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field
- 10+ years of SAP migration, implementation, or consulting experience in software or technology industries
- Experience as a technical lead or mentor on SAP S/4HANA RISE migrations
- Deep expertise in one or more of: ABAP development, SAP BTP, SAP BASIS, SAP integration, or SAP technical architecture

Preferred qualifications:
- 10+ years of infrastructure architecture, database architecture, and networking experience in customer-facing delivery contexts
- Deep knowledge of SAP systems including Business Suite, S/4HANA, BW, HANA, and Business Objects and their architecture and infrastructure requirements
- Hands-on experience with SAP clean-core design, including build using non-SAP technologies across Generative AI, agentic AI, and data and analytics
- Experience with ABAP Cloud, Core Data Services, RESTful Application Programming Model, Fiori, SAPUI5, APIs, workflows, forms, and enhancement frameworks
- Experience with SAP BTP services including Integration Suite, Extension Suite, Cloud Foundry, Kyma, SAP Build, Event Mesh, API Management, or related capabilities
- Experience with SAP BASIS and HANA administration across system landscapes, transports, upgrades, performance tuning, high availability, disaster recovery, monitoring, and operational support

jobs.title: Government and Public Affairs: Community Engagement Manager
jobs.description:
Job Details:

Job Description:

The Role and Impact

Intel is seeking a collaborative and community-focused professional to help strengthen relationships with the public and private sector in Ohio, with a primary focus on the Columbus, New Albany, Johnstown, and Licking County region. The Government and Public Affairs, Community Engagement Manager will support Intel's efforts to advance education, workforce development, economic opportunity, and community impact through strategic engagement with schools, nonprofits, civic organizations, neighbors, and other community stakeholders.

Working in close partnership with the Ohio Director of Government Affairs, this role will help build trust, foster meaningful partnerships, and manage community investment initiatives that support Intel's long-term presence and success in Ohio. The successful candidate will serve as a consistent and visible liaison between Intel and local community organizations and neighbors, helping to ensure the company's philanthropic investments, volunteer programs, and community engagement activities create measurable value for both local communities and Intel.

Business group

You will be part of Intel's Global Government Affairs (GGA) organization, which focuses on shaping and advancing public affairs strategies to support Intel's business and policy objectives. The team collaborates closely with internal stakeholders, external partners, and government entities to establish strategic alliances and advocate for policies that foster innovation and economic growth. GGA plays a key role in driving Intel's leadership in technology and sustainability while positively impacting communities worldwide.

Key Responsibilities

• Community Engagement and Stakeholder Relations
• Build, maintain, and strengthen relationships with schools, nonprofit organizations, community leaders, workforce development partners, educational institutions, civic organizations, and local government stakeholders throughout Ohio, with a primary focus on the Columbus region, New Albany, Johnstown, and Licking County.

• Maintain regular engagement with local government stakeholders, officials and staff in New Albany, Columbus, and Johnstown, as part of Intel's regular community presence.

• Represent Intel at community events, meetings, conferences, volunteer activities, and stakeholder engagements.

• Serve as a visible and trusted liaison between Intel and local community stakeholders, including leading Intel's Neighbor Relations program.

• Identify emerging community issues, opportunities, concerns, and partnership prospects that align with Intel's business and community objectives. As needed, develop and implement strategic plans to address matters comprehensively with engagement and communications strategies.

• Identify and escalate potential policy, public issues or risks that may impact Intel's reputation or objectives.

• Grants Management and Community Investment.

• Manage charitable contributions, grants, sponsorships, and community investment programs across Ohio.

• Monitor and lead engagement in funded programs and partnerships to measure outcomes, ensure accountability, and communicate impact.

• Program and Event Coordination.

• Support logistics and planning for site visits, community meetings, executive engagements, and stakeholder events.

• Collaborate with internal partners to identify volunteer opportunities and community service initiatives aligned with Intel's priorities.

• Lead communications and outreach efforts that promote Intel's community partnerships and local impact.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration.

• Partner closely within the Government and Public Affairs team, Corporate Responsibility and Intel Foundation, site operations, communications, and business groups to align community engagement efforts and communications with broader company objectives.

• Maintain knowledge of Intel's business priorities, policy positions, technologies, workforce initiatives, and community commitments to effectively represent the company to external audiences and help elevate community feedback internally when appropriate.

Qualifications:

The ideal candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:

• Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
• Excellent written and verbal communication abilities.

• Demonstrated ability to engage diverse stakeholders and build trust across communities.

• Strong organizational and project management skills with exceptional attention to detail.

• Ability to manage multiple programs, deadlines, and stakeholder relationships simultaneously.

• Collaborative, proactive, and service-oriented mindset.

• Ability to work effectively in a highly matrixed and rapidly evolving environment.

• Passion for and experience with community impact, education, workforce development, and civic engagement.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in public affairs, communications, public relations, nonprofit management, education, political science, business, marketing, or a related field.
• 6+ years of experience in community relations, public affairs, corporate social responsibility, philanthropy, nonprofit management, education partnerships, grants administration, or related fields.

• Familiarity with Ohio's community, education, nonprofit, workforce development, or civic sectors, with the ability to quickly build credibility and productive relationships.

• Experience working with external stakeholders and community organizations.

• Ability to manage confidential information appropriately.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience representing a large, complex organization, major employer, public institution, or significant community-facing project.
• Residence in or strong familiarity with Licking County region preferred.

• Experience managing grants, sponsorships and community investment programs.

• Experience working with community foundations, major nonprofit organizations, universities, workforce development organizations, educational institutions, or corporate social impact programs.

• Strong event planning and stakeholder engagement experience.

• Experience tracking budgets, administering funding programs, and measuring community impact.

Your expertise can help us amplify Intel's voice, drive impactful initiatives, and shape the policies that pave the way for innovation. Join us to make a meaningful difference and help power a brighter future.

jobs.title: Procurement & Submittals Mgr., AWS, Power and Cooling
jobs.description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) provides a highly reliable, scalable, and low-cost cloud platform that powers thousands of businesses in over 190 countries.
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

We are looking for a results-oriented individual to support AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)'s Power and Cooling (PAC) sourcing requirements for mission critical equipment and manufacturing for AWS data centers.
Our AWS Procurement team is looking for a results-oriented individual to assume responsibility in our Procurement Operations Center to drive standard process for RFQ (Request for Quote) for capital equipment, Change order management, budget approvals and supplier qualification related to our growing Infrastructure. Wiki - https://w.amazon.com/bin/view/ISCaP/ISCaP_Power_and_Cooling/PAC_Procurement_Ops

Key job responsibilities
As a Procurement and Submittals Manager, you will:
• Generate RFQ (Request for Quote) according to forecasted demand
• Manage the End-to-End Purchase Order (PO) change management process
• Manage the funding reallocation process to enable issuance of PO
• Collaborate with internal stakeholders to drive change management
• Proactively communicate risks and issues to key stakeholders and recommend mitigations
• Develop Key Performance Indicators (KPI's) and track progress against goals
• Develop new processes for supplier qualification and onboarding
• Adapt to a fast paced, constantly changing environment

jobs.title: Product Line Lead, Clinical & Agentic AI
jobs.description:
About AISI

AI Strategy & Innovation (AISI) sits at the centre of AstraZeneca's R&D AI transformation. Our remit is to build, buy and deliver the AI models and agents that change pipeline outcomes, across discovery, translational science, biomarkers and clinical development.

Role Summary

AstraZeneca is building agentic AI products that take work out of clinical development and clinical operations, starting with automating site-monitoring reports and data review for clinical research associates. We are seeking a Product Line Lead, Clinical & Agentic AI, to own the product line that takes these agents from proof of concept to GxP-validated use, and to set the direction of the agentic AI platform layer that supports them.

You will lead product ownership across the line, including the product owner for the clinical research associate (CRA) agent, and set priorities, lifecycle gates and decision rights between product and engineering. You will make sure each product is built with the data access, human oversight and validation evidence that regulated clinical settings require, from the start. You will also guide how the platform layer evolves as enterprise AI assistants take on more of AstraZeneca's everyday agentic work, including which use cases still need a purpose-built, governed platform because of patient data.

You will work with clinical development and operations leaders, AI scientists and engineers, R&D IT, Enterprise AI platform teams, Quality, and external delivery partners. This line is early in its life and the platform landscape is changing. We are looking for someone who is decisive, comfortable with ambiguity, and credible with both clinical and engineering audiences.

Accountabilities:

Product Line Strategy and Roadmap

• Define and own the strategy, roadmap and success measures for the clinical and agentic AI product line, tied to AISI's must-win outcomes and the multi-year plan.

• Decide what to start, scale, merge or stop across the line, using clear lifecycle gates and evidence of value.

• Define and maintain decision rights between product and engineering (product decides what and why; engineering decides how), and make them hold in practice.

• Keep one current view of the line's portfolio, funding, cost and risk, and report on it to AISI leadership.

Leading Product Owners and Delivery

• Direct and develop the product owners on the line, starting with the CRA agent product owner. Make sure every product has an accountable owner, a roadmap, a backlog and a value case.

• Work with engineering leaders and external delivery partners to clear blockers, including data access, environments and integration dependencies.

• Set the operating rhythm (planning, reviews, stage gates) so that delivery scales as the line grows.

Clinical Agentic Products

• Own the path of the CRA agent from proof of concept through silent pilot to GxP-validated release, including sign-off from business owners across therapeutic and operational areas.

• Translate clinical operations needs into product requirements and measurable outcomes, such as monitoring effort saved and trial capacity gained.

• Make human-in-the-loop design, auditability and validation planning product requirements from the first release.

Agentic Platform Direction

• Set the product direction for the agentic platform layer used by R&D, and recommend where to build, buy, adopt or retire platforms.

• Define and defend the boundary for patient data and regulated use: which use cases need a governed, purpose-built platform, and which can run on enterprise assistants.

• Lead the transition plan and user communications when platforms change, working with Enterprise AI and IT partners.

Governance, Compliance and Quality

• Work with Quality, Compliance and Data Privacy so that products meet GxP computerised system validation, data privacy and AI governance requirements.

• Own the line's risk register and raise issues early, including security findings and control gaps.

• Support audit and inspection readiness for the line's products and processes.

Financial and Vendor Stewardship

• Keep cost visible across headcount, contractors, cloud compute and model usage, and contribute to planning cycles.

• Manage vendor and outsourced delivery partners to agreed scope, quality and cost.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

jobs.title: Principal Cybersecurity - Threat Hunter (Government)
jobs.description:
AT&T Global Public Sector is a trusted provider of secure, IP-enabled, cloud-based network solutions and professional services to the Federal Government. We are dedicated to recruiting, developing, and empowering a diverse, high-performing workforce that is passionate about what they do, committed to our shared values, and dedicated to our customers' missions.

AT&T Public Sector's National Security organization delivers mission-critical solutions supporting the nation's most important priorities. We serve customers across the Department of Defense, Department of Homeland Security, Defense Industrial Base, and Intelligence Community, combining AT&T's technology, global network capabilities, and experienced professionals to support highly sensitive and complex missions.

AT&T is seeking an experienced and intellectually curious Principal Cybersecurity - Threat Hunter to support a Federal National Security customer. This is not a traditional alert-monitoring or ticket-processing position. The successful candidate will proactively investigate large-scale network metadata, including NetFlow and DNS, develop and test hypotheses, identify meaningful patterns in ambiguous data, and translate technical evidence into clear, actionable intelligence. The successful candidate will synthesize analytic reports, assess their significance and limitations, and connect the findings into an understanding of threats and customer risk.

The threat hunter will independently lead day-to-day mission support while working alongside a cross-functional cybersecurity team including data scientists, analysts, software developers, and security engineers. The role requires someone who enjoys finding the story within complex data, challenging initial assumptions, and pursuing investigative leads that may not be identified through predefined rules or traditional security alerts.

This position will leverage AT&T's global network visibility, threat intelligence, analytics, and cybersecurity expertise to identify and investigate emerging threats. Approximately 50% of the role will focus on threat hunting, investigations, reporting, and customer briefings. The remaining time will support advancing threat-hunting tradecraft, evaluating new sources of threat intelligence, analytic prototyping, research and development, and peer collaboration.

This is a full-time onsite role based in the location(s) posted and is performed from the designated work location five days per week. No relocation is offered.

The position is primarily based at AT&T's Chantilly, Virginia office, with occasional presence expected at the customer site. The role generally operates during standard business hours.

Description of Job Duties/Responsibilities:

• Lead threat analysis and investigations using AT&T Internet traffic metadata, including NetFlow, DNS, and related network telemetry.
• Identify anomalous behavior, high-risk communications, malicious infrastructure, and potential indicators of compromise.
• Independently manage the day-to-day customer mission, including occasional presence on the customer operations floor.
• Prepare and deliver recurring threat briefings, investigative findings, and actionable recommendations to customer SOC and operations leadership.
• Develop and document repeatable threat-hunting tradecraft, playbooks, analytic workflows, and reporting practices.
• Prototype Splunk/SIEM queries and dashboards, lightweight scripts, visualizations, and new hunt concepts to improve threat detection and analysis.
• Translate threat-hunting tradecraft into functional and analytic requirements for developers, engineers, and data scientists.
• Collaborate with AT&T analysts, intelligence teams, developers, and data scientists to advance threat-hunting methods and customer capabilities.
• Mentor other analysts and contribute to peer reviews, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

Required Clearance: TS/SCI with polygraph. (#ts/sci) (#polygraph)

Additional Clearance Requirements:

U.S. citizenship; customer-required polygraph; clearance, polygraph, and customer access eligibility must be maintained.

Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience in cybersecurity, computer science, information technology, data science, intelligence studies, mathematics, or similar discipline
• Minimum of 3 to 5 years of experience in threat hunting, network security analysis, cyber threat intelligence, incident investigation, or a related analytical discipline.
• Demonstrated ability to conduct proactive, hypothesis-driven investigations across large datasets, particularly when information is incomplete or does not match a predefined alert.
• Strong knowledge of TCP/IP, Internet infrastructure, and network behavior, with hands-on experience analyzing NetFlow, DNS, or comparable network metadata.
• Experience using Splunk or another analytics or SIEM platform to query, correlate, investigate, and visualize security data.
• Knowledge of attacker behavior, threat intelligence, indicators of compromise, and adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures.
• Ability to identify meaningful patterns and anomalies, evaluate competing explanations, and distinguish observed facts from analytic judgments.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting technical findings, confidence assessments, and actionable recommendations to customer security and operations leaders.
• Ability to independently manage a customer-facing engagement while collaborating effectively with analysts, intelligence teams, engineers, developers, and data scientists.
• Ability to prototype queries, lightweight scripts, or analytic workflows and translate investigative needs into clear technical requirements.
• Working knowledge of Linux and command-line analysis tools.

Desired Qualifications:

• Experience using threat intelligence platforms and sources such as MISP, OSINT, government, or commercial intelligence.
• Experience tracking threat actors, malicious infrastructure, botnets, command-and-control activity, proxies, scanning, beaconing, or exploitation behavior.
• Experience developing threat-hunting playbooks, mapping findings to MITRE ATT&CK, and converting investigations into repeatable methods.
• Familiarity with Python, SQL, shell scripting, statistical baselining, anomaly analysis, data visualization, or evaluating AI/ML-assisted analytics.
• Academic or professional exposure to economics, philosophy, intelligence analysis, or another discipline emphasizing critical reasoning, hypothesis development, pattern recognition, and evidence-based argumentation.
• Experience supporting Federal or National Security customers, working in classified environments, or operating alongside customer SOC and operations teams.
• Relevant cybersecurity certifications such as CISSP, Security+, CySA+, GIAC, Splunk, or comparable credentials.

jobs.description:
Under general supervision, performs mechanical assembly, maintenance, and overhaul on equipment. Works to pre-defined procedures in line with established work practices and Quality standards. Conducts all business activities in accordance with Baker Hughes HSE policies, Legal Compliance requirements, and Baker Hughes Core Values.

ARMO Tech

Are you interested in working with electro‑mechanical assemblies in an industrial environment?

Do you enjoy following structured procedures, reading technical documentation, and supporting reliable equipment operations?

Partnering with the Best

Our ARMO and operations teams play a critical role in supporting equipment reliability and operational excellence. The ARMO Tech supports this mission by performing electro‑mechanical assembly and maintenance activities while adhering to established safety, quality, and compliance standards.

Fueling Your Passion

As an ARMO Tech you will support electro‑mechanical activities by reading technical documentation, assembling components, and following formal procedures and maintenance practices. You will apply basic technical skills and use standard tools to support shop and operational requirements in an industrial setting.

As an ARMO Tech, you will be responsible for:

• Reading and interpreting blueprints, wiring diagrams, assembly prints, and parts lists.
• Following formal procedures, work instructions, and maintenance practices.
• Performing basic soldering and assembly of electro‑mechanical devices and components.
• Using standard hand tools and equipment in accordance with safety and quality requirements.
• Documenting work activities and maintaining records using basic computer systems.
• Supporting shop and operational activities based on business needs.
• Conducting all work in accordance with company Health, Safety, Environmental (HSE) policies and compliance standards.

To be successful in this role you will:

• Have a Technical diploma or Associate degree OR a minimum of 2 years of relevant industrial experience (e.g., airline, military, oilfield, automotive).
• Have the ability to read and interpret technical drawings, wiring diagrams, and assembly documentation.
• Have basic skills in soldering and electro‑mechanical assembly.
• Have basic computer skills for documentation and reporting.
• Have the ability to follow standardized procedures and work instructions.
• Have the ability to work safely in an industrial environment while using required personal protective equipment (PPE).

Work in a Way That Works for You

This role is based in an industrial shop or operational environment. Work schedules may vary based on operational requirements.

Working with Us

Our people are at the heart of our success. We foster a safe and collaborative environment that values learning and continuous improvement.

Working for You

We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, which may include:

• Career development and training programs
• Medical and wellness benefits
• Financial and retirement programs
• Additional voluntary benefits

You will be eligible to participate in Company-sponsored benefit programs, including health & welfare programs and the Thrift Plan (401k). You will have a choice of coverage options that best suit your needs. Coverage options and contribution amounts are related to your benefit elections, base salary level, and specific requirements of each of these plans.

This position is eligible for our comprehensive and competitive benefits package, which can be found here, and is further eligible for additional forms of compensation such as bonuses subject to the terms of the applicable benefit plans or policies.

The Baker Hughes internal title for this role is: ARMO Tech - Equip I

jobs.title: Technical Support Engineer
jobs.description:
Technical Support Engineer, Coiled Tubing

Are you passionate about providing technical solutions that enable safe, efficient, and reliable coiled tubing and well intervention operations?

Join our Pressure Pumping team

Our Pressure Pumping team combines field expertise, advanced engineering, and digital technology to help customers execute complex coiled tubing and well-intervention operations safely, efficiently, and reliably.

Partner with the best

As a Technical Support Engineer, Coiled Tubing, you will provide engineering expertise and technical support for the planning, design, and execution of coiled tubing and associated pressure pumping operations. You will work closely with customers, field personnel, operations teams, maintenance personnel, and third-party service providers to develop technically sound job programs and support flawless operational execution.

You will be responsible for delivering engineering analysis, operational modelling, equipment application support, risk assessments, execution monitoring, and post-job technical evaluations across a broad range of coiled tubing intervention services.

As the Technical Support Engineer, Coiled Tubing, you will be responsible for:

• Reviewing customer objectives, well data, completion schematics, operating conditions, and equipment limitations to develop technically robust intervention solutions.

• Selecting and specifying coiled tubing strings, bottom-hole assemblies (BHAs), downhole tools, fluids, pumping parameters, and contingency equipment.
• Developing operating envelopes and technical limits for pressure, depth, speed, fatigue utilization, pump rates, differential pressure, and equipment loading.
• Preparing job procedures, engineering calculations, BHA schematics, pressure-control stack-up drawings, equipment layouts, pumping schedules, and contingency plans.
• Verifying compatibility between coiled tubing units, injectors, reels, power packs, pressure-control equipment, pumping systems, treating iron, downhole tools, and customer well configurations.
• Supporting equipment readiness through reviews of maintenance status, certifications, inspection records, pressure-testing requirements, and inventory availability.
• Participating in equipment audits, function testing, yard testing, system integration testing, and pre-job readiness reviews.
• Leading and participating in HAZIDs, HAZOPs, Management of Change (MOC) reviews, technical reviews, risk assessments, and pre-job meetings.
• Providing real-time technical support during field operations, monitoring critical operating parameters, troubleshooting technical challenges, and recommending corrective actions within approved operating limits.
• Maintaining coiled tubing fatigue-management records and pipe-management systems to ensure compliance with operational and safety requirements.
• Supporting investigation and closure of incidents, equipment failures, operational deviations, and non-conformance events.
• Leading or supporting pre-job and post-job reviews while ensuring technical documentation packages are complete, accurate, and properly archived.
• Preparing daily engineering updates, technical reports, post-job analyses, lessons learned documentation, and end-of-job summaries.
• Maintaining complete engineering records, operational data, calculations, job histories, and equipment documentation.
• Supporting feasibility studies, technical proposals, equipment selection processes, tender submissions, and cost-estimate development.
• Serving as a technical focal point between customers, Baker Hughes operations teams, maintenance personnel, suppliers, certification authorities, and third-party providers.
• Coaching field engineers and operational personnel on engineering software, equipment applications, operating limits, and best practices.
• Identifying opportunities to improve service quality, operational performance, engineering processes, equipment utilization, and customer outcomes.

Fuel your passion

To be successful in this role you will:

• Have a bachelor's degree in petroleum engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or another relevant engineering discipline.
• Have a minimum of 5 years of experience in coiled tubing, pressure pumping, well intervention, completions, or related oilfield operations.
• Have demonstrated experience supporting the planning, design, and execution of coiled tubing operations.
• Be proficient in coiled tubing job-design and modelling software, preferably Baker Hughes CIRCA applications or equivalent industry platforms.
• Have practical knowledge of coiled tubing strings, injectors, reels, power packs, pressure-control equipment, pumping systems, treating iron, and downhole intervention tools.
• Have experience conducting force analysis, fatigue analysis, hydraulic modelling, solids transport studies, and operational reach assessments.
• Demonstrate knowledge of coiled tubing metallurgy, fatigue management, string design, corrosion mitigation, wellbore hydraulics, pressure limitations, and sour service requirements.
• Have experience designing and selecting BHAs for cleanout, milling, nitrogen lifting, chemical treatment, cementing, stimulation, isolation, and abandonment applications.

Desired Characteristics

• Required to load coils on dereelers making sure you have the right size C hook for the coil and centering the hoist over coil.
• Required to use the safety chain when loading coils.
• Remove and cut first wrap off of the coils and place magnet back on the coils.
• Make sure at coils are loaded on both sides of the dereeler at every press at end of shift.
• Required to palletize material off of the conveyors.
• Operates an electric pallet truck to move completed pallets/boxes of lamination to the staging area.
• Operates a hoist to hang coils and when palletizing material that weighs 50 lbs. or over.
• Operates pneumatic shears, pneumatic stapler and hydraulic lift tables, as needed.
• Material handlers will make up boxes to keep production going and must leave adequate amount for next shift made up.
• Makes sure that all lines are cleared at the end of the shift.

• Perform daily clean up at end of the shift.

jobs.description:
Job Posting End Date

11-11-2026

Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

Responsible for the effective planning, staffing, and execution of engineering projects as well as oversight of technical support services to deliver safe, cost-effective solutions for AEP’s new and existing Power Generation fleet. This includes resource management, coordination, and supervision of engineering efforts as they pertain to the specific discipline, systems and/or equipment groups. Responsible for providing direction and guidance to employees to promote continuous improvement, development, and talent retention. Responsible for effectively insuring engineering deliverables are produced in accordance with Engineering standard work and Quality Assurance procedures.

Job Description

What you’ll do:

• Lead, develop, and manage a multidisciplinary engineering and technical team supporting utility-scale solar photovoltaic (Solar), battery energy storage systems (BESS), other renewable generation, build/transfer projects, and acquisition opportunities, including staffing, workload, performance, succession planning, resources, and budgets.
• Establish organizational priorities and foster a culture of safety, accountability, technical excellence, collaboration, inclusion, employee development, and continuous improvement.
• Lead engineering execution for self-developed Solar and BESS projects across the project lifecycle and provide engineering oversight of developer-led Solar, BESS, and other renewable build/transfer projects through acceptance, turnover, and closeout.
• Serve as the primary engineering integrator among Project Engineering, Self-Development, Self-Build, Acquisition and Project Management teams, Engineering Services, Operating Companies, developers, AE/EPC firms, OEMs, Independent Engineers, suppliers, and consultants to align technical requirements, project or transaction objectives, operating needs, and long-term asset performance.
• Direct resolution of technical interfaces, design changes, deviations, nonconformances, engineering issues, commercial-technical interfaces, and risks affecting safety, quality, cost, schedule, reliability, compliance, or transaction value.
• Own and maintain the applicable portions of the New Generation EPC Specification, ensuring requirements for Solar, BESS, and other applicable technologies remain accurate, complete, and aligned with Engineering Services design criteria, technical specifications, design standards, portfolio requirements, and lessons learned to provide a consistent technical basis for new AEP assets delivered through AE, EPC, or similar delivery models.
• Ensure project engineering and design comply with the New Generation EPC Specification, where applicable, Engineering Services requirements, codes and regulations, permits, quality requirements, and contractual commitments.
• Provide engineering leadership for design reviews, safety-in-design, constructability, operability, maintainability, interconnection, quality, commissioning, startup readiness, and other technical activities necessary to deliver safe, reliable, and maintainable Solar and BESS facilities.
• Lead technical due diligence for Solar, BESS, renewable generation, energy-storage, and other acquisition opportunities, coordinating internal subject-matter experts and Independent Engineers to evaluate design basis, asset condition, performance, construction quality, reliability, compliance, remaining useful life, anticipated capital requirements, and material technical risks.
• Promote standardization and application of proven engineering solutions and lessons learned across Solar, BESS, build/transfer, and acquisition activities, ensuring project, operating, and due-diligence experience is incorporated into future projects and the New Generation EPC Specification.
• Ensure critical design-basis decisions, assumptions, engineering rationale, approved deviations, due-diligence findings, risk assessments, lessons learned, and decision records are documented and traceable throughout the asset lifecycle, preserving the engineering knowledge and design history of the portfolio.
• Ensure completed and acquired facilities are supported by complete, accurate, organized, and retrievable engineering records that preserve design intent and accurately represent the asset. Lead engineering turnover, project closeout, and acquisition transition to support Operations, Maintenance, and long-term asset management.

What we are looking for:

Engineering Manager SG10

Education

• Bachelor's degree in engineering in a program accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET).

Experience:

• Requires a minimum of ten years of experience in utility engineering work. Project/ initiative leadership experience is required. Direct supervisory experience is preferred.

Required License(s)/Certification(s):

• Registration as a Professional Engineer (PE) in any U.S. state is preferred

In addition:

• Significant progressive engineering experience in power generation, renewable energy, energy storage, major capital projects, asset acquisitions, or comparable infrastructure.
• Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams and coordinating engineering activities across project management, engineering disciplines, developers, contractors, consultants, and operating organizations.
• Experience with renewable generation, energy storage, project development, build/transfer execution, and/or technical evaluation of generation assets.
• Experience managing technical risk, project or transaction interfaces, engineering requirements, and complex technical decisions.
• Demonstrated experience establishing, evaluating, and maintaining clear, traceable design-basis documentation, including technical assumptions, design decisions, deviations, due-diligence findings, configuration information, and engineering records necessary to understand and operate an asset.
• Physical demand level is Sedentary.
• Maintains safety as the highest priority and demonstrates behaviors that support zero harm both at work and at home.
• Demonstrates the highest standards of ethical behavior and support the Company's Corporate Compliance Policy.
• Demonstrates leadership ability to effectively organize, direct, and coordinate the work of other personnel.
• Demonstrates ability to communicate effectively and present ideas clearly both orally and in writing, including making presentations and recommendations to senior management and external audiences.
• Exhibits strong teamwork skills which include collaboration.
• Demonstrates strategic risk-assessment, customer focus and business awareness to support technical decision making.
• Focuses on continuous improvement and employee development.
• Strong planning and organizational skills required.

In addition to competitive compensation, AEP offers a unique comprehensive benefits package that aims to support and enhance the overall well-being of our employees.

Where Putting the Customer First Powers Everything We Do

Guided by our mission to put the customer first, we strive to exceed expectations by listening, responding, and continuously improving the way we serve our communities. Perform work involved with the installation, rearrangement, maintenance, operation, removal, and inspection of electrical transmission and distribution facilities, drive and operate line trucks and associated auxiliary equipment. All job duties apply to overhead and underground equipment and facilities. The Line Mechanic C builds upon the skills, abilities and knowledge learned as a Line Mechanic D (or equivalent).

This position is posted in a range from Line Mechanic D-A

This job requires "recommended" results on the HireVue Line Worker Virtual Job Tryout—an untimed online assessment that typically takes about 45 minutes; all applicants will be automatically invited, but employees already in the Line progression are exempt and may disregard the request; see the Employment Test Prep section at https://www.aep.com/careers/testprep/ for details.

• Perform line work on energized and de-energized electrical systems in accordance with classification level, training progression, and safety requirements.
• Assist with and perform switching operations, sectionalizing activities, grounding procedures, and restoration activities to ensure safe and reliable electric service.
• Operate and maintain company equipment including trucks, aerial devices, digger derricks, specialized line tools, and testing equipment.
• Install, maintain, and troubleshoot underground residential distribution (URD) systems, commercial underground facilities, street lighting systems, transformers, regulator banks, capacitor banks, and related electrical equipment.

• Direct and assist assigned employees as required while supporting employee training, development, and apprenticeship progression.
• Maintain accurate records, reports, apprenticeship documentation, and operational information.
• Communicate with customers regarding service interruptions, meter locations, and service requirements as appropriate.

At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a underwriter to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Underwriting

AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.

How you will create an impact

• This role will focus on underwriting new and renewal business to help drive the profitable growth of our Property
• You will be responsible for assessing the desirability of risk through regular contact with brokers, close co-ordination with AIG subject matter experts and robust reviews of claims history and general company information.
• Your relationships with brokers will be key to your success. You will need to provide excellent service to brokers through a consistent, timely, and proactive approach to underwriting. You will also aim to generate new business by expanding your broker network, attending broker events, and building new relationships across the market – in line with a sales plan established with your manager.
• Another key aspect of the role is the provision of accurate monthly management information including submissions, bind rate, average premium, and total premium.

What you’ll need to succeed

• Some underwriting experience is preferred; however, you are welcome to apply if you have other professional experience.
• The ability to analyze financial statements.
• Strong communication, networking and relationship building skills.
• Good organizational and time management skills.
• Customer and Sales orientated behaviors: motivated, tenacious, focused, technically skilled, proactive, and accountable.

Ready to prove your potential? We would love to hear from you.

At AIG, we value in-person collaboration as a vital part of our culture, which is why we ask our team members to be primarily in the office. This approach helps us work together effectively and create a supportive, connected environment for our team and clients alike.

Enjoy benefits that take care of what matters

At AIG, our people are our greatest asset. We know how important it is to protect and invest in what’s most important to you. That is why we created our Total Rewards Program, a comprehensive benefits package that extends beyond time spent at work to offer benefits focused on your health, wellbeing and financial security—as well as your professional development—to bring peace of mind to you and your family.

Reimagining insurance to make a bigger difference to the world

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a global leader in commercial and personal insurance solutions; we are one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks. It is an exciting time to join us — across our operations, we are thinking in new and innovative ways to deliver ever-better solutions to our customers. At AIG, you can go further to support individuals, businesses, and communities, helping them to manage risk, respond to times of uncertainty and discover new potential. We invest in our largest asset, our people, through continuous learning and development, in a culture that celebrates everyone for who they are and what they want to become.

Welcome to a culture of inclusion

We’re committed to creating a culture that truly respects and celebrates each other’s talents, backgrounds, cultures, opinions and goals. We foster a culture of inclusion and belonging through learning, cultural awareness activities and Employee Resource Groups (ERGs). With global chapters, ERGs are a cornerstone for our culture of inclusion. The talent of our people is one of AIG’s greatest assets, and we are honored that our drive for positive change has been recognized by numerous recent awards and accreditations.

AIG provides equal opportunity to all qualified individuals regardless of race, color, religion, age, gender, gender expression, national origin, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected categories.

AIG is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to job applicants and employees with disabilities.  If you believe you need a reasonable accommodation, please send an email to candidatecare@aig.com.

jobs.title: Data & Analytics Lead Consultant
jobs.description:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Leads complex data and analytics initiatives that deliver trusted, secure, and scalable enterprise data capabilities. This role combines technical expertise, business knowledge, and cross-functional leadership to advance data strategy, governance, quality, modernization, and analytics across the enterprise.

The Data & Analytics Lead Consultant provides strategic and technical leadership to deliver enterprise data and analytics capabilities that support business goals and enable trusted, data-driven decision making. This role combines strong data and analytics expertise with business knowledge to lead complex initiatives, establish scalable solutions and standards, and foster collaboration across business, technology, analytics, and data governance teams.

The Lead Consultant will contribute to enterprise data strategy across Data Governance & Quality, Analytics Ecosystem, Master Data Management, and Data Information & Security, while helping modernize data platforms and engineering practices.

Key Responsibilities:

Data & Analytics Strategy

• Lead complex, cross-functional data and analytics initiatives aligned with business and enterprise data strategies.
• Translate business objectives and requirements into actionable data, analytics, and technology solutions.
• Contribute to functional strategy and define measurable success criteria for enterprise-wide initiatives.
• Develop frameworks, roadmaps, and implementation plans for strategic data initiatives.
• Identify opportunities to improve how enterprise data is collected, integrated, managed, governed, and consumed.
• Evaluate technical approaches and communicate recommendations, risks, dependencies, and trade-offs to stakeholders.

Data Solutions & Modernization

• Lead the design and delivery of scalable data solutions supporting analytical and business needs.
• Provide technical guidance for data ingestion, transformation, integration, storage, modeling, and consumption.
• Apply modern data technologies and frameworks such as Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Spark, Python/PySpark, SQL, Kafka, dbt, or equivalent technologies.
• Support modernization of legacy data platforms and processes through cloud, lakehouse, and modern data engineering patterns.
• Promote reusable patterns and standards that improve consistency, scalability, maintainability, and delivery efficiency.
• Ensure data solutions meet expectations for performance, reliability, security, and operational support.

Data Governance & Quality

• Establish and promote practices that improve the reliability, consistency, accessibility, and quality of enterprise data.
• Partner with business and technology teams to define data ownership, stewardship, metadata, lineage, and quality expectations.
• Define and monitor data quality controls, validation rules, reconciliation processes, and key data quality metrics.
• Help establish trusted and governed data sources that can be consistently reused across business and analytical applications.
• Ensure appropriate data lifecycle, retention, privacy, and governance requirements are incorporated into data solutions.

Analytics Ecosystem

• Enable the appropriate data, platforms, and capabilities needed to conduct analysis, inform decisions, and deliver measurable business outcomes.
• Partner with analytics, data engineering, product, and business teams to develop integrated analytical capabilities.
• Promote consistent and reusable approaches to data modeling, data access, semantic definition, and analytics consumption.
• Identify gaps in the analytics ecosystem and recommend improvements to platforms, processes, and capabilities.

Master Data Management

• Support the development and adoption of trusted enterprise sources for key business data.
• Establish processes and standards that improve the consistency, quality, and usability of shared data across business domains.
• Partner with data owners, data custodians, technology teams, and business stakeholders to establish authoritative data definitions and ownership.
• Identify opportunities to reduce duplication and inconsistencies across enterprise data assets.

Data Information & Security

• Partner with security, governance, and technology teams to protect enterprise data through appropriate security and access controls.
• Ensure data solutions align with applicable privacy, security, regulatory, and enterprise requirements.
• Incorporate security considerations into data architecture, integration, storage, and consumption designs.
• Promote appropriate data classification and access practices throughout the data lifecycle.

Program Leadership & Enterprise Collaboration

• Lead integrated, multi-track projects and initiatives, ensuring high-quality deliverables, effective risk management, and alignment with business objectives.
• Develop project plans, establish controls, track performance, manage dependencies, and communicate risks and status.
• Collaborate across business units and technology teams to resolve complex data and delivery challenges.
• Foster enterprise-wide collaboration and alignment across data engineering, analytics, architecture, governance, security, and business teams.
• Translate complex technical concepts into clear business implications, capabilities, risks, and recommendations.
• Communicate effectively with technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior leadership.
• Mentor team members and promote knowledge sharing and adoption of data and analytics best practices.

Core Skills

• Strong knowledge of data and analytics strategy, data governance, data quality, data engineering, and analytics.
• Strong understanding of modern data architecture, including lakehouse, data warehouse, batch and streaming processing, and cloud-based data platforms.
• Hands-on knowledge of technologies such as Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Spark, Python/PySpark, SQL, or equivalent modern data technologies.
• Experience with data modeling, data integration, metadata, lineage, master data management, and data quality practices.
• Understanding of Microsoft Fabric capabilities including Lakehouse, Warehouse, OneLake, Notebooks, Data Pipelines, and Semantic Models.
• Experience with modern software and data engineering practices including Git, automated testing, CI/CD, monitoring, and observability.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work through complex technical and business problems.
• Demonstrated ability to lead complex cross-functional initiatives and influence outcomes without direct authority.
• Ability to translate technical concepts into business capabilities and communicate effectively with senior stakeholders.
• Strong collaboration, facilitation, consulting, and written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Skills

• Experience with Microsoft Fabric and Azure data services.
• Experience modernizing legacy data platforms and processes into cloud or lakehouse architectures.
• Knowledge of enterprise data governance, data catalogs, metadata management, lineage, and data quality frameworks.
• Experience with Master Data Management and enterprise data standardization.
• Experience with data security, privacy, classification, and access-control practices.
• Familiarity with generative and agentic AI capabilities and their application to data, analytics, and engineering productivity.

Experience

• 7 or more years of relevant experience in data, analytics, technology, consulting, or related disciplines (Preferred).
• Experience leading complex or cross-functional data and analytics initiatives (Preferred).

Analytics, Analytics Strategy, Data Analysis, Data Strategies, Enterprise Data

• Evaluate new technologies, frameworks, and patterns to improve data infrastructure and engineering capabilities.

• Share knowledge and mentor less experienced engineers, contributing to team growth and best practices.

• Strong proficiency in developing scalable data pipelines using PySpark and Python.
• Hands-on experience with modern data engineering frameworks and tools, including Apache Spark, Kafka, Flink, dbt, or equivalent technologies.

• Experience designing and developing batch and/or real-time streaming data solutions.
• Hands-on experience with Microsoft Fabric Notebooks for developing, debugging, testing, and operationalizing data engineering workflows.
• Experience with containerization and orchestration technologies, such as Docker and Kubernetes.
• Experience implementing monitoring and observability solutions, with Datadog experience preferred.
• Ability to work effectively in collaborative, iterative, and product-centric engineering environments.
• Strong communication, analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills

Preferred Skills

• Experience with cloud data services (Azure, AWS).

• Hands‑on experience with Microsoft Fabric components, including Lakehouse, Warehouse, Data Pipelines, Dataflows Gen2, and Semantic Models.

jobs.title: Allstate Sales Agent Trainee
jobs.description:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Become an Allstate Sales Agent Trainee: Kickstart Your Sales Career with Unlimited Earning Potential

Are you ready to break into sales—or take your early sales career to the next level? Do you love talking to people, enjoy the thrill of finding new opportunities, and want a job where you decide how much you earn?

If this sounds like you, a career as an Allstate Sales Agent Trainee might be the perfect fit.

Why Allstate?

• Unlimited Earning Potential: Earn uncapped commissions. The more you put in, the more you make—simple.
• We Train You: No insurance experience? No problem. We provide paid training, licensing support, and ongoing coaching to help you grow quickly and confidently.
• Marketing Support: You’ll have access to marketing tools and resources so you can focus on what you do best: connecting with people and selling.
• Day-One Benefits: Flexible benefits start right away, plus Employer‑Matched RRSP after 90 days.

Role Designation: Onsite

About the Role: This isn’t just another sales job—it’s your chance to build a successful career from the ground up. If you’re energetic, love meeting new people, and enjoy the challenge of finding opportunities, you’ll thrive here. We’re looking for someone with a go‑getter attitude who’s excited to learn how to prospect, build relationships, and help clients choose the right protection.

With Allstate’s strong commission structure, you stay in control of your earning potential—the more effort you put in, the more you can make. You’ll learn how to become a trusted advisor to your clients and make a real impact on their lives, all while building a rewarding career in sales.

We Train You:
No insurance experience? No problem. We provide paid training, licensing support, and ongoing coaching to help you grow quickly and confidently. You’ll also receive extensive 10‑week onboarding that includes license preparation, systems training, product knowledge, sales tools, and proven sales techniques designed to build and strengthen the skills you need to be successful in this role.

What You’ll Do:

• Build Your Own Pipeline: Prospect, reach out to new leads, and grow your book of business through cold outreach, networking, and community involvement.
• Help People Protect What Matters Most: Learn to understand client needs and offer the right insurance solutions.
• Grow Your Presence: Get involved locally, attend events, and build strong relationships that turn into long‑term clients.

What You Bring:

You don’t need years of sales experience—this job is built for people with the drive to succeed. We’re looking for candidates who are:

• Go‑Getters: You enjoy meeting new people and aren’t afraid to start conversations.
• Motivated by Earnings: You want to be in control of your paycheque and love the idea of uncapped commission.
• Coachable & Eager to Learn: You’re open to feedback and excited to develop new skills.
• Professional Communicators: You’re reliable, friendly, and trustworthy.
• Licensed or Willing to Become Licensed: We’ll help you get there.

Skills:

• Prospecting & Hunting: Demonstrated ability to build a book of business from the ground up through cold outreach, lead generation, and strategic follow‑up.
• Relationship Building: Ability to build trust quickly, understand client needs, and maintain long-term, value-driven relationships.
• Business Development Mindset: Entrepreneurial drive with the discipline to manage your pipeline, track activity, and continually seek new revenue.
• Communication Skills: Clear, persuasive, and professional communicator across phone, email, and in-person interactions.
• Organization & Time Management: Ability to efficiently manage prospects, follow-ups, and client meetings in a fast-paced, target-driven environment.
• Resilience & Tenacity: Comfortable working through rejection, staying motivated, and pushing for consistent results.
• Adaptability & Learning Agility: Willingness to learn insurance products, master sales tools, and adapt to evolving market needs.

Lead Generation, Lead Prospecting, Networking, Sales

jobs.title: Senior Medical Science Liaison - Rare Disease-GPA/MPA & Sjögren’s Disease - North Texas
jobs.description:
Career Category

Medical Affairs

Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer.  As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Senior Medical Science Liaison - Rare Disease-GPA/MPA & Sjögren’s Disease - North Texas

The territory will include North Texas (Dallas).

What you will do:

The Sr. Medical Science Liaison (MSL) acts as the primary scientific/clinical resource to Opinion Leaders (OLs), Population Heath Decision Makers (PHDMs) and other health care providers and is responsible for executing Amgen Medical function and product strategy as led by MSL Leadership, with the goal of giving accurate information to OLs, community healthcare providers and PHDMS to improve patient outcomes. The GPA/MPA & Sjögren’s Disease Sr. MSL, is a field-based position within the U.S. Medical team reporting to the GPA/MPA & Sjögren’s Disease Disease West Region MSL Field Director.

Accountabilities and Responsibilities for the Sr. MSL include:

Strategic Execution:

• Majority of time spent on peer-to-peer activities with Rare Disease Opinion Leaders, community healthcare providers, and PHDMs to discuss and advance the scientific platform as aligned with Amgen’s corporate goals and objectives.

• Engage with PHDMs within assigned IDNs and other institutions to communicate scientific based data of clinical value, outcomes, and economic data.

• Connect external and internal stakeholders to amplify Amgen’s reach and access for patients.

• Conduct in-depth scientific exchange to provide focused and balanced clinical and scientific information consistent with MSL compliance standards.

• Support Amgen sponsored research and may serve as a study lead.

• Liaise with potential investigators in non-sponsored clinical research.

• Provide and/or present field observations and insights to internal stakeholders to inform Amgen strategies.

• Lead and support congress activities as aligned with strategy.

• Support speaker training as requested and ensure the speakers are updated on new data.

• Lead and/or participate on project teams that support MSL strategies and tactics as delegated by MSL leadership.

Cross Functional Collaboration:

• Compliantly partner across all Amgen field roles who share customers to create an appropriately coordinated One Amgen experience.

Core Competencies:

• MSLs instill passion and move HCPs to take action in improving patient care related to closing care gaps

• Mentor other MSLs as designated by MSL leadership.

• Execute all administrative responsibilities and training (e.g., Veeva CRM, expense reports, compliance modules, etc.) in a timely manner.

• Maintain and improve clinical/scientific acumen and expertise with current data/information and healthcare trends.

• Ability to build and maintain strong relationships with external stakeholders, and possess excellent communication skills to effectively communicate scientific data.

Basic Qualifications:

• Doctorate degree & 2 years of Medical Affairs experience

OR

• Master’s degree & 6 years of Medical Affairs experience

OR

• Bachelor’s degree & 8 years of Medical Affairs experience

Preferred Qualifications:

• Pharm.D., Ph.D., M.D. or D.O. (other doctoral degrees considered)

• Seven or more years in a medically related field, including 1 year focused on clinical practice, clinical research, or medical research. Experience in a medically related field can include post-doctoral training (i.e., residencies and/or fellowships)

• 2 + years in a medical science liaison role in a biotech or pharmaceutical company Current experience in Scientific Affairs or Medical Affairs at a biotech or pharmaceutical company

•Rheumatology, GPA/MPA and/or Sjögren’s Disease expertise

• Experience with designated territory

What you can expect from us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.

In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include:

• A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts
• A discretionary annual bonus program, or for field sales representatives, a sales-based incentive plan
• Stock-based long-term incentives
• Award-winning time-off plans
• Flexible work models where possible. Refer to the Work Location Type in the job posting to see if this applies.

Apply now and make a lasting impact with the Amgen team.

careers.amgen.com

In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

Application deadline

Amgen does not have an application deadline for this position; we will continue accepting applications until we receive a sufficient number or select a candidate for the position.

Sponsorship

Sponsorship for this role is not guaranteed.

As an organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for people around the world, Amgen fosters an inclusive environment of ethical, committed and highly accomplished people who respect each other and live the Amgen values to continue advancing science to serve patients. Together, we compete in the fight against serious disease.

Amgen is an Equal Opportunity employer. We make all employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

We provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities, consistent with legal requirements. Please contact us to request accommodation.

Job Title: Global Study Manager – TSH

Location: Woolloongabba, AUS

Job Type: Permanent, Full Time

About the Job:

• The Global Study Manager is a key role within the Clinical Team, responsible for the operational delivery of all studies within a specific project of the Translational Science Hub (TSH). The role is accountable for delivering studies on time, within budget and to the required quality standards. Working closely with the Head of Clinical Operations, the Global Study Manager creates synergies across studies and proposes innovative approaches to study operationalization.

Key Responsibilities:

• Study design input: Work with the Clinical Team to ensure operational considerations are built into an efficient study design.
• Cross-functional coordination: Coordinate the Clinical Team with representatives from Global Clinical Department platforms, GCI, GPV, RA, Clinical Supply Chain and other relevant departments on all operational aspects of the study.
• Feasibility and risk management: Ensure study feasibility assessments are completed with input from other functions (RA timelines, country selection, recruitment potential, budget needs). Integrate the findings into the study plan and risk log and follow up on risks to keep all Clinical Team members and functions aligned.
• Planning and budget assumptions: Develop and maintain optimized study plans with other functions. Provide assumptions on the number of sites and enrollment rates for budget and planning purposes across all studies in the program.
• Vendor and CRO management: Work with CROs on the operational delivery of studies.
• Network and partnership development: Develop clinical trial networks and vendor partnerships for the program through the TSH.

Interactions

• Internal: Members of the Clinical Team, including the Global Clinical Development Strategic Expert and the Global Biostatistician. The role works closely with the Head of Clinical Operations to build the TSH's clinical trial capacity.
• External: Clinical Research Organizations, external partners, sites and investigators.

Requirements

Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in a relevant scientific field, or equivalent qualification
• Formal training in GCP

Experience

• 6+ years of experience in clinical research, preferably in vaccines
• Clinical trial experience (required), including experience in vaccine trials
• Proven track record of delivering high-quality, GCP-compliant clinical trials
• Project management and budget management experience

Desirable

• Experience working with CROs on full-service clinical trials
• Advanced team-working and negotiation skills
• Experience working in a global environment with multicultural teams

Better is out there. Better medications, better outcomes, better science. But progress doesn’t happen without people – people from different backgrounds, in different locations, doing different roles, all united by one thing: a desire to make miracles happen. So, let’s be those people.

• Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
